source.weave: The Weave's Mephistopheles is a demon lord who holds Anjelica's mother and 'washes her sins away' through torture-brainwashing — keeping the Faustian soul-broker's essence (the demon who claims and corrupts souls by twisted bargain) as a torturer of the damned.

title: Mammon
teaser: A gluttonous demon lord, mayor of G'ru'l.
body: A massive, perpetually sleeping demon lord, mayor of the Hell town G'ru'l (his rivals tend to die or drop out). Greedy and broke from squandered payouts. He ends up holding four of the five god-killing weapons for the conspiracy.

title: Ragnarok
teaser: Not an apocalypse — the end of the universe.
body: The demon lords' true goal: far beyond an Earth Apocalypse. Using the five god-killing weapons to summon the Four Horsemen, break the four seals, and free the bound Titan Surt — who would reclaim his weapon (the Sword of Damocles), lay siege to Heaven, and destroy the gods and the universe in fire.

source.real: Ragnarök is the Norse 'doom of the gods' — a foretold final battle in which Odin, Thor, Freyr, Loki, and the giants fall; the sun darkens, the stars vanish, and the earth sinks into the sea, before a cleansed world rises renewed. It is the most complete eschatology in Norse myth: the gods themselves are mortal, and their end is written from the beginning.
source.weave: The Weave borrows the name and the shape — the demon lords' true goal, far beyond a mere Earth apocalypse: free the bound end-bringer and destroy gods and universe in fire. The myth's 'even the gods die' becomes the Weave's highest-stakes endgame.
source.excerpt_ref: Völuspá, the fall of the gods

crosslinks.summary: The Weave's apocalypse FUSES Norse Ragnarök with Christian Revelation — Surt's fire and the Four Horsemen's seals are one end-times engine.

interactions.note: Surt's fire (Norse) is the literal end — freeing him is the goal.
The four seals (Revelation) must break to loose the Horsemen — Christian mechanism welded to Norse doom.
The Horsemen (Revelation) are summoned to free Surt (Norse) — the two apocalypses made one.
The five god-killing weapons (Greek + Revelation) are the tools of the ritual.

title: Surt
teaser: A Titan bound in the core of the world.
body: One of the most powerful Titans the gods battled across the universe eons ago, bound into the core of Earth. Should he escape, he would destroy the gods and bring fire and brimstone upon all creation. His own weapon is the Sword of Damocles, kept in Heaven. Freeing him is the aim of Ragnarok.

source.real: Surtr is the fire-giant of Norse myth who guards Muspelheim, the realm of flame, wielding a sword brighter than the sun. At Ragnarök he leads the fire-giants against the gods, kills the god Freyr, and engulfs the world in fire, burning the cosmos so a new world can rise from the sea. He is the appointed end-bringer, fire as cosmic reset.
source.weave: The Weave makes Surt the most powerful bound Titan, whose freeing IS its version of Ragnarök — fire and brimstone upon all creation. It fuses the Norse fire-giant with the Greek Titan-imprisonment motif: an end-bringer the gods could only bind, never kill.
source.excerpt_ref: Völuspá, the coming of Surtr at Ragnarök

title: The Titans
teaser: The cosmic enemies the gods once fought.
body: Ancient, immensely powerful beings the gods did battle with across the universe long ago. The most powerful, like Surt, were bound away rather than destroyed. Their return would threaten gods and universe alike.

source.real: The Titans are the elder gods of Greek myth — Cronus, Rhea, and their kin — overthrown by Zeus and the Olympians in the Titanomachy and imprisoned in Tartarus. Primal, immense powers predating the current divine order, bound rather than destroyed.
source.weave: The Weave's Titans are 'ancient, immensely powerful beings the gods battled across the universe long ago,' the mightiest (like Surt) bound away rather than destroyed — keeping the Greek Titans' essence (elder powers defeated and imprisoned, ever threatening to return) and fusing the Norse fire-giant Surt into their ranks.

crosslinks.summary: The Weave FUSES the Greek Titans with the Norse fire-giant Surt — the elder powers of two traditions become one class of bound primordial enemies.

interactions.note: Surt, the Norse fire-giant of Ragnarök, is folded into the Greek Titans — the mightiest Titan, bound rather than destroyed.
Zeus overthrew the Titans (Greek), the same order-imposing act that later split him from Odin.
The Titans' return = Ragnarök: freeing the bound Titan Surt is the Norse end-times in Greek-Titan dress.

title: The Four Horsemen
teaser: Famine, War, Pestilence, Death — riding in harmony.
body: The four siblings of prophecy, banished to another universe, who can only be recalled by breaking the four seals with enormous power. They can sense the key to Surt's prison and travel between worlds. Each rides a colored horse and carries a weapon. At Conquest's climax Kimberly takes up the mantle of Death herself.

source.real: The Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse ride forth in Revelation 6 as the first four seals are opened — commonly read as Conquest (white horse), War (red), Famine (black), and Death (pale). They are the heralds of the end-times, each loosed to bring a portion of the world's undoing.
source.weave: The Weave's Four Horsemen are 'four siblings of prophecy, banished to another universe, recalled by breaking the four seals' — keeping Revelation's exact mechanism (seals opened to loose the riders) and their identities (Death, War, Conquest, and Misery/Famine), tied to freeing the Titan Surt.
source.excerpt_ref: the opening of the first four seals

crosslinks.summary: The Weave's five god-killing weapons map onto Revelation's Four Horsemen — each rider's arm becomes one of the apocalyptic weapons, with the Dagger/Scythe as Death's.

interactions.note: Conquest (white horse) → the Lance of Conquest.
War (red horse) → the Hammer of War.
Famine/Misery (black horse) → the Bow of Misery.
Death (pale horse) → the Dagger reforged as Death's Scythe.

title: The Four Seals
teaser: What keeps the Horsemen out of this world.
body: Four seals placed in Hell that bar the Four Horsemen, who were banished to another universe. Breaking them requires incredible power — which the conspirators gather by harvesting the magical souls of monsters.

source.real: In Revelation, the Lamb opens a scroll sealed with seven seals; the breaking of the first four looses the Four Horsemen. The seals are the locks on the apocalypse — each one broken brings the end nearer.
source.weave: The Weave's Four Seals 'bar the Four Horsemen,' and breaking them requires immense harvested power — keeping Revelation's seals-as-apocalyptic-locks exactly: undo them and the riders (and the end) are loosed.

title: Mathias's Prophecy
teaser: The soothsayer who was never wrong.
body: A passage in the 13th-century text 'On the Topic of Apocalyptic Scenarios' by the soothsayer Mathias, foretelling the ritual that rips a hole in life — fae blood spilled and salted worldwide, demon blood bound in a pentagram, pixie blood spilled in Hell — so the dead walk again, aided by 'four siblings riding in harmony' and 'the titan who will retake its place among the stars.' Kimberly has used it to stop several Apocalypses.

title: The Sword of Damocles
teaser: Surt's weapon, kept in Heaven.
body: One of the five weapons that can kill a god — and originally the Titan Surt's own weapon. Held in Heaven for safekeeping. If Surt reclaims it he can lay siege to Heaven. Kimberly wields it in the final battle against the Horsemen.

source.real: The Sword of Damocles is the famous moral legend (told by Cicero) of the courtier Damocles, who envied the tyrant Dionysius's power — until Dionysius seated him at the feast beneath a sword hung by a single horsehair. It is the eternal image of power held under constant, precarious threat: privilege and peril inseparable.
source.weave: The Weave's Sword of Damocles is one of the five god-killing weapons, originally the Titan Surt's own blade, held in Heaven — if Surt reclaims it he can lay siege to Heaven. It keeps the legend's essence (a hanging threat over the seat of power): the sword that, returned to its owner, dooms Heaven itself.

title: The Bow of Misery
teaser: A god-killing bow stolen from the armory.
body: One of the five weapons that can kill the Devil, stolen from Katrina's armory by the wraith to be used in the Ragnarok ritual; used in the assassination attempt that nearly killed Katrina.

source.real: The third Horseman of Revelation rides a black horse carrying a pair of balances, heralding famine and scarcity — 'misery' in the sense of want and deprivation. (The first rider on the white horse carries a bow.)
source.weave: The Weave's Bow of Misery is one of the five god-killing weapons, bound to a Horseman — keeping the Revelation rider's weapon-iconography (the bow of the first horseman, the misery/famine of the third) as one of the apocalyptic arsenal.

title: The Lance of Conquest
teaser: A god-killing lance, guarded on Mars.
body: One of the five god-killing weapons, kept under heavy guard in the weapon-vault beneath Olympus Mons on Mars — and stolen by the wraith via summoning magic, despite Akta's pursuit.

source.real: The first Horseman of Revelation rides a white horse, crowned, 'conquering and to conquer' — the rider of Conquest, the opening agent of the apocalypse.
source.weave: The Weave's Lance of Conquest is the god-killing weapon of the Conquest Horseman, vaulted beneath Olympus Mons on Mars — the Revelation conqueror-rider's arm made one of the five weapons that can end a god.

title: Pastor Bill (the Wraith)
teaser: A soul-harvesting ghost behind the True Path.
body: A blue wraith — a ghost wielding magic through smashed soul-orbs — revealed as Pastor Bill, leader of the True Path church. He steals and harvests souls (and ultimately a whole congregation's worth) to gather the power needed to break the four seals and summon the Horsemen. Works with another wraith, Shirley, in service of the larger conspiracy.

title: The True Path Cathedral
teaser: A reactionary demon religion that worships old Hell.
body: A fast-growing church in Dis (its symbol an upside-down horned cross in a yellow circle) preaching that Hell should be ruled by a god or fallen angel, not a human, and that modernization betrays Hell's sacred purpose of 'saving' humanity. A mass movement strong enough to rival Katrina's army; secretly a front for the Ragnarok plot under Pastor Bill.

title: Lilith
teaser: The mother of demons, den-mother of Earth.
body: The oldest demon on Earth, called the mother of demons, who keeps track of every demon operating in her territory. She acts as Kimberly's wary informant — rivals, she says, not quite enemies. Around a hundred angels and a hundred demons work Earth at any time, tipping the scales of mortal souls.

title: Thriaska
teaser: A pixie-killing demon outside the Devil's protection.
body: A demon who broke the Devil's one law — no murdering humans or monsters — by slaughtering pixies across the continent, grinding their bones into signature sigils. Hunted and banished by Kimberly. He also cryptically warned of an impending Apocalypse, setting Kimberly on the trail of the prophecy.

title: Demons on Earth
teaser: The rules demons live by among the living.
body: At any time roughly a hundred demons (and a hundred angels) operate on Earth, mostly tipping mortal souls toward depravity — a delight for them. They live by the Devil's code: no murdering humans or monsters (though they may tempt them to self-destruction). Break it and the Devil disowns you, making you fair game for hunters like Kimberly.

title: Sven
teaser: Akta's gentle troll friend, who chose a side.
body: The kind blue troll who befriended Akta on Earth three thousand years ago, now named Sven and living in Dis. Lonely and easily led, he is drawn into Asmodeus's fold by the promise of family and belonging — and betrays Akta and Julia to the conspiracy, a wound that cuts Akta deeply.

title: Mars (Hell's Annex)
teaser: A red planet hollowed for Hell's overflow.
body: The first planet Katrina annexed for Hell's expansion, its core hollowed into pits by deal with Queen Nebet of the long-lived, subterranean Martians. Olympus Mons — far taller than Earth's old Mount Olympus — houses the Martian government and a vault for one of the god-killing weapons. Ikura serves as the queen's envoy to Akta.

title: Queen Nebet of Mars
teaser: Ruler of the Martians who leased Hell their core.
body: Queen of the blue-skinned, long-lived Martians who live inside their planet. She made the deal letting Katrina build a Hell-annex in the Martian core for handsome payment. Proud and easily offended; her envoy Ikura manages relations with Akta.

title: Michael the Archangel
teaser: Heaven's smug, battle-loving emissary.
body: The archangel who handles Heaven's dealings with Hell, contemptuous of Katrina's reforms but a lover of a good fight. He guards the Sword of Damocles, processes souls at Heaven's gate, and ultimately leads Heaven's host into alliance with Katrina against the Horsemen — coming away grudgingly impressed by her work.

source.real: Michael is the archangel who leads Heaven's armies — 'one of the chief princes' in Daniel, and in Revelation the angel who wars against the dragon and casts him down. He is the warrior-defender of the heavenly order, traditionally the counterweight to the fallen Lucifer.
source.weave: The Weave keeps Michael as Heaven's enforcer-archangel, the martial face of the order Lucifer rebels against — the myth's war-in-heaven preserved as institutional muscle.

title: The Queue of Heaven
teaser: Eternity spent waiting to be judged.
body: At Heaven's golden gate an old man judges souls from a ledger; those tipping Hellward drop through the floor. Many choose instead to stand in an endless line that stretches to the horizon — never judged, never damned — shuffling forward for centuries only to be sent to the back again. Better than Hell, Michael notes, and the odds of getting in are astronomical anyway.

title: The Muse (Aphrodite)
teaser: A goddess who animates the art she inspired.
body: A patron muse — tied to Aphrodite — who inspired Renaissance masterworks and animated the Uffizi's statues to protect them during the Apocalypse. The artworks call her their lady and patron. Kimberly seeks her through the living statues while tracking the key.

title: Aziolith (Conquest era)
teaser: The vain dragon, ally once more.
body: Aziolith returns to aid Akta and Kimberly, shrinking to a dapper lizard-man form (via potion) to move through modern Dis and resuming dragon form for battle. Still nursing a 3,000-year grudge over the Dagger of Obsolescence Lucifer never returned to him, he nonetheless rallies the ancient dragons of Hell to the final fight.

title: Death's Kiss (1989)
teaser: A prequel: Kimberly the college student, before she was Death.
body: The first of Darkness's three internal books, set in 1989 — five years after Julia's sacrifice and long before the Ragnarok war. College-age Kimberly studies under occult scholar Dr. Dankworth while obsessively hunting a way to free Julia's soul from Hell. Aziolith (revived by Julia's blood) is her companion. The arc ends with the near-summoning of the god of Death.

title: Dr. Reginald Dankworth
teaser: The world's foremost occult scholar — and a grieving widower.
body: Professor at North Larchmont University in Havenbrook, Connecticut, curator of its occult museum, and the foremost occult scholar alive. He takes Kimberly as his star pupil. Secretly desperate to resurrect his dead wife Evelyn, he decodes the cipher to summon Thanatos and betrays Kimberly — attempting the ritual alone, which requires four to contain the god of Death.

title: Molly
teaser: Kimberly's roommate — and secret pixie.
body: Kimberly's college roommate, unaware at first that pixie blood runs in her veins. Taken hostage by Lilith to force Kimberly's hand, she survives and becomes Kimberly's apprentice — learning her wings and the hunt over six months, just as Julia once trained Kimberly. Still needs pixie dust to teleport.

title: Clarice
teaser: A cherub cast out of Heaven.
body: A cherub exiled from Heaven after conceiving a child with the demon Charlie and ending the pregnancy — which God deemed unfit for a chaste cherub. Now she scrapes by selling paid 'miracles,' degrading and hollow without the warmth of the gods' light. Cannot die. Her cherub hair is an ingredient in the Thanatos ritual.

title: Thanatos
teaser: The god of Death, bound and dangerous to summon.
body: The Greek god of Death, imprisoned and summonable only through an ancient ritual from a book hidden in the Cenacle shrine. Lilith warns it takes at least four casters to contain him — summoning him alone risks freeing him to wreak havoc. Dr. Dankworth nearly looses him trying to revive his wife.

source.real: Thanatos is the Greek personification of Death — the gentle, inexorable bringer of a peaceful end, twin brother of Hypnos (Sleep), both sons of Nyx (Night). He is rarely worshipped but often invoked; in myth he is once chained by Sisyphus so that no one can die, and must be freed to restore the natural order.
source.weave: The Weave keeps him the Greek god of Death, imprisoned and summonable only by an ancient ritual requiring multiple casters to contain him — the myth's 'Death that can be bound, with dire consequence' made into a literal ritual hazard.
source.excerpt_ref: lines 758-766 (Sleep and Death, children of Night)

title: The Cenacle (Eden Shrine)
teaser: A holy shrine in Russia guarding a forbidden book.
body: A gleaming cross-shaped shrine hidden in a Russian forest, ringed by angel guards, that holds an ancient book written in a dead tongue mixing Hebrew, Latin, Greek, Chinese, and Russian — the text for summoning Thanatos. Demons burn if they enter, so Lilith sends the pixie-blooded Kimberly to steal it.

source.real: The Garden of Eden is the paradise of Genesis, humanity's first home, sealed after the Fall by a flaming sword. The Cenacle is the 'Upper Room' of Christian tradition, the site of the Last Supper and Pentecost. The Weave fuses the two as a hidden holy place guarding an ancient secret.
source.weave: The Weave's Cenacle/Eden Shrine is a cross-shaped shrine hidden in a Russian forest, angel-guarded, holding an ancient polyglot book — merging Eden's guarded-paradise and the Cenacle's sacred-upper-room into one concealed sanctuary of origins.

title: Pete & Ivan
teaser: A demon couple who run Lilith's errands.
body: Two demons (and a couple) sent by Lilith to help Kimberly break into the Cenacle. They use 'glamour' to appear human, enjoy driving over teleporting, and bicker like an old married pair. Both ultimately die at Kimberly's hand once the alliance frays.

title: Glamour
teaser: How demons pass as human.
body: A demon's ability to mask its true red, horned form and appear as an ordinary human to non-magical eyes. Magic-blooded beings (like pixies) see through it automatically, and a demon can choose to reveal itself to anyone — though maintaining glamour is tiring work.

title: Memory-Teleport
teaser: Riding another's memories to a place you've never been.
body: An advanced, rarely-mastered pixie technique: by rubbing pixie dust on the gums (a powerful stimulant that makes the eyes glow pink) and gripping another being's head, a pixie can pull the image of a place from that person's memory and teleport there — reaching destinations they've never personally seen. Kimberly uses it on the handless Charlie.

title: The Kelpie of Tilago Lake
teaser: A water spirit defending her home.
body: A 200-year-old shape-shifting water spirit (horse-hooved even in human form) who lures and drowns campers trashing her lake. Kimberly and Molly spare her, convincing her to merely terrify the polluters and lie low before the military hunts her down — an early lesson for Molly that monsters aren't always the villains.

source.real: The kelpie is the shape-shifting water-horse of Scottish folklore — a spirit haunting lochs and rivers, usually a beautiful black or grey horse that lures riders onto its back, then plunges into deep water to drown and devour them. Even in human form it keeps a tell (hooves, or weed in its hair); its bridle is the key to mastering it.
source.weave: The Weave's Kelpie of Tilago Lake is exactly the folkloric creature — a shape-shifting water-spirit, 'horse-hooved even in human form,' who lures and drowns those who trash her lake. The genuine Scottish water-horse, down to the giveaway hooves, given a conservationist's grudge.

title: Charlie, Handless
teaser: The imp trickster, now without hands.
body: The recurring imp Charlie reappears in the Death's Kiss era having lost his hands (left as stumps), still scheming — he sends Kimberly a cipher amulet on a wild goose chase and tries to kill her with a tripwire bomb. Kimberly forces him to memory-teleport her despite his missing hands.

title: Death's Return (2018)
teaser: The Apocalypse, lived from the streets of London.
body: Darkness's second internal book, set ~2018: immortal Kimberly (gift of Thanatos) and an aged Molly fight on as Lucifer finally cracks Hell open — 666 rifts worldwide. Molly is lost in the first London chasm; Kimberly builds a refugee pixie community in Aziolith's cave and allies with Lilith and her demon-mate Thomas to seize Hell's throne, ending with the long-awaited reunion with Julia.

title: Kimberly, the Immortal
teaser: Death's gift: she stopped aging, and stopped dying.
body: Thanatos warned Kimberly she'd die within a year unless she accepted his gift; ten months later a bullet to the heart proved her immortal. She no longer ages, heals from any wound in hours, and outlives the mortals she loves — a grief that shadows her bond with Molly. Wields daggers, Desert Eagles, a Hell-forged katana (Albrecht the Deceiver's), and pixie magic.

title: Thomas
teaser: Lilith's demon mate, would-be king of Hell.
body: A demon, Lilith's lover, who seizes Buckingham Palace during the Apocalypse and schemes with her to take Hell's throne and 'rule together.' He sends Kimberly to recover the Dagger of Obsolescence from the imprisoned Charlie as his price for Molly's soul. Later hunted across the post-Apocalyptic world.

title: The 666 Rifts
teaser: How the Apocalypse actually broke open.
body: When Lucifer triggered the Apocalypse, 666 Hell-rifts tore open across the Earth at once — chasms swallowing cities (the Thames drained into one; Big Ben and Westminster fell in) as thousands of demons, zombies, ghouls, and monsters climbed out onto the surface. Nations fell within hours; whichever demon could seize a throne claimed it.

title: Sabine
teaser: A child saved into the cave-community.
body: A little girl Kimberly rescues during the London Apocalypse and brings to Aziolith's cave, where a community of pixie-blooded refugees forms. Her father is never found — raptured or killed.

title: The Cave Community
teaser: A refugee colony in a dragon's hoard.
body: During the Apocalypse, Kimberly turns Aziolith's treasure-cave into a hidden sanctuary for rescued pixie-blooded families (Molly's parents Horace and Lydia, Sabine, others). She trains them in their powers; secrecy is enforced on pain of death. Everyone is a billionaire many times over, for whatever that's worth at the end of the world.

title: Death's Bargain
teaser: Kimberly, newly a god, fights to stay alive.
body: Darkness's third internal book: having killed Thanatos with his own Dagger to stop Ragnarok, Kimberly becomes the god of Death — drowning in the voices of the dying. The god Momus holds her Dagger and demands she separate from Thanatos within a week or die. Her search takes her through the Godschurch and into the rival Odin pantheon, ending with Nyx reforging the Dagger into Death's scythe.

title: Kimberly, the God of Death
teaser: A pixie who took up a Horseman's mantle.
body: By killing Thanatos with the Dagger of Obsolescence during Ragnarok, Kimberly absorbed the god of Death's essence and became Death — one of the Four Horsemen. Humanity isn't built for godhood: the screams of every dying soul flood her mind, and she self-medicates to cope. Hypnos confirms Thanatos is now fused with her like hydrogen in water. Her weapon becomes a black scythe.

crosslinks.summary: Kimberly as God of Death wields the reforged Dagger (Death's Scythe) — she carries the Reaper's weapon; see the Scythe/Dagger.

interactions.note: Kimberly as God of Death wields the reforged Dagger (Death's Scythe) — she carries the Reaper's weapon; see the Scythe/Dagger.

title: Momus
teaser: Thanatos's brother, who wants Kimberly dead.
body: A god, brother to Thanatos, who holds the Dagger of Obsolescence and threatens to destroy it (and Kimberly) unless she separates herself from his brother to bring him back. He files the proper Godschurch kill-authorization. In the end his own mother Nyx reabsorbs him.

title: The Godschurch
teaser: The cosmic bureaucracy that oversees the pantheons.
body: An ancient institution that protects and administers the pantheons of the universe, quadrant by quadrant — with masters (Headmaster Fizzle, Hilmos, Gilbarge), directors (Verford), analysts, and strict procedures, including kill-authorization paperwork required before one god may slay another. Earth sits in a neglected backwater quadrant. Mags and Char serve it; it is the institution the Godsverse RPG's agents belong to.

title: The Pantheons
teaser: Many gods, many worlds, old feuds.
body: The universe holds many divine pantheons across many planets, each developing at its own pace. The Zeus (Greek) pantheon and the Odin (Asgard) pantheon split long ago — over Zeus casting out the Four Horsemen after Surt's defeat — and remain enemies. The Godschurch tries to keep order among them all.

crosslinks.summary: THE GREEK–NORSE SCHISM: the founding political rupture of the Weave's cosmos. Zeus (Greek) cast the Four Horsemen out of the universe after the Titan Surt's defeat, fearing their power; Odin (Norse) broke with him over it. The two pantheons — and their two halves of the Underworld — have been estranged ever since.

interactions.note: Zeus's order-imposing fear (the same impulse that drove him to bind the Titans) cast out the Horsemen and split the Greek line from the Norse.
The Horsemen were bound to fight Surt, then exiled by Zeus once Surt was beaten — the exile is the schism's cause.
The schism is mirrored geographically: the Underworld's hot side (Greek/Egyptian/Celtic) and frozen side (Norse Hel) meet at the Great Divide.
Surt — the Norse fire-giant the Horsemen were made to fight — is the hinge: his binding caused the schism, his freeing is Ragnarok.

source.real: Real-world mythologies are many and parallel — Greek, Norse, Egyptian, Hindu, and more — each a self-contained pantheon with its own chief god. Comparative mythology notes both their independence and their echoes (sky-fathers, death-gods, world-trees recurring across cultures).
source.weave: The Weave literalizes comparative mythology: the universe holds many pantheons across many planets, and the Greek (Zeus) and Norse (Odin) lines SPLIT long ago over Zeus casting out the Four Horsemen after Surt's defeat. It turns the scholarly fact of parallel pantheons into in-world political history — the gods are real, plural, and feuding.

title: Odin, the Allfather
teaser: Lord of Asgard, who prizes bravery above all.
body: Head of the Norse pantheon, who fought beside the Greek gods in the war on Surt but broke from Zeus over his casting-out of the Four Horsemen. He values truth, bravery, and loyalty above all. He secretly loosens Kimberly's bond to the Dagger and points her toward Nyx — the connection that links the Death arc to the Godschurch and the Godsverse RPG.

source.real: Odin (the Allfather) is the chief god of the Norse pantheon — god of wisdom, war, poetry, and death. He sacrificed an eye at Mimir's well for wisdom and hung nine nights on the world-tree Yggdrasil to win the runes. He rules Asgard, presides over the slain in Valhalla, and is fated to die at Ragnarök swallowed by the wolf Fenrir. He prizes knowledge and is willing to pay terribly for it.
source.weave: The Weave keeps him as head of the Norse pantheon who prizes truth and loyalty — and gives the wisdom-seeker's instinct a plot role: he secretly loosens Kimberly's bond and points her toward Nyx, the knowing hand behind the scenes exactly as the myth's restless seeker of hidden things.
source.work: Snorri Sturluson, Prose Edda / Poetic Edda

title: Bragi
teaser: A Norse god gone native; the muse's ex.
body: A pudgy, music-loving god of the Odin pantheon, living among a working Viking village, formerly involved with the muse Mags. Honest to a fault (which is why Odin tolerates him), he helps Kimberly gain audience with Odin.

source.real: Bragi is the Norse god of poetry, eloquence, and music — a wise bard among the Aesir, husband of Idunn (keeper of the gods' apples of youth), who welcomes the honored dead to Valhalla with verse. Skaldic poetry itself was sometimes called by his name.
source.weave: The Weave's Bragi is 'a pudgy, music-loving god of the Odin pantheon... honest to a fault,' living among a working Viking village — keeping the god of poetry's gentleness and his association with song and truth.

title: Nyx
teaser: Primordial goddess of night, mother of dark gods.
body: An ancient, near-formless goddess of the night — mother of Thanatos, Hypnos, and Momus — who dwells in the void between worlds, visible only as two glowing purple eyes. To save Kimberly she reabsorbs Momus, then reforges the Dagger of Obsolescence into a black scythe, Death's proper weapon, and summons Kimberly to the planet Yrowet, calling it her true home.

source.real: Nyx is the Greek primordial goddess of Night, one of the first beings born from Chaos in Hesiod's Theogony. She is ancient and powerful enough that even Zeus fears to offend her. From her issue many forces — Sleep (Hypnos), Death (Thanatos), the Fates, Doom, and Strife among them. She dwells at the edge of the cosmos and is mother to much of what the daylight gods cannot control.
source.weave: The Weave keeps Nyx as one of Chaos's four primordial pillars — Darkness itself — the night-force from which the other primordial powers and the line of gods descend.

variants.summary: The primordial Night appears under two names in two threads — Nyx in the Godsverse, Nox in the Obsidian Spindle Saga — the same cosmic darkness wearing a different face per universe.

faces.label: Nyx
faces.note: The ancient, near-formless primordial of Night — mother of Thanatos, Hypnos, and Momus — dwelling in the void between worlds, one of Chaos's four pillars. The cosmological Night.

faces.label: Nox
faces.note: The fairy-tale thread's counterpart — a hands-on night-goddess who gives Chelle corporeal form and strains beside Rose to close Surt's rift. Same Night, but an active player in a fairy-tale universe rather than a remote primordial.

title: Death's Scythe
teaser: The Dagger of Obsolescence, reforged.
body: After Odin loosens Kimberly's bond to it, Nyx reshapes the Dagger of Obsolescence into a black-bladed scythe — the proper weapon of the god of Death. Kimberly feels an immediate kinship with it.

source.tradition: European personification of Death (and Revelation's pale rider)
source.real: The scythe is the iconic instrument of Death personified — the Grim Reaper who harvests souls like grain — and the pale horse's rider in Revelation 6 is named Death. The reaper's blade is the West's enduring image of mortality itself.
source.weave: The Weave reshapes the Dagger of Obsolescence into a black-bladed scythe, 'the proper weapon of the god of Death' that Kimberly wields — giving the god of Death the Reaper's classic scythe, the instrument that mythically harvests the dead.

crosslinks.summary: ONE OBJECT, TWO FORMS: Death's Scythe is the reforged Dagger of Obsolescence — the Grim-Reaper form of the same relic that served as Death's dagger among the Horsemen.

interactions.note: The Scythe is literally the Dagger reshaped by Nyx; see the Dagger for its Revelation/Horseman origin.
Wielded by Kimberly as God of Death — she feels immediate kinship with the reaper's proper weapon.

title: Origin of the Horsemen
teaser: Four gods bound to weapons to cage a Titan.
body: To make them strong enough to fight the Titan Surt, four gods had their essences bound to their weapons, becoming the Four Horsemen — Thanatos (Death) bound to the Dagger of Obsolescence among them. After Surt was interred in Earth's core, Zeus, fearing their power, cast the Horsemen out of the universe; they can only return when the four seals are broken. This is why killing Thanatos made Kimberly Death.

source.real: In Revelation the Four Horsemen — Conquest, War, Famine, Death — are loosed by the breaking of the first four of seven seals, each rider an agent of apocalyptic judgment.
source.weave: The Weave's origin binds four gods' essences to their weapons to make them strong enough to fight Surt, becoming the Horsemen (Thanatos/Death bound to the Dagger) — an origin story for the Revelation riders, explaining the seals and the weapons as a war-measure against a Titan.
source.excerpt_ref: the four riders and the seals

title: Yrowet
teaser: Nyx's planet — Kimberly's 'true home.'
body: A planet Nyx names as Kimberly's real home world, summoning her there at the close of the Death arc. The Godschurch knows its location. A thread left open into Chaos.

title: The Zeus Pantheon
teaser: The Greek gods — Earth's distant overseers.
body: The Greek pantheon headed by Zeus, the divine line that Earth's gods (Bacchus, Thanatos, the Horsemen) belong to. Zeus cast the Four Horsemen out of the universe after Surt's defeat, fearing their power — the act that split the Odin pantheon away. Administered, at a distance, through the Godschurch.

source.real: Zeus is king of the Greek gods, who overthrew his father Cronus and the Titans to rule from Olympus. The Greek pantheon — Olympians descended from the Titans — is the line that includes Dionysus (Bacchus), Thanatos, and the personified powers.
source.weave: The Weave's Zeus Pantheon is the Greek divine line Earth's gods belong to; Zeus cast the Four Horsemen out of the universe after Surt's defeat, fearing their power — keeping Zeus as the order-imposing king (as he was over the Titans) and making that very impulse the cause of the Greek-Norse schism.

title: Anubis
teaser: The first ruler of Hell.
body: The god who, with Hades and the other gods, first crafted Hell — and the first link in the chain of tricked Devils, passing the throne to Hades before departing. Because he built the office, its power vastly outstrips whoever later occupies it.

source.real: Anubis is the jackal-headed Egyptian god of mummification and the dead, guardian of the necropolis and guide of souls. He presides over the Weighing of the Heart, where the deceased's heart is balanced against the feather of Ma'at (truth); he is the embalmer of Osiris and the keeper of the threshold between life and death. Among the oldest Egyptian gods, he predates and prepares the underworld others come to rule.
source.weave: The Weave makes Anubis the god who 'first crafted Hell' with the other gods and the first link in the chain of tricked Devils, passing the throne onward — elevating the myth's original keeper-of-the-dead into the literal architect of the underworld others inherit.
source.work: The Egyptian Book of the Dead (Budge tr., 1895)

title: Cercopes
teaser: God of monkeys, overseer of humankind's rise.
body: The god of monkeys who oversaw the evolution of monkeys into humans — and who thwarted Obren's plot to destroy humanity, sentencing the first pixie to mortality and cursing his line to live among humans.

title: Cherubs
teaser: Heaven's servants, born without free will.
body: The servant-class of Heaven, created to serve the gods without the free will granted to pixies like Obren — whom they envied for it. A cherub (like Clarice) can be cast out and stripped of the gods' light; cherub and demon share enough lineage to conceive a child.

title: Chaos (the finale, +10,000 yrs)
teaser: The end of the Godsverse — and its rebirth.
body: The climactic book of the Godsverse, set ~10,000 years after the Death arc. Five POVs (Kimberly, Rebecca, Julia, Katrina, Akta) converge as the primordial gods reconstruct themselves to wake the sleeping goddess Chaos and end the universe. It closes with Katrina becoming the new Chaos, holding the next universe in her dreaming mind.

title: Projekt Kaos
teaser: The plot to wake Chaos and end the universe.
body: An ancient scheme — older than the Godless, traceable to the universe's origin — to reconstruct the four primordials (by killing the gods who carry their fragments) so they can enter the Source and wake Chaos, ending the cosmos. Eros drives it, harvesting love-gods to reconstitute himself, then reassembling Tartarus. Velaska was investigating it and was framed for it.

title: The Source (revealed)
teaser: Not a void — a vast city of all souls.
body: At the universe's heart, the Source is revealed to be an endless luminous metropolis where cleansed souls live among flying cars and towering buildings, bathed in white light. Underworlds across the cosmos cleanse souls and return them here as raw creation-energy; Chaos sleeps somewhere within. Counterbalanced by Nyx's Darkness — yin and yang of creation, not good and evil.

title: Katrina, the God
teaser: Devil, then god, then the universe itself.
body: Ten thousand years on, Katrina is a full god who killed Hera and Zeus and battled Cronus — a reluctant celebrity-diplomat for the Godschurch. Still ruled by instinct and a fierce need to simply be left in peace. At the universe's end, Chaos names her 'my greatest creation' and passes her the role of catalyst: Katrina becomes the new Chaos, dreaming the next universe.

title: Rebecca Lobdell
teaser: Director of a shattered Godschurch.
body: Director of the Godschurch, hardened and weary, holding the organization together after the Battle of the Obelisk killed 90% of its agents and most of its dues-paying gods. Trains new recruits like Julia personally, distrusts Cronus, and chases the soul-drain and Projekt Kaos. Dissolves with the universe at the end.

title: The Godschurch (10,000 yrs on)
teaser: A cosmic agency in decline.
body: The Godschurch now protects gods across 100,000+ planets via a teleporter network (every god-touched world has a Godschurch portal to its underground base near the Source). Once 2,000 dues-paying gods strong, it has dwindled below a hundred and to ~10% staffing after the Battle of the Obelisk. The institution the Godsverse RPG's agents serve.

title: Julia, Godschurch Agent (and Gaia)
teaser: The detective who became a primordial.
body: After 10,000 years as the underworld's investigator, Julia joins the Godschurch as a rookie under Rebecca — a patient investigator among aggressive soldiers. When she kills Gaia, the Earth-primordial's power transfers into her, overwhelming her mortal frame. Compassion is her defining trait, even toward those she must kill.

title: Akta, the Devil's Bodyguard
teaser: 13,000 years on, freed but still fighting.
body: Released from her debt to Hell's throne by Velaska, Akta serves ~10,000 years as Katrina's personal bodyguard and a Godschurch agent — still a hunter at heart who loathes diplomacy and bureaucracy. Mentors Julia. Her instincts (spotting a soul bomb in a veena) repeatedly save lives.

title: The Soul Bomb
teaser: A dead soul packed tight enough to kill a god.
body: A weapon made from the remains of a dead soul compressed until it bursts, vaporizing everything in its path — even a god. First used by Asmodeus during Ragnarok; the plans were thought destroyed, but they resurface millennia later in Godless/Horde hands, used to assassinate gods on the NOX hit-list.

title: The NOX List
teaser: A live hit-list of the gods.
body: A constantly-updating database tracking hundreds of gods and their real-time locations — used by Projekt Kaos to hunt and assassinate the carriers of primordial fragments (love-gods first). Katrina's name is on it.

title: Gaia
teaser: The Earth primordial, in every world.
body: The primordial of Earth, who spread a piece of herself into every planet in the cosmos — life-touched or not. Weary of humanity ('a cancer on my worlds'), she works toward the universe's end. Killed by Julia, who absorbs her power; leaves moss and grass in her every footstep.

source.real: Gaia is the primordial Earth in Greek myth, who emerges just after Chaos and gives rise to Ouranos (Sky), the mountains, and the sea, then bears the Titans with Ouranos. She is the literal ground of being — mother and grandmother of the gods, who repeatedly shapes the succession of divine rulers from Ouranos to Cronus to Zeus.
source.weave: The Weave makes Gaia the Earth-pillar among the Primordials, who 'seeded every planet' — taking Hesiod's mother-of-all and scaling her up from one world to all of them.

title: Eros
teaser: The Love primordial, reborn from Cupid.
body: The primordial of Love, dissolved long ago into the concept itself. He reconstitutes by killing every love-god (Cupid evolving into him), then sets about reassembling Tartarus to wake Chaos. Coldly methodical — 'that's not how this works' — he kills Velaska as 'an unavoidable misstep.'

source.real: In Hesiod's Theogony, Eros is not the winged cherub of later art but a primordial force — 'fairest among the deathless gods, who unnerves the limbs and overcomes the mind.' He is desire as a cosmic principle, present at the very beginning, the attraction that drives creation to combine and multiply.
source.weave: The Weave casts Eros as the Love-pillar among the Primordials who 'dissolved into the concept of love' itself — exactly Hesiod's primal Eros: not a god who causes love but love as a foundational force woven into the cosmos.

title: Tartarus
teaser: The Underworld primordial, beneath every Hell.
body: The primordial of the Underworld, whose essence forms the basis of every underworld ever created. Reassembled by Eros (his heart shrunk to fit his reformed body), he rampages toward the Source seeking Chaos, volatile and blaming Eros when the hunt falters.

source.real: Tartarus is both a primordial being and a place in Greek myth: in Hesiod's Theogony it is one of the first entities to emerge after Chaos, and also the deep abyss below Hades — as far beneath the earth as the sky is above it — where the defeated Titans are imprisoned behind bronze gates. It is the lowest pit of the cosmos, the foundation under every underworld.
source.weave: The Weave makes him the primordial of the Underworld whose essence underlies every underworld ever created — taking Hesiod's double nature (the being and the abyss) and treating the being as the literal source-substance of all lands of the dead.

title: Velaska, Reformed
teaser: The old Devil, now a Godschurch member — and scapegoat.
body: The former Devil (who once cursed Akta) resurfaces millennia later as a vain, scone-loving Godschurch member who tricked her way in. She'd been quietly investigating Projekt Kaos back to the universe's origins — which made her the perfect frame. She dies at Eros's hand, mourned by the friend who hated her, Katrina.

title: Cronus & Rhea
teaser: The Mad Titan, caged beside the Source.
body: The Mad Titan Cronus and his bride Rhea — the universe's greatest threat in a million years, defeated at the Battle of the Obelisk. By Katrina's deal they live near the Source under the Godschurch's guard (and its god-killing weapons). Cronus, unnervingly aware, feeds Katrina the names Indra and Ananke before he and Rhea die — the loss that pushes Rebecca over the edge.

source.real: Cronus is the leader of the Titans, who castrates his father Ouranos to seize power, then swallows his own children to prevent a prophecy that one will overthrow him — until Rhea hides the infant Zeus, who later frees his siblings and casts the Titans down into Tartarus. Cronus rules the 'golden age' but is defined by the cycle of a ruler devouring the future to keep his throne.
source.weave: The Weave invokes Cronus (with Rhea) as part of the old order that 'hoarded the Source's creation-power' before it reopened to all pantheons — the myth's devouring, hoarding father turned into the Weave's account of why creation-power was once monopolized.

title: The Many Pantheons
teaser: Greek, Norse, Hindu, Egyptian — all real, all feuding.
body: The cosmos holds countless pantheons, each named for its chief god — the Zeus (Greek), Odin (Norse), Brahman (Hindu), Osiris (Egyptian) lines and more. Zeus and Cronus once hoarded the Source's creation-power; after the Battle of the Obelisk it reopened to all. Gods are powerful, near-immortal, vain, and self-aware hypocrites who avoid creating too many humans lest they drown in mortal time.

crosslinks.summary: The cosmos holds countless pantheons, each named for its chief god (Zeus/Greek, Odin/Norse, Brahman/Hindu, Osiris/Egyptian). Beneath them sit the Primordials, and beneath those the Old Ones — the 'all myths draw from one Source' thesis as literal cosmic structure.

interactions.note: The founding Greek-Norse schism splits Zeus's and Odin's lines — see the Pantheons for the rupture.
The Primordials sit beneath all the named pantheons.
Beneath even the Primordials, the Lovecraftian Old Ones — the deepest layer of the cosmos.
All pantheons ultimately draw from the Source — the one origin behind every mythology.

source.real: Each major culture's gods form a pantheon named for its chief deity — Zeus (Greek), Odin (Norse), Brahman (Hindu), Osiris (Egyptian). Real comparative mythology studies how these systems differ and overlap.
source.weave: The Weave names its pantheons exactly this way — the Zeus, Odin, Brahman, Osiris lines and more — with Zeus and Cronus's history beneath them. The map of world religion rendered as the Weave's actual cosmic politics.

title: Yama
teaser: A human-born god of an underworld.
body: A human-born god, vain and gold-obsessed, who rules the underground city of Patala — spires and bridges hung in a vast chasm, his guards armored in show-gold. In The Dark Prince he aids Red and the ailing Epiales onward to Kur after their prison break. (Also appears in the Godsverse around the events of Chaos.)

source.real: Yama is the Hindu god of death and lord of the dead — the first mortal to die, who thereby became ruler of the departed and judge of their deeds. He presides over Naraka (the underworld) and the south, weighing each life's karma. Solemn and exacting, he is death as cosmic law rather than malice, the keeper of the ledger of deeds.
source.weave: The Weave makes Yama a 'human-born god' who rules the underground city of Patala — keeping the genuine Hindu detail that Yama was the first human to die and so became the dead's ruler, and the real Hindu netherworld Patala as his domain — while coloring him vain and gold-obsessed.
source.excerpt_ref: the hymns to Yama; Naciketas and Yama

title: Kimberly's Reapers
teaser: Death, scaled across a million Earths.
body: As the god of Death for Earth and a million worlds like it, Kimberly commands thousands of black-robed reapers across the cosmos, handling the souls that cling too tightly to life — making her, by her own account, 'more a bureaucrat than anything.' Muriel is one such reaper.

title: The Absence
teaser: The nothing between universes.
body: Pure nothingness — not darkness, but the absence of everything — where Chaos passes the power of creation to her successor. There the old Chaos dissolves and the new one (Katrina) holds every living essence that will ever exist, to fold out into the next dreamed universe and back again forever.

title: Dolos
teaser: Who led the Godless at the Obelisk.
body: The leader of the Godless at the Battle of the Obelisk — the epic confrontation a decade before Chaos in which the Godless and the Godschurch (allied with the gods) shattered each other. His movement, wielding god-killing Horde tech, survives in scattered cells.

title: Cupid
teaser: A love-god who 'evolved' into Eros.
body: One of the last love-gods under Godschurch protection. When killed, he doesn't merely die — he evolves into the primordial Eros, a key step in Projekt Kaos's reconstruction of the four pillars.

title: Eternity (the origin keystone)
teaser: The crossover that explains the whole Cosmic Weave.
body: The deep-canon book (and Book 13 of the Obsidian Spindle Saga) that unifies the Godsverse, Obsidian Spindle, and Dragon Strife into one universe. Three POVs — Velaska (a Godschurch agent millennia before her time as Devil) and Rose & Chelle (heroes of the Obsidian Spindle Saga). It reveals Velaska's origin as a god, the history of the Horsemen and the god-killing weapons, Pandora's box, and the reincarnation cycle that underpins everything.

title: The Cosmic Weave
teaser: The single tapestry all the stories share.
body: The overarching reality binding nearly all of Russell Nohelty's series into one universe. The Fates weave every soul's life into a vast quilt; the universe is a tapestry that must be fully woven before it can end. Author's framing: almost every story he fully owns is a thread of the Cosmic Weave.

title: The Old Ones
teaser: The dark Primordials who want the universe back.
body: The Lovecraftian aspect of the Primordials — the 'Old Ones,' led by Nyarlathotep and Chernabog — who hold that darkness, struggle, and entropy are the universe's true natural state, and that the gods' imposed order is a perversion. They seek to remake the cosmos in their image (insects and night their chosen). The gods fear them above all.

source.real: In H.P. Lovecraft's 'The Call of Cthulhu' (1928, now public domain), the Great Old Ones are vast, ancient cosmic entities who ruled the Earth before humanity and lie 'not dead but dreaming,' waiting to return when the stars are right. Lovecraft's horror is cosmic indifference: these beings are not evil so much as utterly beyond human morality and scale, and human order is a thin, temporary accident against their immensity. (Note: the later 'Elder Gods vs. Old Ones' good-vs-evil framing was August Derleth's addition, not Lovecraft's, and is NOT public domain.)
source.weave: The Weave names them outright as 'the Lovecraftian aspect of the Primordials' — entities who hold that darkness, struggle, and entropy are the true natural state and the gods' order a perversion. It does exactly what the series thesis promises: folds Lovecraft's cosmic horror UNDER the Weave as the oldest, most indifferent layer beneath every human pantheon.
source.excerpt_ref: the dream of dead R'lyeh; 'not dead but dreaming'

crosslinks.summary: The Weave unifies THREE traditions' primal-darkness powers: Lovecraft's Old Ones, the Greek Primordials, and the Slavic black-god Chernabog — all one entropy-faction beneath the gods.

interactions.note: The Old Ones ARE the Lovecraftian aspect of the Greek Primordials — same primal beings, two traditions' names.
Nyarlathotep (Lovecraft) leads them — the Crawling Chaos as their herald.
Chernabog (Slavic black-god) is enlisted among them — entropy's recruiter across pantheons.
Night-Gaunts (Lovecraft) herald their arrival.

title: Chernabog
teaser: The most-wanted god — and an Old One.
body: A legendary agitator god aligned with the Old Ones, the Godschurch's most wanted for eons (he killed two of Velaska's partners). He courts the darkness, recruits agents to chaos, and manipulates Velaska into retrieving Pandora's box. Believes the universe's true beautiful state is darkness and struggle.

source.real: Chernobog ('black god') is a Slavic deity of darkness and misfortune named in medieval chronicles — a shadowy figure of bad fate, popularized as the demonic mountain-god of Bald Mountain. He embodies the dark, chaotic counter-principle to the bright gods.
source.weave: The Weave's Chernabog is 'a legendary agitator god aligned with the Old Ones,' the Godschurch's most-wanted, who courts darkness and recruits agents to chaos — taking the Slavic black-god of misfortune and enlisting him among the Lovecraftian Old Ones as entropy's recruiter.

title: Nyarlathotep
teaser: An Old One who hunts Rose and Chelle.
body: A powerful Old One whose face the Fates foresaw as the harbinger of the universe's doom. He attacks Rose and Chelle on Earth, destroying their home and driving them back into the realms to fight the incursion of the Old Ones and the Horde.

source.real: Nyarlathotep first appears in Lovecraft's 1920 prose-poem of the same name (public domain) — the 'Crawling Chaos,' a cosmic entity who walks among humans in mortal form, spreading madness and foreboding as civilization unravels. Unlike the dreaming, remote Old Ones, Nyarlathotep is active and present, the messenger and soul of the outer gods who moves openly through the world.
source.weave: The Weave makes him a leader of the Old Ones whose face the Fates foresaw as the harbinger of the universe's doom — keeping Lovecraft's defining trait: the cosmic horror that, unlike the others, comes to YOU, walking the Earth to begin the unmaking.

title: Night-Gaunts
teaser: Anti-magic harbingers, killable only by obsidian.
body: Winged nightmare-creatures made of anti-magic that herald the arrival of the Old Ones. Conventional weapons and god-magic can't touch them — only obsidian weapons can kill them. Their presence means the Old Ones are close to entering the universe; they swarm thickest around what most needs protecting.

source.real: Night-gaunts are Lovecraft's faceless, winged, black creatures — first from his childhood nightmares, then his sonnet 'Night-Gaunts' and The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath. Silent, horned, rubbery flyers that carry off dreamers; they do not speak and have smooth, faceless heads.
source.weave: The Weave's Night-Gaunts are 'winged nightmare-creatures made of anti-magic that herald the Old Ones' — keeping Lovecraft's silent winged horrors and making them immune to god-magic, killable only by obsidian: the heralds whose arrival means the Old Ones are near.
source.work: H. P. Lovecraft, Fungi from Yuggoth / Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath

title: Velaska's Ascension
teaser: How a Godschurch slave became a god.
body: For 8,000 years Velaska served the Godschurch as an agent — effectively a slave, since leaving meant withering to dust and eternal torture, and the gods always refused to make her immortal. She finally became a god by killing the trapped goddess Pandora (absorbing her full power, not a fraction), winning freedom no god could grant — and the universal hatred that came with it.

title: The Agent's Contract
teaser: Why Godschurch agents can never truly leave.
body: Godschurch agents are ageless only while serving; the binding magic frays if they quit, and they wither to nothing — then, being old souls, face eons of torture in the underworld before returning to the Source. Only a god's boon (or becoming a god) grants true immortality, and the gods refuse to set that precedent. The Masters — ancient empowered humans — are the only ones who can override a god.

title: The Masters of the Godschurch
teaser: Ancient humans who can command gods.
body: Three ancient humans endowed with god-tier power who run the Godschurch in the gods' name, spending their days contemplating the cosmos. They are the only beings who can persuade a god to act against its own desires — and thus the only ones who could free an agent from their contract.

title: Rose
teaser: A worn-down human who wakes inside a fairy tale.
body: Once Queen of Oz, blessed by Hypnos and Persephone — by the end perhaps the most powerful human alive. In the finale she discovers the simple cure for the Spore (the blue spores themselves), turns possessed gods back mid-battle, and carries a dying Chelle to safety. She survives: she and Chelle retire to a quiet Montana farm with their dog and Jamil, married and at peace, mourning Red.

title: Chelle
teaser: A half-gorgon who follows her love into another world.
body: Rose's half-gorgon love and a part-time Fate. Tortured nearly to a husk by Odin, she fights on through the final battle against the Spore, killing gods with Red's golden dagger. She lives — retiring with Rose to a Montana farm, the most powerful being in Urgu, finally able to simply exist alongside the woman she loves.

title: Pandora & the Box
teaser: A goddess sealed in an obsidian box of forbidden knowledge.
body: A goddess trapped inside an obsidian box on a derelict Mount Olympus, guarding knowledge that could end the resurrection cycle. The box and its key are forged of the same rare obsidian used to make the universe — the one material that survives between cycles. Pandora has Velaska kill her so the evil within can be re-sealed and Velaska can become a god.

source.real: Pandora is the first woman in Greek myth, fashioned by the gods as a punishment for humankind after Prometheus steals fire. Given a sealed jar (later 'box') she is forbidden to open, she opens it anyway, releasing every evil into the world — leaving only Hope trapped inside. She is the mythic origin of human suffering, and of hope as its strange companion.
source.weave: The Weave keeps Pandora and her box as the vessel that loosed the world's evils — using the myth's most famous object as a literal artifact in the cosmology.

title: The God-Killing Weapons (forged)
teaser: Five obsidian arms made to fight Surt.
body: The weapons that can kill a god — including the Dagger of Obsolescence, Bow of Misery, Lance of Conquest, and Sword of Damocles — are forged of obsidian (by Yilir) and bound to the Four Horsemen to fight Surt. After the battle they pass through Velaska to Zeus, then come to rest in Earth's underworld, where they recur throughout Hell's history.

source.real: The same apocalyptic arsenal — the Horsemen's weapons plus the Sword of Damocles — here described as forged of obsidian and bound to the Four Horsemen of Revelation.
source.weave: The God-Killing Weapons are forged of the first obsidian by Yilir and bound to the Four Horsemen to make them strong enough to fight Surt — the Weave's origin for the Revelation arsenal as obsidian relics.

title: The Obsidian Spindles
teaser: Obsidian gateways between realms.
body: Spindles of the first obsidian that serve as portals between worlds and realms (Dream, Nightmare, Fairy, Celestial, Earth). Built with the Old Ones' own magic, they repel that magic — making them among the few things that can slow an incursion. Central to the Obsidian Spindle Saga; Rose and Chelle were gifted one.

source.tradition: European fairy tale (Sleeping Beauty) + Greek (the Fates)
source.real: The spindle is the cursed instrument of 'Sleeping Beauty' (Perrault/Grimm), on which the princess pricks her finger to fall into enchanted sleep; the spindle is also the tool of the Greek Moirai (Fates), who spin the thread of every life. Two of myth's most potent spindles — the sleep-curse and the thread of destiny.
source.weave: The Weave's Obsidian Spindles are portals between worlds where the gorgon-Fates weave the Quilt of Life — fusing the Fates' spinning of destiny with the Sleeping-Beauty spindle (the whole 'Obsidian Spindle Saga' is a fairy-tale thread). The instrument of both fated sleep and fated life, made the axis of the worlds.
source.excerpt_ref: the cursed spindle; the loom of the Fates

title: The Realms
teaser: Dream, Nightmare, Fairy, Celestial, Underworld.
body: The interconnected realms of the Obsidian Spindle side of the Weave: the Dream Realm (Oz, ruled by Queen Aine, home of the Fates), the Nightmare Realm, the Fairy Realm, the Celestial Realm (the gods' old home), and the Underworld. Linked by Obsidian Spindles and now under assault by the Old Ones and the Horde.

title: Queen Aine
teaser: Ruler of Oz who betrays Chelle.
body: Queen of the Land of Oz in the Dream Realm, who owes Rose a favor — but, under pressure of the invasion, betrays Chelle, having her arrested for 'treason' to use as a bargaining chip. A pragmatic ruler willing to sacrifice an ally to save her realm.

title: Nox
teaser: The imprisoned darkness-goddess, once teacher to the child who became the Sovereign.
body: The goddess of night (the Obsidian Spindle Saga's counterpart to Nyx) who gave Chelle corporeal form. In the finale she and Rose strain to close the rift Surt tears open; pierced by Surt's flaming sword, she dies passing Rose the obsidian weapons and the obligation to end the universe and dream a new one. In the Obsidian Spindle Saga, Nox grants eternal life at a price — binding Mydnyte to guard a door into the Dream Realm.

source.real: Nox is the Roman name for Nyx, the primordial goddess of Night — one of the first beings, mother of Sleep, Death, and the Fates, a power so ancient even the king of gods steps carefully around her. Roman writers (Ovid, Virgil) invoke her as Nox; she and Nyx are the same primordial Night under two languages.
source.weave: The Weave explicitly makes Nox 'the Obsidian Spindle Saga's counterpart to Nyx' — the night-goddess who gives Chelle corporeal form. This is the Weave's own internal echo: the same primordial Night appearing under her Roman name in the fairy-tale thread, distinct from the primordial Nyx of the Godsverse.

title: Yilir & Charon's Bargain
teaser: How the architect won the right to wed the ferryman.
body: Yilir, chief architect of the underworld (she designs every Mount Olympus's 153 buildings) and forger of the obsidian weapons, agrees to help fight Surt only if the gods end her paramour's betrothal so she may marry Charon. Velaska brokers it with Zeus — the deep-past root of the Yilir/Charon romance seen bound to the Mirror of Yilir in Ruin.

title: Velaska Made Guardian of Hell
teaser: Why the old Devil ended up running Hell.
body: After the battle, Zeus tricks Velaska — bound by her vow never to fight him — into guarding the god-killing weapons on the planet destined to become Earth, taking over from Anubis and then Hades. This is the deep-past origin of how Velaska came to hold Hell, and the seed of the chain of tricked Devils (Anubis→Hades→Velaska→Lucifer→Katrina).

title: Surt, the World-Eater (first binding)
teaser: The Titan first bound to the seal — by the Horsemen.
body: In the deep past, the great beast Surt — large enough to swallow worlds — is beaten and bound in Earth's underworld. The Four Horsemen are fixed to a blue seal ringed by four red seals and can only free him acting in concert. Prophecy: when Surt returns, every god dies fighting it, and peace comes only in the last god's blood. This is the binding the Ragnarok plot later tries to undo.

source.real: Surtr, the Norse fire-giant of Muspelheim, who at Ragnarök engulfs the world in flame. His sword brighter than the sun ends the old world so a new one may rise.
source.weave: The Weave's deep-past binding: Surt, 'large enough to swallow worlds,' is beaten and bound in Earth's underworld, the Four Horsemen fixed to a seal over him. The fire-giant's world-ending role becomes a chained doom waiting beneath the planet — the first-binding face of the figure whose freeing is Ragnarok.

title: The Horde
teaser: Insectoid servants of the Old Ones with god-killing tech.
body: The swarming, insectoid forces of the Old Ones — their 'chosen beings' — who infest worlds and wield technology capable of killing gods. They invade the realms alongside the night-gaunts, and their salvaged tech later fuels the Godless cells that shatter the Godschurch. To the Old Ones, the Horde are the universe's rightful inheritors and humanity the pest.

title: Change (1980s, the prequel)
teaser: A Cold-War caper that opens the Godsverse.
body: Chronologically the first book of the series — a self-contained 1980s spy story with almost no on-page cosmology. The changeling Sadie is hired by the fixer Ollie to track a magical dagger from a Soviet weapons program across Berlin, Moscow, and Egypt, only for it to surface back in Los Angeles. It sets up Magic, where Ollie recovers the dagger and is betrayed by the demons who hired her.

title: Sadie
teaser: A changeling retrieval agent who just wants out.
body: The narrator of The Change — a changeling (shapeshifter) mercenary working out of 1980s Los Angeles, able to take any form and never constrained by weight. Tough, wry, and devoted to her girlfriend Leigh, she takes a too-lucrative job from her fixer Ollie to hunt down a dagger, a search that drags her across Cold War Europe and the USSR and back home again.

title: Leigh
teaser: Sadie's girlfriend and the life she wants to keep.
body: Sadie's girlfriend, the grounding 'only good thing' in her life, who joins the final leg of the dagger job. Their quiet domesticity (and the dream of retiring on one big payday) is the heart Sadie is fighting to get back to.

title: Ollie
teaser: A hard-nosed fixer who can open portals.
body: Sadie's demanding fixer-client, who pays too well to refuse and can open portals — but only when physically present with you. All business, cheap with expenses, and relentless about retrieving the dagger before a hard deadline.

title: The Dagger (Sadie's quarry)
teaser: A small magical knife everyone wants.
body: The relic at the center of The Change — the dagger Ollie sends Sadie around the world to find, only for it to turn up in the Los Angeles magical black market. An early appearance of the recurring Godsverse dagger.

source.real: Death's weapon — the dagger/scythe of the pale rider (Revelation) and the Reaper. This is the same relic tracked in an earlier era.
source.weave: 'The Dagger (Sadie's quarry)' is the Dagger of Obsolescence appearing in the Change era — the SAME object as the god-killer that becomes Death's Scythe. One relic across the timeline; see the Dagger's main entry for the full Revelation/Reaper root.

title: Blezor
teaser: An LA art dealer with a warded gallery.
body: A wealthy Los Angeles art-and-weapons dealer in the Hollywood Hills whose glass mansion doubles as a heavily-warded gallery of magical artifacts. He ends up holding the dagger — and is, awkwardly, obsessed with Leigh.

title: Magic / Black Market Heroine
teaser: Ollie's story — the perfect way into the Godsverse.
body: The novelization of the Black Market Heroine graphic novel (and three linked stories), written as the eighth Godsverse book but designed as the entry point to the series. Across three internal parts — Black Market, Blacklisted, and Black Hearted Heroine — the LA arms-fixer Ollie recovers the dagger from Change, is betrayed by the demons who hired her, and unravels a layered conspiracy ending in Hell. Sets up Evil, which follows the demon girl Anjelica.

title: Oleander 'Ollie' White
teaser: Half-angel, half-demon — and hates both.
body: The fixer from Change revealed in full: Oleander White, daughter of an angel mother (who passes as a strict human) and a demon father — which gives her second sight (seeing through any illusion to a being's true nature), a scent for every race, immense strength, and freedom from food and sleep. A black-market arms-and-artifact dealer in Los Angeles who casts magic through Welsh spell-words and a wand, drives her beloved car Lily, and works for no one but the right price. Loathed and feared across the monster underworld.

title: Second Sight & Spellcraft
teaser: Seeing the truth, and shaping it with words.
body: Ollie's second sight pierces any illusion charm to reveal a being's true nature, and her sensitive nose reads each race by smell (demons of charred meat, orcs of moldy cheese, humans of rotting flesh). Magic in this era is cast through Welsh-language command-words focused through a wand or improvised foci; raw, adrenaline-charged casting is more powerful but wildly harder to control.

title: Anjelica
teaser: A demon girl who didn't know she was a demon.
body: A young half-demon kidnapped by Balaam and Moloch and briefly weaponized as an 'antichrist' to trigger an Apocalypse, until Ollie and Kimberly drain the power and save her. Quick-witted, fearless, and endlessly curious, she burrows out of trouble (literally gnawing through a car seat) and becomes the heart Ollie didn't know she needed. The series' next book, Evil, follows her.

title: Ollie's Mother
teaser: An angel who hated the demon in her daughter.
body: Ollie's mother — an angel passing as a vain, status-obsessed human in a gated LA community — who blamed every flaw in her daughter on her demon father's blood and refused to support her dreams. She loves Ollie but will never admit any wrong. Her angelic nature is why Ollie is half-angel.

title: Lily
teaser: Ollie's car — and her most trusted ally.
body: Ollie's 1968 Plymouth Barracuda, named Lily — the one relationship she fully trusts, repaired again and again by Phil. She prefers driving Lily to teleporting because it gives her time to think.

title: Phil
teaser: A cold-blooded alien tech-genius and Ollie's friend.
body: A small, green, cold-blooded alien inventor whose suburban house bristles with sci-fi defenses (force-fields that survived a Gamrillian laser cannon, sub-floor gun emplacements). He speaks in probabilities, fixes Lily, and is one of the only non-toxic relationships in Ollie's life.

title: Kimberly (BMH era)
teaser: A dagger-wielding hunter who helps Ollie.
body: A fierce, teleporting fighter who aids Ollie against the demons and spirits Anjelica away to safety afterward. Wields daggers and pixie-style flash-travel — the same Kimberly whose long arc runs through Hell, Ruin, and the Death books, here crossing Ollie's path.

title: The Market
teaser: LA's monster underworld, hidden in plain sight.
body: The 'black market' Ollie works — a network of monsters (orcs, demons, kitsune, arachne, trolls, gorgons) living disguised among humans as clerks, cops, and dealers, trading magical weapons, charms, and contraband. Safe houses like the Palomino bar let them mingle openly; normals forget what they see.

title: The Palomino
teaser: A neutral-ground bar for LA's monsters.
body: A country-music bar in Los Angeles, run by Billy and Tommy, that serves as safe neutral ground for the monster underworld — normals who wander in forget everything but a good time. Ollie's home turf.

title: Et'atal
teaser: A demon arms-lord who rules from a gold castle in Hell.
body: The ghost-like mastermind behind the plot against Ollie — a refined demon arms-and-contraband lord who never meets clients in person and operates a gaudy gold castle in Hell. A theatrical showman who orchestrated the betrayal for sport and profit; the true target of Ollie's revenge.

title: Balaam & Moloch
teaser: Two thuggish demons who betrayed Ollie.
body: A pair of muscle-bound demons (Balaam, six-eyed; Moloch, tall-horned) who pay Ollie with a duffel of cut phone books instead of money and try to kill her for the dagger. Iced by Ollie, later revived in Hell to serve Et'atal and nurse their grudge.

title: Lucifer (BMH era)
teaser: A weary Devil in a blacked-out castle.
body: Ollie meets Lucifer in his dim, near-empty castle above Hell's lava lake — tired, unbothered, candid that the Devil's throne is 'mostly a ceremonial position filled with bureaucracy,' worn down by endless assassination attempts whenever he tries to improve Hell. He calmly escorts Ollie to destroy the dagger, recognizing it as one of the few god-killing weapons.

source.real: Lucifer/Satan as ruler of Hell — the fallen angel enthroned over the damned in Christian tradition.
source.weave: The Weave's wry inversion: Ollie finds Lucifer tired and unbothered in a near-empty castle, candid that the Devil's throne is 'mostly a ceremonial position.' The dread lord of Hell rendered as a bored middle-manager — the same figure, a different thread's tone.

title: Black Market Heroine (comic)
teaser: The graphic novel Magic novelizes.
body: The Godsverse graphic novel that Magic expands into prose. Ollie's introduction to readers in comic form; the book was written as its companion novelization plus linked stories, and reframed as the ideal entry point to the whole series.

title: Evil (Anjelica's coming-of-age)
teaser: A vulnerable hero, a small town, then a whole new world.
body: Book 2, following Anjelica directly out of Magic. A deliberate slow-burn and tonal outlier — a dystopian-flavored coming-of-age built around a hero who cries, fears, and keeps going anyway. Anjelica is hidden among fairy-folk in small-town Missouri to learn control, then is pulled through a portal to another world where she joins a rebellion and helps remake a tyranny into a republic. Three internal books.

title: Junebug & Carl
teaser: Fairy-folk foster parents in small-town Missouri.
body: A warm rural couple in Bronard, Missouri who take Anjelica in to keep her safe. Junebug runs the Dessertation bakery and has a drop of fairy blood (magical intuition); Carl has more, able to move through the ether like Kimberly. Loving but protective wardens, with a daughter, Lizzie. They give Anjelica the closest thing to a real family she's known.

title: Bronard, Missouri
teaser: A small farm town quietly full of fairy-folk.
body: A tiny town hours from St. Louis where cows outnumber people ten to one — and where a community of fairy-folk live hidden, looking out for each other. Kimberly hides Anjelica here to learn control away from the demons that hunt her in Los Angeles. Home of the Dessertation bakery.

title: Margaret-Regina
teaser: A girl in a wheelchair who becomes a queen.
body: A sharp, fearless girl who uses a wheelchair — the first true friend Anjelica makes in small-town Bronard. She crosses into the world of Onmiri alongside Anjelica and Kimberly, throws herself into the rebellion against King Ulthar unflinchingly, and ultimately becomes a queen.

title: King Ulthar
teaser: A tech-worshipping tyrant from another world.
body: The brutal, self-mythologizing king of a conquering nation, an offworlder obsessed with returning home to his lost wife via the god-paths — a journey that requires sacrificing one of his own bloodline (he killed his infant son Clevin to open a bridge). His regime worships technology to a near-religious degree, which is also its great weakness. Deposed with Anjelica's help.

source.tradition: Lovecraftian (name borrowed from the PD place)
source.real: Ulthar is Lovecraft's Dreamlands town ('The Cats of Ulthar,' 1920) — a place-name, not a king.
source.weave: The Weave's King Ulthar is a brutal, self-mythologizing conqueror who borrows the Lovecraftian place-name as his royal title — an offworlder cutting a path home through the god-paths. The name nods to Lovecraft's Dreamlands while the character is the Weave's own.
source.work: H. P. Lovecraft, 'The Cats of Ulthar' (1920)

title: Prince Yimnit
teaser: Ulthar's son, who argues justice over freedom.
body: King Ulthar's surviving son, who challenges Anjelica's faith in democracy — insisting people crave justice, safety, and a good livelihood more than abstract freedom. A cunning antagonist used to broker a constitutional transition before his death.

title: Onmiri / Risyl
teaser: The offworld nation Anjelica helps reshape.
body: The world Anjelica is flung to through the Godschurch portals — a land under King Ulthar's tech-worshipping monarchy, riven by rebellion (Sindra, Volkim, Madam Fantasmo, Director Frente). Anjelica's Earth-born instinct for constitutional government reshapes it into a fledgling republic under Queen Margaret. She chooses to stay and help rebuild.

title: The Onmiri Rebellion
teaser: Freedom fighters against a god-haunted crown.
body: The underground resistance to King Ulthar — including the seer Madam Fantasmo, fighters Sindra and Volkim (who salute 'our hearts beat as one'), and the pragmatic Director Frente. They want to abolish the monarchy entirely; Anjelica steers them toward a constitutional transition instead.

title: Araphel
teaser: A gentle death-god who ferries Anjelica.
body: A death-god (a reaper-lord of the darkness, seen tending the between) who repeatedly pulls Anjelica back from death in 'the between,' sharing pancakes with her and counseling her choices. His mercy works because of her demon blood. He guides souls and lets Anjelica decide her own path before intervening.

title: Baron Samedi
teaser: A captured god, freed in battle.
body: A loa death-god whom Anjelica frees during the assault on Ulthar's stronghold; his power turns the battle and he revives the mortally-wounded Anjelica — noting gods don't keep human logic about returning favors. Another of the cosmos's many pantheon-gods.

source.real: Baron Samedi is the loa of death and the cemetery — head of the Gede family of spirits, master of the crossroads between living and dead. Depicted in a top hat, black tailcoat, and dark glasses with a skull-like face, he is irreverent, ribald, and fearless: he drinks rum, smokes, jokes, and guards the dead while deciding who may yet be healed. Death as a charismatic, laughing power.
source.weave: The Weave's Baron Samedi is a loa death-god who turns a battle and revives the mortally-wounded — 'noting gods don't keep human logic about returning favors.' It keeps his nature: death that is also generous, irreverent, and bound by its own strange rules.

title: Time (Lizzie & the threads)
teaser: A prophecy, a decade on the run, and the loom of fate.
body: Book 3, the series' first time-travel story, centered on Lizzie. An Oracle's prophecy — 'in the ashes of her past she will rise, and her death will save us all' — sends Lizzie fleeing for a decade, severing every attachment, until her fate catches her anyway. Dying, she journeys through Heaven and Hell to undo a corrupted timeline and confronts the Fates' loom directly. Sets up the team-up finale, Heaven.

title: Lizzie
teaser: Junebug & Carl's daughter, doomed by prophecy.
body: The adopted daughter of Junebug and Carl and Anjelica's 'sister.' At sixteen the Oracle Starr Wolfsong foretold her death would save the world, so Lizzie ran for ten years — changing names and towns every season, never letting anyone close, to keep her past from 'burning.' Carries a black opal protection amulet. In the end she embraces her destiny, choosing death to save the child Veronica.

title: Starr Wolfsong
teaser: A dying Oracle who sees every visitor's death.
body: The Oracle of Bronard, said to descend from the seers of Delphi — gaunt, chain-smoking, and unable to offer false hope, for she sees the death of every soul who enters her trailer. Her prophecy sets Lizzie's tragic course.

title: White & Red Threads
teaser: The color of a life going right — or wrong.
body: In the Fates' loom, each soul's thread runs white when its life unfolds as it should and turns red when the timeline goes wrong (a death that shouldn't happen, a choice that breaks fate). The Fates and Talinda must coax red threads back to white before they reach the loom — the mechanic that makes meddling with time catastrophic.

title: Doretha
teaser: A Fate's daughter who murdered her mother to remake the world.
body: The true villain of Time: across a hundred timelines and a thousand attempts she manufactured Lizzie's trust — even faking her own death in a burning world to 'prove' Lizzie right — all to turn her against Talinda and seize the time-stopwatch and the dagger, with the trickster god Loki as her accomplice.

title: The Time Being
teaser: The keeper of time, found through madness.
