body: The being who governs time, sought by Lizzie through Hell to reverse Veronica's death. The path runs through Rosalie Louey, a prophet driven mad in Hell who speaks only in riddles and strings of numbers — and ultimately to Talinda's loom, where time and fate are one.

title: God (of Heaven)
teaser: The distant deity who tasks Lizzie.
body: The God of Heaven in the Godsverse — who, despite his reputation for hating monsters, tasks the half-fae Lizzie with reversing time to save Veronica. A remote, judging power whose angels keep watch over every Apocalypse prophecy.

title: Overbrook, Oregon
teaser: A small town where a saved child is hidden.
body: A small Oregon town where Kimberly places the rescued Veronica with her stern preacher father and his son Barry, to be made strong for her future. The same town that later appears, ravaged by the Apocalypse, when Kimberly reunites with Julia.

title: Heaven (the team-up finale)
teaser: Four heroes, four threads, one Apocalypse plot.
body: Book 4, the Avengers-style finale of the early arc, told in four rotating POVs — Kimberly, Anjelica, Lizzie, and Ollie — years after their own books. A doomsday cult and a treasonous angelic insurrection try to crack open the Apocalypse; the four converge, each earning an ending that explains their absence from the rest of the series. Bridges directly into Death.

title: The Blue Trident
teaser: A doomsday cult that would end the world to save it.
body: A secretive end-times cult — a portent of the Apocalypse, per the dragon Aziolith — whose members die mysteriously when tracked. They believe the only mercy is to end the world to relieve Lucifer's collapsing underworld, and their cause becomes the lever Et'atal and the rebel angels use.

source.real: The trident is the three-pronged spear of Poseidon (Roman Neptune), Greek god of the sea — with it he stirs storms, splits rock, and shakes the earth. The emblem of sea-power and of the god who can wreck the world's coasts at will.
source.weave: The Weave's Blue Trident is a secretive end-times cult bearing the trident as its sign — borrowing Poseidon's world-shaking emblem for a doomsday sect that believes the only mercy is to end the world. The sea-god's destroyer-symbol as an apocalyptic banner.

title: Geordi
teaser: A god-touched boy Kimberly hunts to save.
body: An eleven-year-old boy touched by the gods, taken by the demon Ch'ri'yl — the missing-child case that pulls Kimberly into the Blue Trident plot. Recovered and reunited with his fiercely devoted mother Malika, who gives up everything to keep him safe under Kimberly's protection.

title: Agent Davis
teaser: A Godschurch agent who recruits Lizzie.
body: A Godschurch agent who operates discreetly within Heaven, tasked with spiriting away the treasonous archangels to a hidden penal colony — work that must stay off the Godschurch's books to avoid Zeus's notice. He recruits the newly-empowered Lizzie to join him, sealing her path into the wider galaxy.

title: Michael
teaser: The archangel who holds Heaven's line.
body: The archangel Michael, who leads the loyalist defense when most of Heaven's archangels turn traitor under Gabriel, and quietly arranges to hide the captured rebels rather than let the Godschurch — or Zeus — learn how badly Heaven fractured.

source.real: Michael is the warrior archangel who leads Heaven's armies against the dragon in Revelation and stands as the great prince and defender in Daniel. He is the martial counterforce to the fallen Lucifer — Heaven's general.
source.weave: The Weave keeps Michael as Heaven's enforcer-archangel, the martial muscle of the order — consistent with his myth as the angel who casts down the rebel.

title: Et'atal, Lucifer's son
teaser: The arms-lord revealed as the Devil's heir.
body: The demon arms-lord who menaced Ollie in Magic is revealed in Heaven to be Lucifer's own son — the architect of the Apocalypse plot, wielding the Dagger of Obsolescence and allying with rebel angels. Barred from his father's warded castle, his convoluted schemes repeatedly collapse, and Akta exploits exactly that.

title: Death (Katrina Hates the Dead)
teaser: Katrina's rise from survivor to Devil to god.
body: Book 5, the novelization of the Katrina Hates the Dead graphic novel, in three internal books (Hates the Dead / Gods / Universe). It tells Katrina's full origin: a foul-mouthed Apocalypse survivor in Overbrook, Oregon who sets out to kill the Devil, accidentally inherits Hell, modernizes it, and rises to godhood across ten thousand years. The prose source for the comic in the app, and the keystone of Katrina's whole arc.

title: Katrina Clark (before the throne)
teaser: The survivor who refused to die.
body: Before she was the Devil, Katrina was a brash, scarred young woman from Overbrook, Oregon — surviving two years into the Apocalypse on pure stubborn will, delivering pizza, burying her father (an engineer who restored the town's dam and begged her to kill him rather than let him turn). Her refusal to give up the will to live is the engine of her entire ascent.

title: Connie (Veronica)
teaser: The prophecy child Lizzie saves — Katrina's frenemy and a future Devil.
body: Born Veronica, a fae 'prophecy girl' hunted by demons from birth. In Time, after her mother Becky is murdered, Lizzie smuggles her across the country and even dies bargaining with the Time Being to undo the child's death; Kimberly hides her in Overbrook, Oregon, with a hard preacher father who renames her CONNIE to make her strong for what's to come. In Death, grown up in Overbrook with her boyfriend Dennis and her brother Barry, she becomes Katrina's brash, fierce best frenemy through the Apocalypse and the wars in Heaven — and when Katrina ascends, Connie takes her place as the Devil of Hell. The girl Lizzie crossed timelines to save becomes the next link in the chain of tricked Devils.

title: Barry
teaser: Katrina's zombie ex-roommate, a gentle monster.
body: Connie's brother and Katrina's freeloading ex-roommate, who rose as a lucid zombie after the Apocalypse and can't stomach the slaughter other monsters revel in — so he files paperwork in Hell instead. He guides Katrina and Connie through Hell. (The same Barry whose preacher family fosters Veronica in Overbrook.)

source.real: The zombie originates in Haitian Vodou belief — a corpse reanimated and stripped of will — and was transformed by modern horror (Romero) into the shambling, hungering risen dead of an apocalypse. The body without the self, or the dead that will not stay down.
source.weave: The Weave's Barry 'rose as a lucid zombie after the Apocalypse' but, unusually, keeps his mind and can't stomach the slaughter — inverting the mindless-undead trope: a self-aware zombie with a conscience, set in the risen-dead apocalypse.

title: Thomas
teaser: A shapeshifting demon who briefly seized Hell.
body: A predatory shapeshifting demon who seduces Katrina, then manipulates her into killing Lucifer so he can seize Hell's power and wage war on Heaven. Katrina kills him with God's flaming sword — and in doing so becomes the Devil herself. (He reappears, redeemed-ish, as her demon ally in the Apocalypse of Darkness.)

title: Urania
teaser: Katrina's mother — and her great weakness.
body: Katrina's mother, who pressed a protective rosary on her at the Apocalypse's start. Years later Katrina risks the entire universe to save her from torment, choosing her mother over the fate of all creation. A muse-like figure (sharing the name of the Greek muse of astronomy) who becomes Katrina's steadfast companion and the heart that keeps her human.

title: The Horde (unleashed)
teaser: Insectoid devourers loosed by killing Zeus.
body: When Katrina kills Zeus, she inadvertently unleashes the Horde — insectoid servants of the Old Ones wielding planet-killing technology and soul-harvesting weapons. Their planet-killer is led by the Bug Pharaoh L'l'itoh, whom Katrina ultimately persuades to leave the universe rather than destroy it, sending it through a black hole toward Cronus.

title: Katrina Hates the Dead (comic)
teaser: The graphic novel Death novelizes.
body: The Godsverse graphic novel that Death expands into prose — Katrina's introduction in comic form, the first Godsverse comic the author paired with a novel (back in 2017, alongside Hell for Pixie Dust). Available in the app's comic reader.

title: Dennis
teaser: Connie's boyfriend, who fights to the universe's edge.
body: Connie's boyfriend from Overbrook, who survives the Apocalypse alongside Katrina and Connie and ends up fighting beside gods at the universe's farthest reaches — from Hell's pits to the Horde's planet-killer. Loyal, blunt, and pragmatic in a crisis.

title: Doom (Rebecca & the Godschurch)
teaser: How a mercenary became the Godschurch's director.
body: Book 6, in three internal books ('Every Planet Has a Godschurch,' 'There's Every Reason to Fear,' 'The End Tastes Like Pancakes'). It is Rebecca's origin: a scarred mercenary on a ruined Earth, recruited by Velaska into the Godschurch, who rises to lead it through the Battle of the Obelisk and remakes its mission from protecting gods to seeking justice for all. Chronologically sits just before Hell.

title: Thebos
teaser: A ruined Earth city carved up by demon warlords.
body: The slum-ridden city where Rebecca lives as a mercenary, twenty years after the Horde War — Earth reduced to demon-warlord fiefdoms (Piggy, Ctumiti 'Itty,' Gliporg, all under Ul'brem). Brown water, hoarded aspirin, daily kill-lists. The bleak ground floor from which the Godschurch lifts Rebecca.

title: The Sun Incident
teaser: The day Earth fell into a black hole — and came back.
body: Thirty years before Doom, Earth's sun collapsed into a black hole and swallowed the planet whole, killing eighty percent of humanity in an instant, before spitting Earth back into the universe unharmed. Rumored to be the work of Apollo. A scar across human history that precedes the Horde War.

title: The Battle of the Obelisk
teaser: The Godless-vs-Godschurch war that broke the church.
body: The climactic battle on the planet Niloria: the Godschurch's full force, with Katrina, Urania, Apollo, and Velaska, storms the Godless stronghold at the Obelisk amid Cronus and Rhea's rampage. A massacre that kills most of the Godschurch's agents and dues-paying gods — the wound the church is still nursing a generation later. Rebecca emerges its leader and reforges its purpose.

title: Aranya
teaser: A peerless warrior who lost her god and her home.
body: A fierce sword-wielding warrior Rebecca meets after the Godless annihilate Aranya's home and her god Thor. Channeling grief into vengeance, she vows to hunt the Godless across the cosmos and fights at Rebecca's side through the Battle of the Obelisk.

title: Persephone
teaser: A goddess who walks among her people once a year.
body: A goddess of the Zeus pantheon, unusual for descending from Mount Olympus once a year to walk among mortals — a habit other gods mock as weakness. Rebecca is assigned to protect her from a Godless bomber, an early Godschurch mission. Her 'light' tastes of sugared pomegranate.

source.real: Persephone is the Greek goddess who becomes queen of the underworld, daughter of Demeter and Zeus. Carried off by Hades, she eats pomegranate seeds in the underworld and so must return there for part of each year — the myth the Greeks used to explain the cycle of the seasons, her ascent bringing spring and her descent winter. She is both the maiden (Kore) and the dread queen of the dead.
source.weave: The Weave nods directly to the myth — her 'light tastes of sugared pomegranate,' the fruit that bound her to the underworld — while giving her the unusual habit of descending among mortals, a gentleness the other gods mock.
source.excerpt_ref: the pomegranate and the bargain of the seasons

crosslinks.summary: Persephone (Greek) sits on the cross-pantheon underworld map — linked across the Great Divide to the Norse Hel and guided by the Vodou Legba.

interactions.note: Hel (Norse) rules the frozen side; Persephone (Greek) the warm — the two queens face each other across the Great Divide.
Legba (Vodou) is the gatekeeper who guides souls to the queen — Vodou and Greek underworlds interlinked.
Her Greek realm sits on the hot side of the cross-pantheon underworld border.

title: The Light (divine travel)
teaser: Every god's flash of teleportation has a flavor.
body: Every god can vanish and reappear anywhere on a planet in a flash they call 'the light' — instant within a world, but interstellar jumps tax the body. Each god's light carries a distinct taste (Persephone's is sugared pomegranate; Katrina's maraschino cherry), a quiet signature of who passed through.

title: The Demon Warlords
teaser: Post-war Earth, ruled by feuding demon kingpins.
body: After the Horde War, the demons who fought the bugs turned their violence on humanity, carving Earth into warring fiefdoms. Warlords like Piggy, Ctumiti ('Itty'), and Gliporg run cities through fear, money, and hired guns — overseen by the greater warlord Ul'brem. The world Rebecca survives by killing for them.

title: The Vessel
teaser: A walled city, five immortal rulers, and one girl's revolt.
body: A self-contained dystopian science-fiction novel (four internal books: The Journey, The Center, Transference, Redemption), separate from the Godsverse cosmology. In a domed City of six rings sealed under a radiation Bubble, five body-hopping immortals called the Five rule absolutely. A farm girl, Althea, volunteers as a Vessel, uncovers the lie that keeps the City caged, and leads a revolution to open the Bubble.

title: Althea
teaser: A farm-girl mechanic who becomes a god, then frees her world.
body: The seventeen-year-old narrator, a sharp, stubborn farm girl from the Outer Rings betrothed to Jake, who volunteers for Transference against her parents' wishes (they once did a Transference 'to escape,' and it hardened them). Surviving a train disaster, loss, and the Center's trials, she uncovers the Five's lie, wins Transference yet lives, impersonates Earth under duress, and becomes a figure of the rebellion.

title: The Five
teaser: Immortal minds who rule the City body to body.
body: The eternal protectors of the City — five minds that never die, passing from one young human body to the next via Transference, ruling from the Center for millennia while the people stay trapped under the Bubble. Named for elements (Wind, Earth, Time...). Worshipped as gods, with their own scripture (the Book of Books); to be chosen as a Vessel means death of the host and supposed ascension. The story opens with the first true death of one of them — Wind — shattering the belief that they are truly immortal.

title: Transference
teaser: Pouring an ancient mind into a young body.
body: The ritual by which one of the Five abandons an aging body for a fresh young one, killing the chosen Vessel. Eligible youths compete in trials at the Center to be selected; candidates must be virgins and under eighteen. Sold as a holy honor (ascension to the Origin Point), it is in truth how the Five perpetuate their rule. Althea volunteers against her parents' wishes; she and Henry deliberately break the virginity rule as an act of defiance.

title: The City & Its Six Rings
teaser: A walled society stratified from Center to rim.
body: The whole of known society: a vast walled City of six concentric rings radiating from the Center where the Five live. Wealth and power sit nearest the Center (the First Ring); farmers, miners, and the poor are pushed to the Fifth and Sixth; the crowded Third teems with shanties. All of it sealed beneath the Bubble.

title: The Bubble
teaser: A force field sold as shelter — and a cage.
body: The energy dome enclosing the City, maintained by Wind, said to shield citizens from lethal outside radiation. Its true purpose is control: the radiation threat is a lie that keeps the population caged and dependent on the Five. Althea opens it at the story's end, breathing free outside air for the first time in thousands of years.

title: The Muties
teaser: An outcast underclass — and the seed of rebellion.
body: Mutants barred from jobs, housing, and the right to breed, herded into the shanties of the Third Ring as 'an affront to the natural order.' It is from the Muties that the rebellion rises, leaking the data that exposes the Five and rallying behind Althea's march to the Bubble.

title: Skritch's Revenge
teaser: A cyberpunk revenge heist in a neon hellscape.
body: A self-contained cyberpunk novel, its own world apart from the Godsverse. Skritch — a cybernetically-rebuilt, cat-sized 'cryptophage' — loses the only family she has when her adoptive father Jammer is murdered, and tears through the towering city of Zhakatal hunting his killer with a stolen edge over a crime boss. A story of grief, revenge, found family, and thieving in an end-stage-capitalist nightmare.

title: Skritch
teaser: Not a cat — a cybernetic cryptophage thief.
body: The narrator — a cryptophage: a small, cat-sized being who is emphatically NOT a cat (she has opposable thumbs, speech, a cybernetic arm and leg, and a metal spinal exoskeleton), and will threaten anyone who tries to scratch her chin. A gifted thief and infiltrator, raised by the hacker Jammer (who named her after finding her, briefly thinking her a stray 'Noodle'). When her father is killed and his secret vault hunted by everyone, she sets out for revenge.

title: Jammer
teaser: A dwarf thief, hacker, and Skritch's father.
body: Skritch's adoptive father and handler — a legendary hacker who runs a hover-car repair shop as a front for a hacking-and-theft operation out of a ship graveyard. Cagey and protective, he guards a mysterious vault whose contents the police, corporations, and The Spike all kill to obtain; his death sets Skritch's revenge in motion.

title: Zhakatal
teaser: A towering, lawless capitalist megacity.
body: The vertical megacity where Skritch lives — hundred-plus-story towers, hover cars, laser-gridded corporate vaults, and a brutal underclass of mutants and orcs preyed on by crime families and bounty hunters. An 'end-stage capitalist nightmare hellscape' where elves hoard nanite tech and the disenfranchised are fodder.

title: Nanites (Skritch's)
teaser: Elf-only microbots, stolen and reverse-engineered.
body: Microscopic robots normally controllable only by elves, reverse-engineered by Skritch's clan and embedded in her cybernetic arm. She uses them to loosen bolts, form ropes, and manipulate metal — until they're destroyed against a laser grid, stripping her of her greatest tool at her lowest point.

title: Mouse (Melita)
teaser: The bounty hunter who killed Jammer.
body: Codename Mouse (real name Melita), a green-mohawked operative who poses as a rescuer from The Spike, then betrays Skritch and Jammer — relying on a pair of combat drones and platinum-weave armor. Skritch's chief target for revenge, finally killed in a drone-filled showdown.

title: Xree
teaser: A hacker with a magical touch and a hard past.
body: A street-raised hacker with an affinity for computers and 'magical things of a certain sort,' once a Zchar-family criminal alongside Mouse, now working for the better side. She becomes Skritch's ally and bridge into the city's criminal web.

title: Gilles
teaser: A crime boss made beholden to Skritch.
body: A powerful, untechnical crime boss who builds an empire from mutants and orcs that polite society discards. Skritch leverages incriminating data to force Gilles's protection — an uneasy alliance with a boss who'd happily cut off her thumb to be free of her.

title: The Zchar Family
teaser: The crime dynasty tangled through Skritch's hunt.
body: A criminal dynasty (Fabian Zchar and kin) whose orbit shaped Mouse and Xree in their youth and keeps resurfacing in Skritch's revenge — from a jailbreak of Vazia Zchar to the deeper conspiracy behind 'The Spike.'

title: Paradise (comic)
teaser: A frozen soldier wakes a century later in a lab that owns him.
body: A Godsverse-flavored science-fiction comic. Cody, an Army Ranger from the dead-end town of Paradise, Alaska, is frozen and wakes in 2112 inside Hort-I-Vex, Earth's most advanced laboratory, where his estranged brother Aesop experiments on 'Paradise survivors.' God-touched with regeneration and raw power, Cody escapes to the city's depths and sets out to free the woman he loved — who is still frozen above. Ends mid-ascent on a cliffhanger.

title: Cody
teaser: An Iraq-vet Ranger, frozen and reborn god-touched.
body: A hard-drinking, fatalistic Army Ranger from Paradise, Alaska who loved his brother's wife, Jo. Frozen and revived a hundred years later in 2112, he awakens with god-touched gifts — energy bursts from his hands and a body that survives a thousand-story fall. Bitter, defiant, and bent on freeing Jo from the lab that froze them both.

title: Aesop
teaser: Cody's brother, who runs the lab that owns him.
body: Cody's estranged brother (the two deny being brothers to the last), married to Jo. A century later he is a power at Hort-I-Vex, overseeing the experiments on the frozen 'Paradise survivors' and calling Cody his 'prized subject.' Insists he is not evil even as he cages his own kin.

title: Jo
teaser: Aesop's wife, the woman Cody won't leave frozen.
body: Aesop's wife and mother of Oscar, weary of her hard farm life in Paradise, Alaska and quietly drawn to Cody. A hundred years on she remains frozen at Hort-I-Vex, not yet thawed — and the reason Cody plans to fight his way back up the tower.

title: Hort-I-Vex
teaser: Earth's most advanced lab — and a prison for the frozen.
body: In 2112, Earth's foremost scientific facility, a thousand-plus-story tower generating a hundred thousand patents a year. It revives people frozen from the town of Paradise to experiment on them; a rare few gain powers like regeneration. Its castoffs are dumped to 'the Dregs' at the city's base.

title: The Paradise Survivors
teaser: People frozen from one town, thawed to be tested.
body: Men and women cryogenically frozen from Paradise, Alaska and revived a century later by Hort-I-Vex as test subjects. Most stay powerless, but a handful — like Cody and Bobby — wake with god-touched abilities such as instant healing, which is exactly why the lab prizes them.

title: Bobby
teaser: A fellow survivor who heals from any wound.
body: An old friend of Cody's, also frozen from Paradise and thawed years earlier, now scraping by in the Dregs. He can knit any wound shut instantly — 'this is why we're so valuable' — and becomes Cody's partner in the plan to storm Hort-I-Vex.

title: The Dregs
teaser: The bottom of a thousand-story city, where castoffs land.
body: The lightless base of the towering 2112 city, where everything — and everyone — Hort-I-Vex discards drifts down: trash, undesirables, and the powerless Paradise survivors. Cody calls it Hell. Home to the bar with the last clean water piping in the city.

title: Dragon Strife (saga)
teaser: A sacrifice, a dragon who saves her, and a kingdom's lie.
body: A five-book fantasy saga (The Dragon Scourge, The Dragon Champion, The Dragon Goddess, Wicked Bodies, Wicked Minds) following Gilda, a girl raised to be fed to the dragon lord Ewig. Its dragons — Ewig among them — connect outward to the wider Cosmic Weave: Ewig also appears in the Godsverse book Eternity. A story of sacrifice, truth, and the gulf between a people and the monster they fear.

title: Gilda
teaser: Raised to be eaten — she lived instead.
body: A girl chosen at birth as the 'cedar sacrifice,' pampered and kept smooth-skinned for fifteen years to be fed to the dragon lord Ewig. When she walks into his lair to die, she discovers every sacrificed girl is secretly alive — and must learn, for the first time, to work and survive. Returning to her village exposes the lie and makes her a bridge between her people and the dragon, earning a seat on the city council.

title: Ewig
teaser: A dragon lord who saves the girls he 'devours.'
body: The great dragon lord bound by a century-old blood pact to the village beneath his volcano: every five years a girl is sacrificed to him, and in return he keeps the volcano dormant and the village safe. The truth is that Ewig devours no one — he secretly shelters every 'sacrificed' cedar alive within his lair. A protector wearing a monster's reputation. Ewig also appears in the Godsverse book Eternity, tying Dragon Strife into the wider Cosmic Weave.

title: The Cedars
teaser: The 'sacrificed' girls, secretly alive in the volcano.
body: The line of sacrifice-girls given to Ewig every five years — each believed devoured, all in truth living together in a hidden community within his volcano: Renata, Mari, Fadia, Selma, Nur, and now Gilda. They hunt, fish, garden, smoke meat, and survive. Bound by a fierce sisterhood and a terrible shared secret they will kill to protect — a tension that once tore them apart in the Exodus.

title: Renata
teaser: A cedar who learned to kill to keep the secret.
body: A cedar sacrificed five years before Gilda, now a hardened hunter, fisher, and the cedars' enforcer who teaches Gilda to survive — but who will kill anyone who threatens the secret that the cedars live, as she nearly does to Leyhan. Morally complex: maternal and patient one moment, lethal the next, she takes too much joy in killing. Her willingness to kill is what split the cedars in the Exodus.

title: Sister Milka
teaser: The nun who trained Gilda to die well.
body: The harsh, unforgiving nun who raised Gilda from infancy to be the perfect sacrifice — drilling the ritual creed into her, controlling her every habit, and never relenting even on Gilda's last day. The human face of the village's pitiless tradition.

title: Leyhan
teaser: Gilda's best friend and would-be love.
body: Gilda's childhood best friend and secret love (cedars are forbidden to love), spared the sacrifice only for being a boy. He alone recognizes Gilda alive behind Ewig and climbs the forbidden mountain to find her — nearly murdered by Renata for it. His insistence on telling the village the truth forces the reveal that ends the lie.

title: Unestra
teaser: The mother goddess prayed to across Dragon Strife.
body: The mother goddess of Gilda's world, invoked in the cedars' prayers ('Unestra, mother goddess, forgive them, for they know not what they do'). A source of comfort, immortal souls, and the promise of rebirth in eternity. Unestra also appears in the Godsverse book Eternity, binding Dragon Strife into the wider Cosmic Weave.

title: Yesiburgh
teaser: The village that sacrificed its daughters to a dragon.
body: Gilda's home village, beneath Ewig's volcano — a hard farming-and-timber town that for a century fed a girl to the dragon every five years. After the cedars return alive, it convulses: the elder council is dismantled for a city council, the cedars reintegrate amid hostility, and the disgraced Sister Milka falls from grace.

title: The Emperor
teaser: The ruler whose army marches on the dragon's town.
body: The emperor whose red-and-yellow army arrives at Yesiburgh once Ewig's defiance of dragon tradition is known. His commanders Lord Bessinger and Dame Farcile come as envoys; his reach and his dragons (and Ewig's own sister among the imperial powers) become the saga's central external threat.

title: Ewig's Sister
teaser: Ramidion — Ewig's sister, who won the war on the gods.
body: Ewig's sister, the dragon Ramidion, who 'started the war on the gods and won their freedom' and holds power in the Emperor's domain. Her envoys tread carefully around Ewig out of her code, but his defiance sets her against him. (She is the same dragon Ramidion who hunts Ophelia a generation later in the saga's second half.)

title: Lord Bessinger & Dame Farcile
teaser: Armand Bessinger — Ewig's old war-comrade, now his enemy.
body: Lord Armand Bessinger, commander of the Emperor's Gilded Army, and his second Dame Farcile. A mountain of a man in gold plate, he fought beside Ewig in the Godwars a century ago and shares the dragon's old taste for slaughter. Sent to 'deal with' the living cedars, he betrays a truce, takes Gilda and Leyhan hostage, murders witnesses to bury the Dragon Charter evidence, and is finally broken when Ewig razes his army.

title: Councilman Edward
teaser: A guilt-ridden elder seeking redemption.
body: Yesiburgh's ex-mayor, now a city councilman, who helped send Gilda to her death and is haunted by it. Gilda's refusal to throw him away moves him toward atonement — choosing to be a hero rather than the monster of the cedars' nightmares.

title: Emperor Paraphal
teaser: The dragon-backed emperor Ewig wars against.
body: Emperor Paraphal, ruler of the domain whose army burned Yesiburgh. After Ewig annihilates Lord Bessinger's force, every soldier and dragon in Paraphal's realm turns against the rogue dragon lord — and Ewig's campaign of vengeance against the emperor drives the open war of the saga's middle.

title: Terzana
teaser: A dragon-mage who joined Ewig — and his real plan.
body: A dragon-mage who joined Ewig after he killed her old tormentor's ally Grimda. Wry, ruthless, and pragmatic ('we all use each other'), she orchestrates the real plan behind the fake peace embassy — and hides its cost from Gilda: that Gilda must eat a dragon's heart and let the goddess Unestra possess her body to breach the barrier. A granddaughter of war-healers, obsessed with magic, brought into it by Ramidion.

title: Sytrol
teaser: Ewig's vain sibling dragon at the Great Gate.
body: Ewig's vain sibling dragon (blue-and-red scaled, purple from afar) who rules the Great Gate prison-fortress and, unlike her war-hungry brothers, does not want war. Gilda comes as Ewig's envoy ostensibly to negotiate peace — but it's cover for a heist. Her fortress falls to Unestra-possessed Gilda and Ewig's army.

title: Ashceles
teaser: The seat the dragon lords seized from the old gods.
body: The realm or seat from which the dragon lords expelled the old gods' brethren after rising up and striking down the mother goddess Unestra. With their expulsion came a barrier sealed around the planet so the banished gods could no longer hear or answer prayers — the dragons' world made deaf to its old deities.

title: The Dragon–God War & the Barrier
teaser: How dragons cast down the gods and sealed the sky.
body: The ancient war in which the dragon lords rose up, struck down the mother goddess Unestra, and expelled her divine brethren from Ashceles — then erected a barrier around the whole planet so the old gods could neither hear nor answer prayers. Gilda's mother framed it bitterly: her people only ever got to choose whose oppression to live under, the capricious gods or the crueler dragons. This war and barrier mirror the dragon-versus-god conflict in the Godsverse book Eternity, binding Dragon Strife into the Cosmic Weave.

title: Gilda, the Vessel of Unestra
teaser: The girl chosen to carry a goddess — and her line.
body: The secret at the heart of Ewig and Terzana's plan: Gilda must consume a dragon's heart and become the living vessel for the mother goddess Unestra, the only one whose returning magic can breach the barrier the dragons sealed. Unestra possesses Gilda to seize the Great Gate, then — spent — implants herself in Gilda's womb to reincarnate, fulfilling a prophecy that 'a god made mortal will create a line that brings the gods back.' The direct seed of Ophelia's story.

title: Ophelia
teaser: A hunted girl who shares her body with a goddess.
body: The narrator of the saga's second half, seventeen, daughter of Gilda and carrier of the goddess Unestra's soul — whom she hears as a constant inner voice. A deal her mother made for Unestra to take Ophelia's body (to defeat Sytrol) went half-wrong: Ophelia kept her own mind and gained Unestra as a nagging companion. Raised a princess at the Great Gate, orphaned and on the run, she's a hot-headed woman of action covered in warlock rune-tattoos that focus, amplify, and ward her magic. She gets herself arrested on purpose to infiltrate Saint Agnes's Academy and steal the Xhasharian.

title: Unestra's Vessel
teaser: A goddess's soul riding in a mortal girl.
body: The arrangement at the heart of the saga's second half: Ophelia's mother bargained for the mother goddess Unestra to take over Ophelia's consciousness and defeat the dragon Sytrol. The transfer failed halfway — Ophelia keeps her own self while Unestra lives on as a voice in her mind, advising, scolding, and rarely praising. Goddess-touched abilities follow (resisting truth-spells, the will to attempt goddess-level magic).

title: The Xhasharian
teaser: The relic that could banish the dragons.
body: The most dangerous book in the world, hidden in a clockwork-guarded archive beneath Saint Agnes's Academy library. Ophelia infiltrates the academy to steal it; with it she could banish the dragons and bring back the gods. She escapes with it through collapsing tunnels, leaving her captured friends behind.

title: Ramidion
teaser: The evil dragon who has hunted Ophelia since she was five.
body: The dragon who sent an assassin to kill Ophelia at age five (her handmaid Claudette died in her place) and rules through her puppet, Emperor Paraphal. The chief dragon antagonist of the saga's second half, against whom Ophelia carries the hope of restoring the gods.

title: Hyspia & Everia
teaser: The dragon-ruled kingdom and its guarded capital.
body: The kingdom (Hyspia/Hypsian) stretching ocean to ocean, ruled by the dragon Ramidion through Emperor Paraphal, its capital the heavily guarded city of Everia. The land where the old gods can no longer be heard, and where Ophelia's rebellion seeks the Xhasharian to bring them back.

title: Fharin
teaser: Ophelia's lifelong guardian and contact.
body: A one-eyed old soldier of Ophelia's childhood guard (the 'dandelion ice cream' friend who treated her as a person, not a savior). He smuggles her toward Everia, reluctantly helps engineer her arrest, and works with the hidden resistance — including Doctor Barclay and Miss Hectarin — to keep her alive.

title: Gilda the Unbreakable
teaser: The sacrifice who became a queen and a legend.
body: What Gilda becomes: 'Gilda the Usurper' to enemies, 'Gilda the Unbreakable' to followers — queen of the Great Gate and figurehead of the rebellion, mother of Ophelia. Held captive (not dead) by Ramidion, her survival drives the finale. Freed, she stuns everyone by choosing peace: she agrees with Ramidion's case and becomes queen-regent of the new constitutional monarchy, freeing every witch and cedar.

title: Miss Hectarin
teaser: An old sorceress with deep roots, aiding Ophelia.
body: A disbarred old lawyer and secret witch with deep roots, palace contacts, and her own history with Saint Agnes. She defends Ophelia at her sham trial, shelters her after the academy escape, and becomes her key ally — wry, unsentimental, helping even when she thinks it foolish. An ancient, well-connected magic-user who takes in the wounded Ophelia, saves her in court, and lends her illusions and palace contacts. Wry and unsentimental, she doubts the wisdom of Ophelia's rescues yet helps her anyway — 'even if I think this is foolish.'

title: The Rebellion (Saint Agnes & the resistance)
teaser: The fight to bring back the gods and topple the dragons.
body: The underground movement to overthrow the dragon Ramidion and Emperor Paraphal and restore the old gods, threading through Everia — including the resistance cells hidden inside Saint Agnes's Academy. Ophelia's friends Celeste, Sylvia, and the spy Frida, plus Doctor Barclay, are its captured members; Gilda the Unbreakable is its symbol.

title: Celeste, Sylvia & Frida
teaser: The friends who risk everything for Ophelia.
body: Ophelia's circle at Saint Agnes's Academy: CELESTE, her kind, brainy roommate (a healer-in-training scarred for a past roommate's offense); SYLVIA, a powerful enchanter who builds clockwork men; and FRIDA, the evocation 'bully' who is secretly a deep-cover resistance agent sworn to Ophelia. Captured helping her steal the Xhasharian, they become the friends she refuses to abandon.

title: Ophelia's Battle-Magic
teaser: Goddess-fueled spells — the sword Gilda never drew.
body: By the saga's end Ophelia wields active combat magic through spoken words and rippling tattoos — concussive shockwaves ('Il'vahassa!'), resistance to truth-spells, and feats that 'take the will of a goddess.' A pointed contrast to her mother Gilda, who never took up a weapon: the daughter fights where the mother endured.

title: The Obsidian Spindle Saga
teaser: Two women, a coma, and a world where fairy tales are real.
body: A dark fairy-tale saga told by two alternating narrators — Rose, a struggling human, and Chelle, her half-gorgon love. When Rose falls into a coma, her mind drops into Urgu, a realm where fairy tales live as grim reality, and Chelle follows to bring her home. Each book twists a familiar tale (beginning with Sleeping Beauty). Its realm of Urgu sits along the same Cosmic Weave as the Godsverse and Dragon Strife, a waystation for souls bound for eternity.

source.real: The spindle is the cursed instrument of Sleeping Beauty and the tool of the Greek Fates who spin life's thread — the two great myths of the spindle.
source.weave: The Obsidian Spindle Saga is the Weave's fairy-tale thread, named for the spindle that fuses Sleeping Beauty's cursed instrument with the Fates' thread of destiny. See the Obsidian Spindles for the object itself.
source.excerpt_ref: the spindle of sleep and of fate

title: Urgu
teaser: A realm where fairy tales are grim and real.
body: The world Rose's mind falls into when she slips into a coma — a land where fairy tales live as harsh reality, frozen for thousands of years, called by its long-dwellers 'a waystation for the damned,' where souls bide time until they join eternity. Beautiful and deadly, full of dragons, witches, and chosen-one prophecies. Rose must wake herself to leave it.

title: Red
teaser: A thousand-year guardian of Urgu, sworn to Rose.
body: The Red Rider (Gabrielle) — an ancient Dreamer gifted by the Fates with the insight to always know the right course. Across the saga she hunts the banished Nimue to the Dark Planet, allies with Nox (revealed a Spore host), and in the final battle wears Nimue's banishing glyph to strike at the Spore. After a life of solitary wandering and reluctant heroism, she dies in the Celestial Realm helping end the Primordial incursion — one of two long-running heroes lost saving the universe.

title: The Divine Spark & the Dream Realm
teaser: Why humans must dream — and what powers Urgu.
body: The gods molded humanity from universal clay and placed a spark of themselves in each person, but made human bodies too brittle to hold that spark for long. So every night the sleeping soul travels to Urgu (the Dream Realm) and deposits its excess spark, which powers everything there, then returns and wakes. A soul whose body falls into a coma or dies in sleep cannot return — and is stranded in Urgu.

title: The Nightmare Realm
teaser: Urgu's dark twin, swelling as dreams die.
body: The shadow counterpart to the Dream Realm, a gateway between Hell and Earth ruled by the trickster god Epiales and fueled by darkness. Once balanced with Urgu, it now grows stronger every day: since Urgu closed to dreamers a century ago, every sleeper's spark flows here instead — which is why Earth itself is sliding into madness.

title: Dreams Into Stories
teaser: Why Earth's fairy tales are real in Urgu.
body: Dreaming is a two-way street: things born in Urgu seep into sleeping human minds and, over generations, become memories, then ideas, then the stories Earth tells. That is why Urgu is full of figures Earth knows as fairy tales — Oz, the Red Rider, the Wicked Witch — they are the originals the stories were copied from.

title: The Six Gods of Urgu
teaser: The imprisoned deities worshipped at the Church of the Six.
body: Six gods bound to or dwelling in Urgu, worshipped (and feared) at the Church of the Six: Hypnos the abandoner, Hera the cruel, Sekhmet the hunter, Anansi the sly, Loki the trickster, and Agrona the merciless. Unlike Earth's distant gods, these appear and visit their wrath on the realm. Only those who surrender their soul to one of them may wield magic.

title: Hypnos
teaser: The lost god who built Oz and kept the peace.
body: The vanished god of sleep and rightful power of Oz, who blessed Rose then disappeared a century ago. The truth: he has been hiding on Earth all along, posing as an old gambler in a Reno casino where only magical creatures can see one another, watched over by the dryad Jamil. Rose's quest-delivery leads her straight to him.

source.real: Hypnos is the Greek god of sleep, son of Nyx and twin of Thanatos. He dwells in a misty cave where the river Lethe (forgetfulness) flows, and can lull even Zeus to sleep — a power he wields, at Hera's urging, in the Iliad. Quiet and gentle, he is the nightly rehearsal of death.
source.weave: The Weave keeps Hypnos's domain (and gives his name to a relic, 'Hypnos's Coin'), drawing on the myth's god who can put even the king of gods to sleep — sleep as a power that levels even the mighty.

title: Epiales
teaser: The trickster god of the Nightmare Realm.
body: The schemer god who rules the Nightmare Realm, distrusted by the other gods. As dreams fail and nightmares swell, his domain grows ever more powerful. He once took the demon Etsop as a lover, and grants Etsop passage between his realm and Earth.

source.real: Epiales (Ephialtes) is the Greek daemon of nightmares — a son of Nyx in some traditions, the spirit who presses on sleepers and brings the suffocating night-terror (the word survives in 'ephialtes,' the nightmare). A minor but genuine personification of the bad dream itself.
source.weave: The Weave promotes him to 'the schemer god who rules the Nightmare Realm,' whose domain swells as dreams fail — taking the small Greek nightmare-daemon and scaling him into a rising underworld power.

title: The Hydra of the Spindle
teaser: The seven-headed guardian of the Obsidian Spindle.
body: A seven-headed hydra chained on the bridge to the Obsidian Spindle, which obeys only the rightful heir blessed by Hypnos. Together with the monster-filled Cursed Sea, it ensures only the worthy — or the desperate — ever reach the Fates.

source.real: The Lernaean Hydra is the many-headed serpent of Greek myth slain by Heracles — grow back two heads for each one cut, it guards its lair with venom and regeneration. The archetypal multi-headed guardian-monster.
source.weave: The Weave's Hydra of the Spindle is 'a seven-headed hydra chained on the bridge to the Obsidian Spindle' that obeys only the rightful heir — keeping the Greek many-headed guardian and setting it to guard the axis of the worlds.

title: Oz / The Emerald City
teaser: Hypnos's city, built to guard the Spindle.
body: The greatest city in Urgu, forged by Hypnos five thousand years ago around his castle to protect the Obsidian Spindle — the only land route to the Fates runs through its throne room. Its rightful queen takes the city's name as a tribute. Now held by the usurper Nimue until Rose retakes it.

source.tradition: American literature (L. Frank Baum, public domain)
source.real: The Emerald City is the capital of Oz in L. Frank Baum's The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900) — the green-glowing city at the end of the yellow brick road, seat of the Wizard and later of Ozma, rightful queen of Oz. A public-domain fairyland capital.
source.weave: The Weave's Oz/Emerald City is 'the greatest city in Urgu, forged by Hypnos to protect the Obsidian Spindle,' with Ozma as its rightful queen — keeping Baum's Emerald City and Queen Ozma and giving the fairyland a cosmic guardianship role over the Fates' spindle.
source.work: L. Frank Baum, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900)

crosslinks.summary: Oz (Baum) is woven into Greek and fairy-tale cosmology — built by the Greek Hypnos to guard the Sleeping-Beauty/Fates spindle.

interactions.note: Hypnos (Greek god of sleep) forged Oz — a Greek deity as architect of Baum's fairyland.
Oz exists to guard the Obsidian Spindle (Sleeping Beauty + Greek Fates) — American fairyland protecting a European/Greek relic.

title: Critterton
teaser: The woodland-creature village where Rose lands.
body: A village of talking woodland creatures (the Woodland Creature Society of Urgu) just outside the Enchanted Forest, where Rose's soul first arrives. Bound by a pact to keep humans out, it is burned by the Wicked Witch's dragons and guard once Rose appears.

title: The Enchanted Forest
teaser: A shifting wood ruled by the pixie courts.
body: A vast, disorienting forest where a wrong step can carry you a hundred miles, home to the Seelie and Unseelie pixies. Travelers who can't navigate it vanish forever; it stands between Critterton and the road to Oz.

title: The Cursed Sea
teaser: The monster-filled waters around the Spindle.
body: The dark, oily sea Hypnos filled with krakens and mermaids to guard the Obsidian Spindle's island. One of only two ways to reach the Fates — by braving its depths — the other being through Oz's throne room.

title: The Seelie & Unseelie
teaser: The fae courts — and which one lies.
body: The pixie courts of the Enchanted Forest. The Seelie were the good guardians; the Unseelie overthrew and devoured them, leaving only deceivers who pose as Seelie. Tiny but mighty, their concentrated magic rivals all but the god-touched; iron and boxwood repel them. Now ruled by the false 'fairy queen' Aine.

source.real: The Seelie and Unseelie Courts are the two divisions of fairy-kind in Scottish folklore — the Seelie ('blessed') inclined to help or warn humans, the Unseelie malevolent and predatory. The two faces of fae-kind: capricious benevolence and outright menace.
source.weave: The Weave's Seelie & Unseelie are the pixie courts of the Enchanted Forest — the Seelie good guardians, the Unseelie having overthrown and devoured them — keeping the authentic folkloric split (blessed vs. unblessed courts) and turning it into a conquest-history.

title: The Church of the Six
teaser: Where Urgu worships its six dread gods.
body: A crooked, six-colored church (and its grander cousin, the Cathedral of the Six beside the Oz castle) where the people appease Urgu's six gods — a prudent habit, since these gods are real and quick to wrath. Dreams are the currency offered at its altar.

title: Dreams (currency)
teaser: Glowing orbs that buy, power, and worship.
body: Pink orbs of captured dream-energy — the lifeblood and money of Urgu. They buy food and goods, power its magic and barrier, and are offered to the gods. As Earth's dreams dwindle, they grow scarce and precious.

title: Magic in Urgu
teaser: Soul-bought spellcraft, spoken with conviction.
body: In Urgu only the god-touched can cast — those who gave their soul to a god (like Nimue to Hera) or who carry inhuman blood (like Chelle's gorgon line). Spells are spoken aloud; Latin is traditional but it's the caster's conviction, not the language, that matters. Concealment amulets (sold by the demon Etsop) hide a monster's true form.

title: Gorgons
teaser: Once-beautiful beings cursed by Hera, hunted for parts.
body: A monster race cursed by Hera from beauty into snake-haired form. Their blood runs red, their snakes are (in Chelle's case) harmless, and contrary to myth they neither turn people to stone nor shapeshift. Hunted to near-extinction for imagined gold and valuable body parts, they survive by hiding among humans.

title: Monster Hunters
teaser: Earth's killers of the hidden magical world.
body: Humans who hunt monsters on Earth for profit and spite, trading in gorgon tails and other parts on a black market. Superstitious and cruel, they killed Chelle's mother and hound Chelle relentlessly — the everyday horror of being a monster in the human world.

title: Nimue (the Wicked Witch)
teaser: Hera's soul-bound regent, usurper of Oz.
body: The Wicked Witch — born Grace — who threaded through every book of the saga as villain, survivor, and at last hero. Flayed and broken, she helped slay King Hastur, then saw the Spore for the dictators they were and turned fully: she devised the realm-wide banishing circle that defeats the Primordials, working with the heroes she once tormented. She dies completing it — an evil thing who, given eternity, finally chose to be good.

title: Ozma (Iris)
teaser: The rightful, Hypnos-blessed queen of Oz.
body: Born Iris, the rightful ruler of Oz, blessed by Hypnos and trusted by the Fates — perpetually child-like in appearance yet ancient and formidable. Deposed by Nimue and driven into hiding for a century, she is a pragmatist who cast out Red for chasing 'false hope,' and ultimately passes the realm's hope to Rose.

title: Ursa
teaser: A dreamed-up bear who first guides Rose.
body: A kindly grizzly in bonnet and reading glasses, dreamed into being centuries ago by a child named Lucy who died in her sleep. A retired schoolteacher of Critterton, she gives Rose her first lesson in what Urgu is — and is killed by dragonfire shielding her.

title: Etsop
teaser: A demon trapped in human form, dealing in passage.
body: A demon cursed into a frail human body after a soul-deal gone wrong, running a derelict 'ET S OP' pet shop that hides a menagerie of magical creatures. Once Epiales's lover, he can open doors between realms — and sends Chelle through the Nightmare Realm in exchange for a future favor.

title: Mydnyte
teaser: Nox's cat-formed concubine, guardian of a door.
body: A shapeshifting demoness with onyx eyes, concubine of the goddess Nox, who granted her eternal life at the price of guarding a door into the Dream Realm until Hera no longer needs binding. She devours those who come to feed her their spark — but responds to revenge, and lets Chelle pass.

title: Jamil
teaser: A dryad friend who sets Chelle's quest in motion.
body: A college friend of Rose and Chelle, secretly a dryad (wood nymph) who hides behind a ruby concealment amulet. She first names Chelle's monster nature, connects her to the vampire Teddy, and helps her begin the search to wake Rose.

title: Teddy
teaser: A four-century-old vampire playing at college.
body: A wealthy, theatrical vampire posing as a student, who sells magical goods and his own healing saliva. For a taste of rare gorgon blood he tells Chelle the truth: to wake Rose she must reach the Obsidian Spindle in the Dream Realm.

source.real: The vampire is the undead blood-drinker of European (especially Slavic) folklore — a corpse that rises to feed on the living, later refined by Gothic literature (Polidori, Le Fanu's Carmilla, Stoker's Dracula) into the seductive, theatrical aristocrat-predator. Immortality bought with others' blood.
source.weave: The Weave's Teddy is 'a wealthy, theatrical vampire posing as a student' who sells magical goods and his own healing saliva — keeping the Gothic vampire's charm and theatricality, here a black-market dealer rather than a stalking predator.

title: Diedre
teaser: An anti-monarchist rebel leader in Urgu.
body: A hardened resistance commander who despises all rulers — Ozma and Nimue alike — as two faces of the same broken system. Distrustful of monsters at first, she fights beside Chelle against a giant and a dragon, voicing the saga's anarchist counter-argument to its restore-the-rightful-queen plot.

title: Balor
teaser: A fire-being and old agent of Ozma.
body: A burly, red-bearded creature of fire, a loyal old agent of Ozma and longtime friend of Red. He keeps his home blazing hot to disadvantage visitors, and helps guide Rose and Chelle toward Ozma and the Spindle.

source.tradition: Irish (Celtic) — fused with the Greek Cyclops
source.real: Balor is the one-eyed giant-king of the Fomorians in Irish myth — his single great eye kills everything it gazes upon, opened only in battle by his attendants. Prophesied to die by his grandson, he is slain by Lugh, who drives a sling-stone through that eye. Mythologists routinely liken Balor to the Greek Cyclops for the shared single devastating eye.
source.weave: The Weave's Balor is 'a burly, red-bearded creature of fire' and old agent of Ozma — a deliberate fusion of the Irish Balor with the Cyclops, both invoked through the single-eye motif. Russell relates the Cyclops's one eye to Balor's Evil Eye and merges the two into one fiery guardian.
source.work: Cath Maige Tuired (The Second Battle of Mag Tuired)
source.excerpt_ref: Lugh slays Balor through the eye

title: The Barrier Machine
teaser: Nimue's device to tear back through to Earth.
body: The Wicked Witch's experiment: a retro-futurist apparatus that channels a fresh dreamer's soul at the precise frequency to puncture the weakened barrier between Urgu and Earth — killing the dreamer to open a door home for Urgu's exiles, at the cost of plunging Earth into dreamless madness. Rose is its intended fuel, twice.

title: The Barrier
teaser: The wall between Urgu and Earth, weakening as dreams die.
body: The powerful, dream-powered barrier sealing the Dream Realm off from Earth and the universe. Stable for ages, it has grown weak since Hypnos vanished and dreams stopped flowing — which is why Rose, uniquely, punched through it into Urgu, and why Nimue believes a dreamer's soul can be used to tear it open.

title: Thorna
teaser: A defiant young cedar who plans to run.
body: A rebellious ten-year-old cedar-in-waiting, the next sacrifices alongside Bella. Hardened and clear-eyed, she refuses to love anyone ('it makes things too complicated') and means to escape her fate by running. The one person besides Gilda that Renata says she doesn't blame.

title: Bella
teaser: The youngest cedar, who wants to be brave.
body: A small girl raised as a future cedar sacrifice alongside Thorna, who looks up to Gilda and wants to face her fate with courage rather than flee. A reminder of the children the ritual keeps feeding to the mountain.

title: Nur
teaser: The cedars' cook, who talks to her plants.
body: A cedar who runs the volcano kitchen, wastes nothing, and 'listens' to the vegetables in Fadia's garden. After the reveal she's the first to move back to town and opens a popular bakery in Yesiburgh.

title: Fadia
teaser: The cedars' gardener, gruff and practical.
body: A long-tenured cedar who tends the volcano's hidden cliffside garden — mud-stained, blunt, and impatient with Nur's whimsy, but the source of the community's fresh food.

title: Selma
teaser: The cedars' healer, who secretly watches home.
body: The cedars' healer, who tends the others' wounds and ailments — and who secretly goes to watch the village proclamations from a hidden vantage, aching for a glimpse of the mother she lost. Sharp-tongued but grieving underneath.

title: Mari
teaser: The cedars' seamstress, with family still in town.
body: A graceful, demure cedar and skilled seamstress whose father still lives in the village. She once risked watching the proclamation and warned Gilda against the same — and after the reveal becomes apprentice to Gilda's mother in her tailor shop.

title: The Exodus
teaser: The schism that split the cedar sisterhood.
body: A past rupture among the cedars: when keeping the secret meant killing outsiders who discovered them, some cedars refused and left the volcano forever, while those who remained (like Renata) accepted lethal measures. A grief Mari still carries, and the moral fault line beneath the cedars' hidden peace.

title: Ewig & the War Against the Gods
teaser: The ancient war that left a dragon in a volcano.
body: Ewig is ancient enough to have fought in the war against the gods (the same dragon-versus-god conflict that echoes through Eternity). Left badly wounded when it ended, he settled in the volcano, whose energy feeds and heals him — so his 'protection' of the village is bound up with his own survival. He has watched everyone he ever loved die and will outlive every cedar.

title: The Dragon Charter
teaser: The century-old contract of the sacrifice.
body: The original contract, kept in a glass case, that laid out the terms of the cedar sacrifice a hundred years ago. Gilda digs it out of the Yesiburgh archives to prove Ewig broke no law by keeping the girls alive — the cedars are his 'property' to do with as he wishes. Bessinger murders the witnesses to bury it.

title: Gertrude (Gerty)
teaser: The townswoman who leads the mob against the cedars.
body: A vicious old woman who rallies Yesiburgh's bigots against the cedars, calling Gilda 'dragon meat' and demanding she die as she was 'supposed to.' She stops short of violence only for fear of the dragon lords' wrath, organizing protests and stone-throwing instead — the human face of the town's cruelty.

title: Bernice
teaser: A brave townsgirl who stands with the cedars.
body: A freckled, red-haired young woman who helps Gilda openly despite the mob's hostility, and whose family forms the core of the counter-protest that defends the cedars. Proof to Gilda — and the argument against Renata's cynicism — that the town holds good people worth saving.

title: Gilda's Father
teaser: The exiled man who returns to save his daughter.
body: Gilda's father, who was exiled from Yesiburgh and vanished into the woods when she was a child after fighting to save her from the sacrifice. A master of the forest, he reappears to ambush the prison caravan with traps and free Gilda, Leyhan, and Renata — a reunion a lifetime in the making.

title: The Godwars
teaser: The war where dragons cast down the gods.
body: The ancient war, a century past, in which the eleven dragon lords rose against and drove back the gods — Ramidion among its architects, and Ewig and Lord Bessinger among those who fought (and reveled in its slaughter) side by side. The founding violence of Gilda's world, and the same dragon-versus-god conflict that runs through Eternity and the Dragon-God War.

title: Grimda
teaser: Ewig's massive brother, killed in single combat.
body: Ewig's far larger, crueler brother dragon, who used his own soldiers for target practice. He ambushes Ewig with an army and nearly kills him in a duel, but Ewig prevails; Grimda's harvested heart, blood, and twenty talons heal Ewig and arm the rebellion. His sorcerer Terzana defects to Ewig.

title: The Great Gate
teaser: Sytrol's vine-clad prison-fortress.
body: A black-brick, vine-shrouded castle and prison ruled by the dragon Sytrol, its hundred-foot gate cranked open by hand. It holds tortured prisoners and the surviving cedars (including Freja) in its sub-basement, and houses the second-greatest spell-library in Ashceles. Captured by Gilda and Ewig, it becomes their stronghold.

title: Brothers Shandril & Mathis
teaser: The human monks who run Sytrol's prison.
body: Brother Shandril, Sytrol's oily, soft-willed 'speaker,' given to the dragon as a baby and risen to be her voice; and Brother Mathis, the squat, genuinely cruel administrator above him who once threatened to hang Terzana. The human faces of the Great Gate's casual brutality toward prisoners and cedars.

title: The Summoning Book
teaser: A spellbook where any page could end the world.
body: The Great Gate library's most guarded treasure — a tome of god-summoning spells so dangerous 'any single spell could lead to the end of the world.' Gilda steals it (leaving a forgery) to summon Unestra; she even uses one of its transformation spells to save Leyhan. Guarded by the sorcerer Buzbo.

title: Buzbo
teaser: The sorcerer-guardian of the forbidden book.
body: The Great Gate's library sorcerer, alerted the instant its doors open. He corners Gilda mid-theft and nearly kills her with old magic — until Leyhan stabs him, freeing the book and, with his death, the library's wards.

title: The Womb Prophecy
teaser: A god made mortal will birth the gods' return.
body: The old gods' last hope, held in their final days: that 'a god made mortal will create a line that brings the gods back to this world.' Spent saving the Great Gate, Unestra implants herself in Gilda's womb to reincarnate and begin that line — the prophecy that drives the saga's second half and Ophelia's birth.

title: Freja
teaser: A cedar imprisoned at the Great Gate, estranged from Renata.
body: A cedar sacrifice held among the emaciated prisoners in the Great Gate's depths, and the source of old, unresolved hurt between her and Renata. Her captivity is part of why Ewig's campaign turns toward the prison; freed in the castle's fall.

title: Gilda & Leyhan's Marriage
teaser: Wed in an army camp, on the eve of danger.
body: Gilda and her childhood love Leyhan marry hastily in the war camp — Ewig officiating, since dragons head the church — before the embassy to the Great Gate. Their bond, and Gilda's near-fatal choice to use the summoning book to save a mortally wounded Leyhan, anchor the human heart of the war.

title: Saint Agnes's Academy
teaser: The 'Wicked Witch Academy' that cages and breaks witches.
body: Saint Agnes's Academy for Wayward Witches — a moated, spike-walled fortress-school in Everia where captured witches are dampened by control-bracelets and indoctrinated to serve Emperor Paraphal and Ramidion. Run on 'survival of the fittest' cruelty by the vain, ice-wielding headmistress Saint Agnes, it trains the empire's witch-hunters and hides the Xhasharian in a clockwork archive below its library.

title: The Witch-Hunters
teaser: White-clad trackers who sniff out magic.
body: Ramidion's specially trained hunters — white-coated, able to smell magic on a witch — who patrol the capital Everia and graduate from Saint Agnes's Academy. The empire's instrument for stamping out the god-touched and the rebellion.

title: Ophelia's Rune Tattoos
teaser: Warlock sigils that focus, amplify, and hide her magic.
body: Runes inked across Ophelia's arms, designed by warlocks of the age of gods to focus and amplify her spellcraft and ward her against detection — the reason she has survived while the whole empire hunts her. She casts spoken spells through them (e.g. 'Il'grais' to grow wood, 'Il'navin' for shadow).

title: The Magic Disciplines
teaser: Evocation, conjuration, divination — and how the academy gates them.
body: Witchcraft at Saint Agnes's is sorted into disciplines marked by dress color (evocation in blue, etc.). Dampener-bracelets choke a witch's power to a trickle; amplifier beads multiply it tenfold. Spells are spoken; Al'verite is a truth-spell that sickens a liar — which Ophelia, god-trained, can resist.

title: Frida
teaser: The academy 'bully' who is secretly Ophelia's sworn agent.
body: A fierce evocation student who rules the academy through fear — and is, in truth, a deep-cover resistance spy whose people have planted agents at Saint Agnes's for a generation, all sworn to Ophelia and her mother before her. Loyal beneath the hostility, she helps steal the Xhasharian and is captured for it.

title: Doctor Barclay
teaser: The academy healer, secretly with the resistance.
body: The academy's healer and Celeste's mentor, who proves a resistance contact by passing Ophelia Fharin's private 'dandelion ice cream' sign. One of the hidden web of allies keeping Ophelia alive inside enemy walls.

title: Miss Thofferziz
teaser: The crotchety keeper of the impossible library.
body: The persnickety librarian of Saint Agnes's, whose library is bigger inside than out and runs on dilated time (a week can pass in a class period). She warns the intruders the library itself is more dangerous than what hunts them — the gateway to the clockwork archive holding the Xhasharian.

title: Illusion Magic
teaser: The subtle, spy's discipline Miss Hectarin mastered.
body: The hardest, most neglected school of magic — disguises and false worlds spun from air, needing imagination and patience few witches have. The emperor disdains it, so illusionists make the best spies; Miss Hectarin hid as a witch for sixty years with it, and Terzana used it to impersonate a vice principal inside the Academy. Ophelia, all blunt force, is hopeless at it.

title: Harold
teaser: Miss Hectarin's son — and her betrayer.
body: Miss Hectarin's grown son, head of Everia's city guard, who jailed magic users for decades never knowing his mother was a witch. He betrays her to the witch-hunters (she's nearly burned at the stake) and, captured, refuses to turn — killed by Fharin, a grief Ophelia carries.

title: Unestra, Chained
teaser: The goddess is a prisoner inside Ophelia's own mind.
body: The truth behind the voice: Unestra is not merely advising Ophelia — she is chained to an obelisk within a field inside Ophelia's mind, able only to watch through a book, a prisoner who hid her own helplessness. Bound to Ophelia's body, she dies if Ophelia dies, and longs above all for a body and freedom of her own.

title: Ghvasta
teaser: Unestra's sister, a fragment sealed in the Xhasharian.
body: Unestra's goddess-sister, who in the old gods' last hour bound a piece of herself inside the Xhasharian to hide its most dangerous magic from humanity until the gods could return. That fragment awakens to speak with Ophelia and Unestra, carrying the memories of her creator.

title: Zuavaqua
teaser: Ewig's sister and closest confidant.
body: A dragon, Ewig's sister and closest confidant, who dwells in the west above the city of Pitiqua. Ophelia sends to her to find Ewig and rally the surviving dragons to the rebellion's final stand.

title: Doctor Troggle
teaser: A magician-doctor who heals with dragon's blood.
body: An Everia doctor secretly gifted with magic, who buys the freedom to practice by handing some patients to the mob — and once saved the emperor himself. He heals the dying Ophelia using an IV and dragon's blood after she nearly burns out on a goddess's magic.

title: Ramidion's Confession
teaser: The dragons' tragic side, and a chosen peace.
body: In the throne room Ramidion reveals the dragons' history: the gods, threatened, hunted them to near-extinction (only nine remain), turning humans against them with dragon-slaying contests until the dragons finally struck back. She ruled cruelly because warring humanity left no other path to peace. Confronted, she chooses to abdicate rather than fight on.

title: The New Republic
teaser: Peace instead of vengeance — the saga's resolution.
body: The saga's surprising end: rather than slaughter the last dragons and force the gods back, Gilda and Ophelia accept Ramidion's offer to convert the empire into a constitutional monarchy — a ceremonial crown over an elected parliament, every witch and cedar freed, the witch-hunters repurposed to help people, and the dragons helping build the new parliament. Vengeance set aside for a world that governs itself.

title: The Bridge to Obsidian Spindle
teaser: Wicked Minds ends by opening the next saga.
body: The final book closes not on Ophelia's world but by replaying the opening of the Obsidian Spindle Saga — Chelle strung up by monster hunters, Rose grinding through a night shift — a deliberate handoff threading Dragon Strife into the modern-day Obsidian story along the shared Cosmic Weave.

title: The Center
teaser: The Five's gated seat at the City's heart.
body: The largest, most secured complex in the City, ringed off and patrolled by guards who shoot petty offenders dead to 'keep the peace.' Home of the Five, the site of the Transference trials, and the only place from which the Bubble can be lowered. Cold, corrupt, and absolute.

title: Wind
teaser: One of the Five — the first to truly die.
body: An ancient member of the Five, weary of endless rebirth ('I can't wait for a new body'), aided by his sharp-tongued assistant Penelope. His murder in the Center — the first real death of one of the Five in memory — triggers the emergency Transference and cracks the myth of their immortality. His confiscated computer later yields the data that exposes them.

title: Earth
teaser: The Five's public face — and Althea's double.
body: A prominent member of the Five who announces Wind's death and the new Transference. Cold and image-obsessed, she becomes the regime's mouthpiece; after Althea wins Transference yet survives, Althea is forced to impersonate her in propaganda videos denying the rebels' exposé.

title: Time
teaser: A member of the Five who leads the march on the Bubble.
body: One of the Five who, in the end, leads a peaceful Gandhi-style protest march toward the Bubble — invoking a forgotten tradition of activists walking to confront oppressors — gathering supporters and cameras until even the military strongman Arrow dares not stop them.

title: Penelope
teaser: Wind's blunt aide, later accused of murder.
body: Wind's sardonic assistant, openly weary of life under the Bubble. Kind to Althea at the Center, she is arrested for a killing she likely didn't commit — one of the many lives ground up by the regime's machinery.

title: Cam & Henry
teaser: Althea's fellow conspirators at the Center.
body: Two friends Althea makes among the Transference candidates: Cam, a tiny, fierce girl loyal to the end, and Henry, an anxious, plan-loving hacker who breaks into the Five's systems to steal the data cell that proves their crimes. Henry is captured and beaten; both share Althea's turn from candidate to rebel.

title: Joan
teaser: A smuggled-out Inner Ring girl, killed for stealing food.
body: A girl born illegally in the First Ring, smuggled out and cast adrift through the rings by parents who feared the Five's wrath. She befriends Althea on the road back, only to be shot dead by guards for stealing a little food — the casual cruelty of the Inner Rings made personal.

title: Arrow
teaser: The military strongman holding the Center.
body: The hardline commander who controls the Center's army and vows the Bubble will be lowered only 'from my cold, dead hands.' The face of the regime's armed power as the rebellion converges, too wary of public opinion to slaughter peaceful marchers outright.

title: The Mutie Rebellion
teaser: The data-dumps exposing the Five's lie.
body: The underground movement — led from among the persecuted Muties — that steals and releases dump after dump of evidence proving the Five are criminals and, crucially, that the world outside the Bubble is safe: the people have been held hostage for the Five's gain. Althea's theft of Wind's data cell feeds it; the regime fights back by forcing her to denounce it on camera.

title: The Spike
teaser: The anti-corruption network with a flying base.
body: A clandestine organization that wages war on corrupt corporations and powerful villains through talented freelancers and volunteers. Obsessed with secrecy and anonymity (no real names), it operates from a cloaked, flight-capable building and is run by Dotty, with agents like Xree. It recruited Jammer and Skritch — and its tangled motives drive much of the betrayal around Jammer's vault.

title: Dotty
teaser: The true head of The Spike.
body: The secret leader of The Spike, responsible for its security and anonymity, who can read truth from voice modulation. She reveals herself to Skritch from behind a forcefield aboard the organization's flying headquarters.

title: Ballister & Node
teaser: Skritch's dwarf cousins who run the front shop.
body: Two dwarf cousins — burly Ballister and smaller, faster Node — who run the legitimate repair shop covering the family's hacking work, and who nicknamed Skritch 'Noodle' before she could speak. They smuggle her help and hack the enemy's drones in the climax.

title: Bull
teaser: A shapeshifting ork ally in the getaway crew.
body: A powerful ork ally who can take a stone-ork form strong enough to rip a phone booth from the ground and hurl it as a shield, fighting beside Skritch and Xree during the vault heist and escape.

title: Jammer's Vault
teaser: The secret everyone is willing to kill for.
body: The mysterious contents Jammer hid away — coveted by the police, The Spike, the power-broker Ihanma Chilaffa, and the megacorp Gensys alike. Skritch seizes it without knowing why it matters, and unraveling its secret drives her hunt.

title: Gensys
teaser: The interplanetary megacorp at the story's edges.
body: A vast interplanetary corporation — the target of Skritch's opening heist and the place the fleeing Xree runs to in the finale, the kind of power that would kill for the information in Jammer's vault.

title: The Old City & the Bunghole
teaser: Skritch's neon-noir cyberpunk turf.
body: The dense, dark cyberpunk sprawl Skritch works — from corporate towers laced with laser-grid security down through the lightless outskirts ('the Bunghole') to the ship graveyard that hides Jammer's base. A city of hover-cars, drones, corrupt police, and creatures of every kind, where humans hold the top rungs of power.

title: Combat Drones
teaser: The hovering guns Mouse fights behind.
body: Paired flying drones with chest-mounted laser cannons and a central red eye, the weapons Mouse relies on instead of fighting directly. They must pause to recharge — the weakness Skritch exploits — and her cousins later hack them to her side.

title: Changelings
teaser: Shapeshifters who wear any form.
body: Beings like Sadie who can reshape their bodies into any form at will, slipping past borders and guards and shrugging off weight — a thief's perfect gift, and the source of the book's title.

title: Ollie's Portals
teaser: Instant travel — but only in person.
body: Ollie's ability to open portals across great distances, with one catch that nearly gets Sadie killed: Ollie must be physically present to open one, so a stranded agent abroad is on her own.

title: The L.A. Magical Black Market
teaser: Where monsters trade weapons and charms.
body: The hidden underworld of Los Angeles where magical weapons, spells, and trinkets change hands among demons, orcs, elves, and dwarves behind illusion charms. The dagger's true hiding place, and the world the next book's narrator works as a 'facilitator.'

title: The Elkman (Benny)
teaser: An elk-headed demon crime-boss who hires Ollie.
body: A demon crime-lord (his people the 'Benny's') with an elk's head beneath his illusion, who hires Ollie and equips his orc-goblin-dwarf-elf troops with consecrated black-steel bullets forged in Hell. Coolly logical, he needles Ollie that she plays every side — having worked for him, the demons, and others at once.

title: The Firestarter (Aimee White)
teaser: A fire-mage who works every side by blood-pact.
body: A magic-warded fire-mage (Aimee White) who burns warehouses and works contracts for rival organizations at once — colliding with Ollie repeatedly before an uneasy alliance. She binds clients with blood-pacts (break it and you burn, soul and all) and leads Ollie toward a pentagram ritual to reach Hell.

title: Candy
teaser: A human survivor who learns monsters are real.
body: A traumatized human Ollie pulls from a massacre, forced to grasp that demons walk among us. Sheltered at Ginger's Diner, she becomes a reluctant, frightened helper in Ollie's hunt — held at arm's length with Ollie's trademark mix of tenderness and threat.

title: Ginger
teaser: The diner-keeper who shelters Ollie's strays.
body: The owner of Ginger's Diner, one of the few safe havens in the city, who takes in the lost souls Ollie brings her and asks no questions — a quiet fixed point in Ollie's dangerous world.

title: Anjelica (in Evil)
teaser: The demon antichrist hiding out, pulled into another world.
body: Continuing from Magic: Anjelica, a demon and one of many 'antichrists' whose blood could end the world (neutralized by Kimberly's potion), flees Los Angeles to tiny Bronard, Missouri to learn control and stay safe. From there she, Margaret-Regina, and Kimberly are drawn into the world of Onmiri, where she becomes a reluctant figure in the rebellion against King Ulthar.

title: Director Frente (Madam Fantasmo)
teaser: The compromised leader of the rebellion.
body: The leader of the rebellion against King Ulthar, who frees Anjelica and Margaret from execution and plans the final raid — but carries a dark past: she once fought FOR the king, helping conquer the very cities now resisting him, a betrayal that enrages Anjelica.

title: Lizzie (in Time)
teaser: The runaway fae fleeing a death-prophecy across timelines.
body: Now grown, Lizzie — the goth girl adopted by Junebug and Carl alongside Anjelica — is a part-fae fugitive who never settles, fleeing a prophecy that she must die in fire to save the world. When demons murder a fae mother, Becky, Lizzie risks everything to save her hunted 'prophecy girl' daughter, Veronica — even dying and bargaining with the Time Being (Talinda) to undo the child's death. The girl she saves is hidden in Overbrook and renamed Connie: she will grow up to stand beside Katrina through the Apocalypse and, in time, become the Devil herself.

title: Lizzie's Prophecy
teaser: 'Her death will save us all.'
body: The oracle's words that rule Lizzie's life: 'In the ashes of her past, she will rise, and her death will save us all.' She runs for a decade to outpace it, only for fire to take her childhood home and father regardless — proof that fate cannot simply be fled.

source.real: Prophecy — especially the Greek oracle, whose ambiguous pronouncements (as at Delphi) shape and doom those who hear them — is the mythic device of a foretold fate that the hearer cannot escape and often fulfills by trying to avoid. The word that rules a life.
source.weave: The Weave's Lizzie's Prophecy is the oracle's verse that governs her life ('in the ashes of her past, she will rise, and her death will save us all') — keeping the Greek oracular pattern: the cryptic prophecy that binds a hero to a fate she lives toward.

title: The Stopwatch & the Knife
teaser: The relics that bend time — and the prize Doretha wants.
body: A glowing stopwatch endowed with Loki's magic that lets its bearer move through time, paired with the recurring dagger — the same obsidian blade later named the Dagger of Obsolescence. Together they are what the villain Doretha engineers a hundred timelines to seize from Lizzie, the dagger being one of the five obsidian weapons forged to kill a god.

title: Loki
teaser: The trickster god aiding Doretha's con.
body: The trickster god who plays his part in Doretha's multi-timeline deception, endowing the stopwatch with his magic and handing over the relics — a small, perfectly-played role in the grand betrayal.

source.real: Loki is the Norse trickster — a shape-shifter of ambiguous loyalty, companion to the gods who repeatedly endangers and rescues them. His schemes drive many myths; he engineers the death of Balder, and at Ragnarök he turns fully against the gods, steering the ship of the dead against Asgard. Clever, treacherous, and indispensable in equal measure.
source.weave: The Weave casts him exactly to type — the trickster who endows the stopwatch with his magic and hands over the relics, a 'small, perfectly-played role in the grand betrayal.' Pure Loki: the helper whose help is always also a trap.

title: Lilith & Xavier
teaser: A demon matriarch and her surly son.
body: Lilith, a demon power who trades in favors and points Lizzie toward leads; and her son Xavier, a contemptuous demon holed up in a derelict Hollywood house, called in to repay one of his mother's countless debts.

title: Kimberly & Molly (in Heaven)
teaser: The monster-hunter and her wife working Earth's demon beat.
body: Kimberly, the dagger-wielding hunter, and her wife Molly (married the first day it was legal in San Francisco) track demons across Earth — picking the locks of reeking demon dens and chasing leads like the name 'Horace Carlson' — one of the four narrating threads that converge on the war in Heaven.

title: Lizzie (in Heaven)
