teaser: Dead and bored stiff in Cloud City — until she kills a demon.
body: Having died, Lizzie finds Heaven (Cloud City) mind-numbingly dull, its few residents drained of all interest. She passes time watching Earth through the clouds — until she discovers and kills a demon that infiltrated Heaven (with the recurring dagger), pulling her into the coming war and the quest to free God.

title: Anjelica (in Heaven)
teaser: Grown ruler of Forche, who storms Hell for her mother.
body: Twenty-five years on, Anjelica is a respected parliamentary leader of Forche in Onmiri, governing beside Queen Margaret. When the war erupts she descends into Hell to ransom her mother from Mephistopheles, wielding hard-won nerve, the Dagger of Obsolescence, and the terrifying power of the freed demon Araphael.

title: Ollie & Cliff (in Heaven)
teaser: Ollie works the docks with a chatty new hacker.
body: Ollie Oleander runs jobs through computerized shipping ports with Cliff, a cocky, fact-spouting hacker who fills the role her alien friend Phil once held — her thread in the converging war.

title: The Bar
teaser: Neutral ground for angels and demons in Scotland.
body: A Scottish house that became sacred neutral ground: two centuries ago a man accidentally summoned a demon while cooking, befriended him, and kept the peace with food and beer under one rule — no fighting. Angels and demons alike now pay respects there, a waystation for monsters passing through.

title: Araphael
teaser: A caged angel-demon of terrifying power.
body: An immensely powerful being kept imprisoned for good reason — he can turn attacking demons and angels to ash in an instant and collapse Hell's portals with a charred soul's blood. Freed during the war, he fights beside Anjelica, revealing exactly why the world wanted him contained. (Distinct from the demon Araphel of Anjelica's dreams.)

title: The War in Heaven
teaser: A desperate assault to free a captured God.
body: The climactic conflict: an enemy seizes God on a guarded platform in Heaven, and a dwindling band — Michael, archangels Saphiel and Ircheal, Earth-warrior angels, Agent Davis, and Lizzie — mounts a suicidal assault, a full frontal charge to mask a small team infiltrating to free God, while demons and angels also tear open portals to invade Earth.

source.real: The War in Heaven of Revelation 12 is the cosmic battle in which Michael and his angels fight the dragon (Satan) and his angels, casting them out of Heaven to the earth. The archetypal celestial civil war between the loyal and rebel hosts.
source.weave: The Weave's War in Heaven has an enemy seize God on a guarded platform while a dwindling band — Michael, the archangels, Earth-warrior angels — fight to free Him — keeping Revelation's Michael-led battle for Heaven and raising the stakes to the capture of God Himself.
source.excerpt_ref: Michael and the dragon war in heaven

title: God (captured)
teaser: The deity held hostage at the war's center.
body: The God of this cosmology, seized and pinned on a heavily-guarded platform in Heaven — the prize the war is fought over, whose freeing (it's believed) is worth any number of angelic lives.

title: Saphiel & Ircheal
teaser: The archangels leading the charge.
body: Two archangels among Michael's dwindling squad in the war for God — grimly resigned that even total annihilation is worth the chance that one survivor frees God, since the slain are vaporized from existence entirely.

title: Atka
teaser: Anjelica's ally who holds a blade to a demon lord.
body: A fierce companion of Anjelica's in the descent into Hell, who presses the Dagger of Obsolescence to Mephistopheles's throat to force the release of Anjelica's mother and Araphael — a doubted ally who proves a true friend.

title: Gabriel
teaser: The angel Lizzie turns to in Heaven.
body: An angel Lizzie seeks out for guidance after killing the infiltrating demon in Heaven — a steady figure in the bureaucracy of Cloud City as the war approaches.

source.real: Gabriel, the archangel of revelation and announcement — messenger of Heaven's word in the Hebrew Bible, Gospels, and (as Jibril) the Qur'an.
source.weave: The Weave keeps Gabriel as a steady figure in Heaven's bureaucracy whom Lizzie seeks for guidance as war approaches — the messenger-archangel preserved as a counselor within the celestial order.

title: The Rapture & Apocalypse
teaser: The world after God called the worthy home.
body: The cataclysm that frames Katrina's origin: a literal Rapture took the worthy to Heaven, then demons, ghosts, minotaurs, three-headed dogs, and hydras overran the Earth. Survivors live in 'Black Zones' without power, crushed by the knowledge that God judged them unworthy — many break, knowing Hell likely awaits.

source.real: The Rapture is the Christian end-times belief (drawn from 1 Thessalonians 4 and Revelation) that the faithful will be caught up to meet Christ, leaving the rest to the tribulation. The dividing of the saved from the world at the end of days.
source.weave: The Weave's Rapture & Apocalypse has a literal Rapture take the worthy to Heaven, then looses demons, ghosts, and monsters on those left — keeping the Rapture's exact mechanism (faithful taken up, the rest abandoned to horror) as the cataclysm framing Katrina's origin.

title: Bacchus (God / Yahweh)
teaser: The lazy regent-god who ruled — and ruined — Earth.
body: Revealed truth of the cosmology: 'God' (Yahweh, Jehovah) is really Bacchus, a sluggish god assigned by Zeus as Earth's regent. Gods number in the millions across the universe, each leaving one regent per habitable planet — and Bacchus botched Earth so badly that Katrina ends up replacing the divine order.

source.real: Bacchus/Dionysus is the Greco-Roman god of wine and ecstatic release. In the Weave's cosmology his ordinary mythic dissipation is repurposed for a reveal.
source.weave: The Weave's key cosmological twist: the figure humanity calls 'God' (Yahweh, Jehovah) is really Bacchus, a sluggish wine-god assigned by Zeus as Earth's regent among millions of gods across the universe. It literalizes the series thesis — every tradition's gods are real — by making the monotheistic God just one minor deity in a vast pantheon-politics.

title: Lucifer (in Death)
teaser: The old Devil, now Katrina's rueful companion.
body: The former Devil who mourns the relics Katrina destroys (like Bacchus's ageless flaming sword), standing beside her and Dennis as she grows into the role — part of the chain of tricked Devils the series traces.

source.real: Lucifer, the fallen morning-star and former lord of Hell.
source.weave: In the Death thread the former Devil mourns the relics being destroyed and stands beside the new Devil as she grows into the role — the deposed adversary as elegiac elder, another thread-face of the same figure.

title: Hercules
teaser: The demigod smith who can mend god-relics.
body: A figure able to repair even the ancient armor and Bacchus's flaming sword that Katrina wrecks — lending muscle and craft to her cause as she comes into divine power.

source.real: Heracles (Roman Hercules) is the greatest of Greek heroes — son of Zeus, of superhuman strength, famed for completing the Twelve Labors as penance. The archetype of brawn harnessed to hard, redemptive work; strength as both burden and gift.
source.weave: The Weave's Hercules repairs even the ancient armor and Bacchus's flaming sword that Katrina wrecks, lending muscle and craft to her cause — keeping the strongman essence and turning his legendary might toward the forge.

title: Katrina Becomes the Devil
teaser: A mortal survivor's path to godhood.
body: The arc of Death: Katrina, a foul-mouthed survivor who simply refuses to die, claws through the Apocalypse and a war among gods to become the Devil herself — ruling for ten thousand years — the pivotal step in the series' chain of tricked Devils and her road toward becoming the new Chaos.

title: Tress
teaser: The Godschurch leader who died at the Obelisk.
body: Rebecca's predecessor as head of the Godschurch, killed when the base exploded and 90% of the agency's agents died at the Battle of the Obelisk — the catastrophe that thrust the reluctant Rebecca into command.

title: Meret & Osiris
teaser: Gods who sit on the Godschurch's councils.
body: Two of the many gods Rebecca must answer to in her endless meetings as Godschurch director — a reminder that the agency serves and is hemmed in by gods from across the universe.

source.real: Meret (also spelled Mert) is an Egyptian goddess strongly associated with rejoicing — with singing, dancing, and the joyful music of celebration and offering. She personifies the gladness given to the gods through music and rite. (She is paired here with Osiris, the Egyptian god of the dead and resurrection.)
source.weave: The Weave lists Meret and Osiris among the many gods Rebecca answers to as Godschurch director — a reminder the agency is hemmed in by deities from across the underworlds. It keeps Meret as a genuine, if minor, Egyptian goddess of joyful rite, alongside the major Osiris.
source.work: Egyptian tradition / Book of the Dead

title: Fezzick
teaser: A captured Godless agent who won't talk.
body: One of the many Godless prisoners Rebecca interrogates — gleefully unhelpful even when beaten. Like most of his faction, he blames the gods for a hard life rather than take responsibility, the recruiting logic of the Godless laid bare.

title: Queen Aine
teaser: The Unseelie fairy queen who plays every side.
body: The Unseelie fairy queen who seized Oz, now reduced to a captive-spy of the nightmare god Epiales and then a refugee queen. When the Dream Realm falls, she leads the survivors of Oz and the Mountain People across the Rainbow Bridge into the Obsidian Spindle, sheltering among the Fates — 'queen of nothing,' and queen of them all.

title: Muirgen
teaser: Aine's guard captain — trickster teleporter.
body: The new captain of Queen Aine's guard, a teleporting Unseelie fairy who 'betrays' Chelle to Hera — actually smuggling her into Hera's castle to find the golden book, per Aine's secret plan. Insolent, distrusted, and central to the scheme to reopen the Obsidian Spindle.

source.real: Muirgen ('born of the sea') is the name given in Irish legend to Lí Ban — a woman transformed into a mermaid/salmon who lived beneath the waves for centuries before being caught, baptized, and revered as a saint. A genuine Irish sea-transformation legend.
source.weave: The Weave's Muirgen is a teleporting Unseelie fairy, captain of Queen Aine's guard, whose 'betrayal' is a smuggling-ploy — borrowing the authentic Irish sea-name for a fae of shifting loyalties.

title: Hera
teaser: The shadow-goddess of Urgu who cursed the gorgons.
body: One of the Six gods of Urgu, ruler of the lightless Dark Domain — she moves in shadow, shows only her purple eyes, and regards humanity across countless planets with contempt. Imprisoned in the Dream Realm by Zeus for her mischief, she is the goddess who cursed the gorgons into monstrous form (the source of Chelle's lineage and grief). After Hypnos vanished she rose to dominance, ruling Urgu and serving as Nimue's divine patron until she revokes her blessing.

title: Boudica
teaser: Queen of the Mountain People fleeing the dark.
body: Fierce, neon-eyed queen of the Mountain People — refugees driven from Agrona's Mountains by an unspeakable 'them' over the last decade. She captures the powerless Nimue and trades her for her people's safe passage, and is an old wilderness mentor of Red's.

source.real: Boudica was a REAL historical queen of the Iceni — who in 60–61 AD led a massive revolt against the Roman occupation of Britain, burning Camulodunum, Londinium, and Verulamium before her defeat. Recorded by Tacitus and Cassius Dio, she became a lasting symbol of resistance against empire.
source.weave: The Weave's Boudica is the 'fierce, neon-eyed queen of the Mountain People,' refugees driven from their land — carrying the real Iceni queen's essence (a warrior-queen leading a displaced people against an overwhelming oppressor) into Urgu, paired with her bound Djinn.
source.work: Tacitus, Annals / Cassius Dio, Roman History

crosslinks.summary: Boudica (real history) stands among myth: the Iceni queen bound to a Middle-Eastern Djinn, walking the same Sandlands as Aladdin — history and folklore interlocked.

interactions.note: Her bound Djinn (Arabian/Islamic) — a real historical queen given a Nights-style genie.
She crosses paths with Aladdin (1001 Nights) in Sekhmet's Sandlands — history meeting Arabian folklore.
Both move through Sekhmet's (Egyptian) Sandlands — the real, the Arabian, and the Egyptian sharing one ground.

title: The Mountain People & Agrona's Mountains
teaser: Refugees fleeing a darkness in the peaks.
body: A brightly-colored nomadic folk with rudimentary magic, driven from Agrona's Mountains by shadow-things they will only call 'them,' massing as refugees at the Gates of Droangor. Their flight is the first sign of the rising threat that even the gods fear.

title: Agrona
teaser: The dread goddess in the highest mountain.
body: One of the Six, dwelling in a living, fleshy castle atop the highest mountain amid endless lightning and sulfur, where massive beasts descend and even the gods are unprepared. The Fates hint Agrona holds the key to returning to Earth — drawing Nimue to her in the epilogue.

title: The Shadow Demons
teaser: Yellow-eyed things spilling out of the mountains.
body: Swarms of black, long-armed, yellow-eyed demons that strike from darkness and are repelled only by light and Hypnos's warded wall — Hera's hunters and a symptom of the larger darkness rising from Agrona's Mountains.

title: The Golden Book
teaser: Blank to most eyes — the key to the Spindle.
body: A weightless golden tome stolen from Hera's library, its pages blank to nearly everyone. Only the Hypnos-blessed Rose can read it, transcribing the exact spell that forces open the Obsidian Spindle — the prize Chelle risks everything for, and Nimue's true goal.

title: The Gates of Droangor
teaser: The only breach in Hypnos's great wall.
body: The three-hundred-foot red gates and rune-carved Wall of Itherium that Hypnos raised to seal Oz from the warring gods' domains — the sole sanctioned crossing into Hera's Dark Domain, guarded by a battalion and unbreached for two thousand years.

title: Edwina
teaser: The official who crowns Rose — then kills her.
body: A trusted member of the small council who completes Rose's coronation and then stabs her in the back, dusting Rose's soul — an assassination that opens the throne for Queen Aine and shatters Chelle's world.

title: Chelle Becomes a Fate
teaser: Trapped in the Spindle, sewing the Quilt of Life.
body: The cost of the bargain: Chelle ends Book 2 imprisoned in the Obsidian Spindle by the gorgon Fates, made to sew the Quilt of Life alongside Clotho and Lachesis — the origin of her becoming one of the three Fates seen in Eternity. She pounds the sealed door in vain, clutching Rose's urn.

source.real: The Moirai — Clotho, Lachesis, Atropos — spin, measure, and cut the thread of every life; their loom is the mechanism of destiny itself in Greek myth.
source.weave: Chelle is bound to sew the Quilt of Life alongside Clotho and Lachesis, becoming one of the Fates — the Weave literalizing the thread-of-life metaphor as a quilt, and writing a mortal's induction into the Greek loom of destiny.

title: Rose, Hollowed
teaser: Back on Earth alive — and feeling nothing.
body: Rose's soul is returned to Earth and her body, but damaged: she feels no pain, no joy, nothing at all, her eyes dull and veined red. She moves back with her parents and goes through the motions of a life she watches like a stranger — the wound that shapes her later road to Queen of Oz and the Cosmic Weave.

title: The Heart of Urgu
teaser: The dead orb at the world's center that must beat again.
body: A vast gray, deathlike orb at the very center of Urgu, ringed by living pink dreams — the engine that lets human Dreamers enter the Dream Realm. It stalled when Hypnos vanished, stranding souls and weakening the Barrier. Only a Fate with a body can restart it; Chelle pours her own life-memory into it to make it beat again.

title: Anansi (Isiah / Kofi)
teaser: The spider-god storyteller of the Mistreach.
body: One of the Six, the trickster spider-god who rules the Mistreach — a fog of madness he wraps around his realm to be left alone. He hides among his people as the gentle innkeeper Isiah (true name Kofi), measuring others by how they treat the small. Aine petitions him for aid, and he agrees to leave his exile to help save the Dream Realm.

source.real: Anansi is the spider-trickster of Akan (Ghanaian) tradition, carried across the Atlantic into Caribbean and African-American folklore. Small and weak but endlessly cunning, he outwits the powerful through wit and words; in one famous tale he wins ownership of all stories from the sky-god Nyame. He is the triumph of cleverness over strength, the keeper of tales.
source.weave: The Weave gives Anansi a human guise (Isiah / Kofi) — keeping the spider-trickster's essence: the cunning underdog who wins by wit. (The name Kofi is itself an Akan day-name, a nod to his Ghanaian origin.)

title: The Mistreach
teaser: Anansi's realm of fog and quiet madness.
body: The most secretive land of Urgu: endless grass and fog that drives intruders into insane, chattering wrecks. Its people want only to be left alone, making it the poorest realm — and the hardest to find, even for a queen.

title: Sekhmet
teaser: The lion-headed war-goddess of the Sandlands.
body: One of the Six, a human-bodied, lion-headed goddess who rules the sun-blasted Sandlands and personally leads her vast, prejudice-free army at the front against the Nightmare Realm's invasion — fighting a hundred days without rest, tearing through monsters in golden streaks.

source.real: Sekhmet is the lioness-headed Egyptian goddess of war, plague, and healing — 'the Powerful One,' the Eye of Ra. Born of Ra's fire to punish humanity, she fell into a blood-drunk slaughter so total that Ra had to flood the land with red-dyed beer to trick her into stopping. She is destruction and cure in one: the fierce protector of pharaohs whose breath was the desert's killing heat. (Her unstoppable battle-rage closely parallels the Hindu Kali's — a noted cross-tradition echo.)
source.weave: The Weave keeps her lion-headed and martial — one of the Six, who leads a 'prejudice-free army' against the Nightmare forces from the sun-blasted Sandlands — carrying the myth's solar fury and protector role into a frontline war-goddess.
source.work: The Book of the Heavenly Cow / Book of the Dead

title: The Sandlands
teaser: Sekhmet's endless burning desert of dream.
body: The vast desert realm of the sun-goddess Sekhmet, crossed on sand-salamanders and sailing-ships over shifting dunes, where the sun never sets. Home to tent-cities, the Cave of Wonder, and the war-front where Sekhmet's golden army holds back the dark.

title: Aladdin
teaser: The immortal thief of the dunes.
body: A perennially cheerful, impossibly old thief roaming Sekhmet's Sandlands, pinching trinkets from everyone (and, he claims, returning them with interest). He guides Red and Boudica toward the Cave of Wonder, insisting the desert's punishing heat is only a dream you can choose not to feel.

source.tradition: Middle Eastern (One Thousand and One Nights)
source.real: Aladdin is the hero of one of the most famous tales associated with the One Thousand and One Nights — a poor young thief who gains a magic lamp and the djinn within it, winning fortune by wit and luck. The archetypal charming trickster-thief of Arabian-Nights tradition.
source.weave: The Weave's Aladdin is a 'perennially cheerful, impossibly old thief' roaming Sekhmet's Sandlands, pinching trinkets and guiding heroes to the Cave of Wonder — keeping the lovable-thief essence and the Nights' iconography (the desert, the cave of wonders, the djinn nearby in Boudica's arc).
source.work: One Thousand and One Nights (Burton tr.)

title: The Cave of Wonder
teaser: The sealed cave beyond the war-front.
body: A guarded cave in the Sandlands, its entrance blocked and watched, lying behind the Nightmare Realm's battle lines — the goal of Red's desert crossing in his hunt for a way to restore Hypnos.

title: Esther
teaser: The Nightmare-Realm gorgon who befriends Nimue.
body: A gorgon who survives the Nightmare Realm by saving trapped Dreamers, and who becomes Nimue's first true friend in a thousand years — disguising and protecting her on the road to Epiales. The friendship is built on a hidden truth: Esther is the mother of the very girl Nimue once tried to kill. When she learns it, she demands a fight Nimue refuses to give.

title: Nefeski
teaser: The cruelest beast of the Schrylands.
body: A monstrous web-spinner of the Nightmare Realm's Schrylands who snares Dreamers and keeps them alive for months before devouring them — the trial by which Esther tests whether Nimue can be trusted.

title: Gwen
teaser: The waitress who calls Rose a 'Quest Girl.'
body: The Sword-Wielder — the lone ordinary human among the heroes, which is exactly her courage. She plans to lift the whole Abyss up through the clouds, beats the Lich King at his own card game to steer Lucy through the tomb-maze, builds a settled Seelie-Unseelie community with Elioti, and stands against Nimue in the final battle though she has no power of her own.

title: Quest Girls
teaser: The name Gwen gives Rose's reluctant adventuring.
body: The motif Gwen names aloud — ordinary girls swept into magical errands across worlds. Rose bristles at being called a 'quest girl,' insisting she's just delivering a package, but the label sticks: good girls who follow orders, or bad ones who choose the quest anyway.

title: Erebus
teaser: Hypnos's father — a primordial with the cosmos in his eyes.
body: The primordial father of Hypnos and Epiales (Nox's mate), living quietly on Earth with the universe swirling in his pupils. He keeps no relic to give, only a reminder: that Epiales was once a gentle child who saved birds and wouldn't step on ants, before he became the god of nightmares.

title: The Six Doors
teaser: Nox's gateways between Earth and the Dream Realm.
body: Six doors Nox created eons ago to find her son Hypnos wherever he roamed — the only crossings between Earth and Urgu, each guarded (the Philadelphia door by Mydnyte). One is found destroyed, the work of Erebus.

title: Gyda
teaser: The fearless tree-dwelling mapmaker of the dark mountains.
body: A solitary hermit who, alone among the people of Urgu, built a permanent home high in the trees of Agrona's lightless Mountain Realm. Fearless, agile, and a meticulous mapmaker of everywhere she's traveled, she guides Red toward a way through the Wall of Itherium.

title: The Cheshire Cat
teaser: The invisible cat who guides Red.
body: A grinning cat able to turn invisible (though not the rope tying him to Red), who leads her through the monster-choked Mountain Realm toward the sea — a wary, sardonic companion in the dark.

title: Ariel, the Drowned Princess
teaser: The would-be queen who drowned, now a mermaid.
body: The Drowned Princess. Chosen as the Spore's intended sacrifice (a conduit through Hypnos to breach the barrier), she refuses a meaningless death: she retrieves the sword Hope Bringer from Nox's vault and, even as the ritual disintegrates her, reaches the throne to save the Dream Realm. She does not die a victim — she ascends, becoming a god of Urgu, the seed planted eight books earlier paying off in full.

title: Eyo
teaser: The merman who fetches Red to the deep.
body: A green-skinned, fanged merman who retrieves Red beneath the sea (where Urgu's mind-construction lets her breathe and speak) and brings her to the drowned princess, on Anansi's word that she was coming.

title: Nimue as Bernadette
teaser: The witch wears a dead Dreamer's body on Earth.
body: Etsop's plan realized: Nimue's soul is locked into the body of Bernadette, a dead Dreamer, letting her finally walk on Earth (with glasses to correct the borrowed eyes). She revels in food, blood, and sensation — and hides that she was ever the Wicked Witch.

title: Thanatos
teaser: The keeper of the fake-Parthenon labyrinth.
body: A death-god shopkeeper guarding a labyrinth beneath a gaudy fake Parthenon, where a statue holds a 'key to imagination' (a door to the Dream Realm). Nimue and Gwen find the maze long-neglected, its minotaur dead and the key already stolen — months before, by a break-in.

title: Boudica's Djinn
teaser: A god-strong genie bound to three wishes.
body: A Djinn — the only power in Urgu as strong as a god — freed by and bound to Boudica until she spends her final wish. Sardonic about her 'poor' wishes, it fights at her side as the Dream Realm falls.

source.real: A djinn (genie) is a spirit of Arabian and Islamic tradition — made of smokeless fire, predating humankind, capable of great power and of granting wishes when bound. In the One Thousand and One Nights, the djinn of lamp and ring grant wishes to whoever holds the vessel.
source.weave: The Weave's Djinn is 'the only power in Urgu as strong as a god,' freed by and bound to Boudica until her final wish — keeping the genuine wish-bond of the Nights' djinn and its fire-born might, sardonic about its mistress's 'poor' wishes.
source.work: One Thousand and One Nights / Islamic tradition

title: Atropos
teaser: The third Fate of the Obsidian Spindle.
body: The third of the gorgon Fates who weave at the heart of the Obsidian Spindle, alongside Clotho and Lachesis — the one who cuts the thread. Named at last when the refugees shelter in the Spindle.

source.real: Atropos ('the inflexible') is the eldest of the three Moirai (Fates) — the one who cuts the thread of life, deciding the manner and moment of each death, alongside Clotho (who spins) and Lachesis (who measures). The Fate even the gods cannot overrule.
source.weave: The Weave's Atropos is the third of the gorgon-Fates weaving at the heart of the Obsidian Spindle, 'the one who cuts the thread,' with Clotho and Lachesis — keeping the exact Greek division of labor (spin/measure/cut) and the Fates' supremacy, reimagined as gorgons weaving the Quilt of Life.

title: Loki's Temple
teaser: The bog-temple Epiales rules from.
body: The trickster Loki's old temple in a misty, stench-ridden bog, its black throne now Epiales's seat. Loki, who feigned loyalty hoping Hypnos would never return, is imprisoned in its back cells alongside other captives.

title: The Top-Hat Man
teaser: The shabby gambler who consoles Rose.
body: A stained-velvet, top-hatted figure at the Reno casino who finds the grieving Rose on the balcony after she gambles away her stake, offering a 'cheer up, little pup' and a wry, knowing kindness — a mysterious presence in the magical poker world.

title: The Underworld & the Consolidation
teaser: Hell, recently renovated — and run on slave labor.
body: The vast Underworld: lush and green as much as fiery, ruled from Dis by Persephone and Hades, who use monsters as unpaid slaves to keep it running (Chelle works the Limbo Carnival). A recent overhaul called 'the Consolidation' reshaped it; beyond the Great Divide lie the cold realms — Helheim, Tounela, Ashanti — and their gods.

crosslinks.summary: The Consolidation is the Weave's thesis made literal: every tradition's land of the dead — Greek (Hades/Persephone), Norse (Hel), Egyptian (Isis/Osiris), Celtic, Hindu — merged into one realm ruled from Dante's Dis, with Heaven's later occupation layered on top.

interactions.note: Splits the merged underworld hot-from-cold — its internal border.
Ruled from Dis (Dante/Roman) — the hell-city as the merged capital.
Includes Mag Mell (Irish), Duat (Egyptian), Helheim (Norse) — all traditions under one administration.
Persephone and Hades (Greek) rule from Dis — Greek royalty over the consolidated dead.

source.real: Every tradition has its land of the dead — Greek Hades, Norse Hel, Egyptian Duat, Celtic Mag Mell, and more. Comparative myth treats these as parallel underworlds; the Weave unites them into one administered realm.
source.weave: The Weave's Underworld Consolidation rules all these lands of the dead from Dis under Persephone and Hades, monsters worked as unpaid labor — the literal merger of every tradition's underworld into one bureaucratic realm, the series thesis applied to the afterlife.

title: The Limbo Carnival
teaser: Where the unbaptized children pass eternity.
body: A carnival in Limbo staffed by enslaved monsters, where the souls of unbaptized or impure children — neither joyful nor pained — wait for a chance at reincarnation. Chelle works a rigged ball-toss booth here, quietly giving the one prize away to brighten a child's day.

title: Fawke & the Resistance
teaser: 'There is a better way' — the rebellion in Hell.
body: An underground resistance against Persephone's regime, fronted by the codenamed Fawke (with Sisyphus, and the rescued Prometheus building devices). They recruit Chelle, extract prisoners from the pits, and bomb the Imperial Palace — making Chelle a wanted fugitive.

title: Sisyphus & Prometheus
teaser: The damned legends of Fawke's cell.
body: Two figures of the resistance: gruff Sisyphus, who leads rescue runs into the pits and refuses to learn the names of the likely-doomed; and Prometheus, freed from the pits to build the rebellion's devices. Mythic punishments turned revolutionaries.

title: Legba
teaser: Rose's all-access guide through Hell.
body: A guide with an all-access pass to anywhere in the Underworld who escorts Rose from the Styx ferry through Central Processing toward Persephone — advising her to address the queen, not Hades, and to mind her decorum. He maps Hell's geography, including the cold realms beyond the Great Divide.

source.real: Papa Legba is the loa of the crossroads — the gatekeeper between the human and spirit worlds, who must be honored at the start of every Vodou ceremony before any other spirit can be reached. Depicted as a stooped old man with a cane, straw hat, and pipe, he speaks all human languages and gives or denies permission to cross over. Nothing in the spirit world happens without his leave.
source.weave: The Weave's Legba is exactly the gatekeeper — a guide with an all-access pass to anywhere in the Underworld, who advises Rose to address the queen with proper decorum and maps Hell's geography. It keeps his essential role: the one you must honor first, who opens the way.

title: Hypnos's Coin
teaser: The passage-token into and through Hell.
body: A coin Hypnos gives Rose that grants passage into the realms of her choosing — entry to Limbo, then to Dis, and an audience with Persephone. More powerful than he let on, and tangled in the feud between Nox and Hel.

source.real: Hypnos is the Greek personification of sleep — gentle son of Night (Nyx), twin of Death (Thanatos), who can lull even Zeus. His touch brings the sleep that mortals and gods cannot resist.
source.weave: Hypnos's Coin is the sleep-god's object in the Weave — carrying the Greek god of sleep's power into a relic. (Hypnos himself, son of Nyx, is woven through the Obsidian Spindle thread as the builder of Oz.)

title: Tom
teaser: The prim, lilac-scented giver of the golden knife.
body: A fastidious, lilac-smelling, oddly old gentleman who befriends Red on Earth, treats her to pizza with absurd table manners, and gives her a golden knife she carries into the Underworld — a small, courtly mystery at the edge of the story.

title: Brad
teaser: Gwen's cured boyfriend, chafing at her control.
body: Gwen's boyfriend, cured by Hypnos of the madness that institutionalized him, now confined 'for his safety' — tracked by an enchanted watch and watched by Nimue (with whom he's secretly sleeping). He rebels, demanding the right to choose his own life, and slips away on a quest of his own.

title: Ferrigold
teaser: The fairy recruiter who owns the diner.
body: A fairy who reveals that the fae secretly own King Arthur's Court — and hundreds of businesses worldwide — hiding in plain sight and exploiting cheap human labor. He comes to recruit a hero and is kidnapped, wounded, by a desperate Gwen.

title: The Sword in the Stone
teaser: The diner relic that names the Sword-Wielder.
body: A 'poor replica' of the Sword in the Stone mounted in King Arthur's Court — in truth the mark of the chosen Sword-Wielder. The fae's interest in Gwen's diner centers on it, and on the hero destined to draw it.

source.real: The Sword in the Stone is the test of true kingship in Arthurian legend — only the rightful king can draw the blade from the stone (or anvil), proving Arthur's claim to the throne of Britain. The archetype of the destined hero revealed by a sword no one else can move.
source.weave: The Weave's Sword in the Stone is a 'poor replica' in King Arthur's Court that is secretly the mark of the chosen Sword-Wielder — keeping the legend's core (the blade that identifies the destined hero) and hanging a prophecy on it.

title: Regent Tholish Flit & Queen Zabasha
teaser: The Snow Queen — cruelest being in all of Hell.
body: The Snow Queen — the cruelest, most powerful being Persephone has ever known, who once took a legion of angels and two dozen gods to bring down and imprison. A thousand years of torture honed her into a force of pure vengeance. Freed through Nimue's unwitting quest, she murders Epiales and steals his power, then unleashes the Great Divide to consume the Underworld.

title: The Daemon
teaser: A smoke-being (not a demon) guiding Nimue.
body: A smoke-bodied daemon — emphatically distinct from a demon — visible only to Nimue, who drinks bourbon by absorbing it and leads her through a blue door into the fairy realm of Symvarah to fulfill Bernadette's destiny. Prone to pop-culture references Nimue can't parse.

title: Symvarah & the Four Courts
teaser: The fairy homeland of the Abyss.
body: Symvarah ('of the air'), the seat of fae power below the cloud-cover Abyss, governed by four courts: Summer and Spring (Seelie — light, order, justice) against Autumn and Winter (Unseelie — chaos). Reached by riding the insectoid 'Flies'; most outsiders who enter go mad. Home of King Loosha's Summer Court.

title: King Loosha
teaser: Summer Court king who names Nimue the Chosen.
body: Ruler of the radiant golden Summer Court of Symvarah, who hails Bernadette/Nimue as the returned Chosen champion and sets her quest: slay the Winter Court's champion — by guile, not open murder, lest it spark all-out fae war.

title: Hel & the Cold Realms
teaser: The unseen goddess of the frozen Underworld.
body: The reclusive goddess of the frozen realms beyond the Great Divide (Ashanti, Nilfheim), unseen for three hundred years, who hates Nox. Red braves the endless blizzard toward her — into the trap where Epiales waits.

source.real: Hel is the Norse goddess who rules the realm of the dead that bears her name (Helheim) — a daughter of Loki, described as half living-woman and half corpse. She receives those who die of sickness or old age, rather than the battle-slain who go to Valhalla. Her cold, dim realm is the Norse counterpart to the warm classical underworld.
source.weave: The Weave seats her over the 'frozen side' of a unified underworld, across the Great Divide from the fiery classical realms — making the myth's distinction (Hel's cold dead vs. the warm lands of the dead) into literal geography where pantheons' afterlives border one another.

title: The Great Divide
teaser: The storm-wall splitting Hell — now unleashed.
body: An endless storm of crackling black smoke and lightning where the hot side of the Underworld (Dis, Patala, Duat, Mag Mell, Limbo) meets the frozen side ruled by Hel and Amokye (Ashanti, Nilfheim). Long contained to a three-mile crack, it is loosed when Zabasha kills Epiales and steals the magic that held it — and begins devouring cities whole.

crosslinks.summary: The underworld's internal border: the HOT side (Dis/Roman, Patala/Hindu, Duat/Egyptian, Mag Mell/Irish, Limbo) meets the FROZEN side (Helheim/Norse, Niflheim, Ashanti realms) — every tradition's land of the dead split by temperature. The warm-vs-cold afterlife motif made one geography.

interactions.note: Frozen side — the Norse Hel's realm.
Hot side — the Irish delightful plain.
Hot side — the Egyptian Duat.
Hot side — the Roman/Dante city of Dis.

source.real: Many traditions split the afterlife into a warm/blessed region and a cold/grim one — Greek Elysium vs. the shades, Norse Valhalla vs. Hel's cold realm. The Weave literalizes this universal division as a single border between all the underworlds.
source.weave: The Weave's Great Divide is the storm-border where the HOT side (Dis, Patala, Duat, Mag Mell, Limbo) meets the FROZEN side (Hel, Amokye/Ashanti, Niflheim) — a cross-pantheon map that fuses every tradition's land of the dead into one geography split by temperature. The series thesis rendered as cartography.

title: Regent Tholish Flit
teaser: The Winter Court regent who cons Nimue.
body: The sweet-toothed, iron-warded regent of the fairy Winter Court (acting for Queen Zabasha), who exposes King Loosha's cruelty to win Nimue's sympathy and sends her to destroy seven binding stones on Earth — the very act that frees the Snow Queen. A spymaster who feeds the Summer king false intelligence.

title: The Seven Binding Stones
teaser: Earth-hidden stones that cage Zabasha.
body: Seven ancient stones scattered in secret, riddle-guarded places across Earth (a Rockies cave, the Met in New York, and more) whose destruction unbinds the imprisoned Queen Zabasha. Nimue hunts them down one by one, not grasping until late what their breaking will release.

title: Txizle & the Unseelie Tribe
teaser: The dark-fairy tribe that heals Gwen.
body: Leader of a peaceful Unseelie tribe living for generations in a glade of the Abyss they call Shangri-la — hunters, farmers, doctors, and children who heal Gwen with pixie dust. Their harmony is destroyed when Seelie raiders (the Priot), disguised as refugees, are led back to camp.

title: Lucy
teaser: Gwen's glamorous friend, crippled in the Abyss.
body: The Dragon Warrior, bonded to Farzinium and able to soar the Abyss (though paralyzed without the dragon's strength flowing through her). She unites the Unseelie clans, braves the Lich King's tomb-maze for Queen Agnostia's amulet, and fights at the Battle of the Obsidian Spindle — confronting Nimue over what the witch did to her.

title: Amokye
teaser: The founding goddess of the cold ferry-towns.
body: The mother goddess who founded Ashanti to welcome the dead across the Great Divide, unseen by her faithful for ages. She dines with Epiales in Nilfheim and fights to end the eternal winter, promising to return to her people once she does.

title: The Ambassadors' Conspiracy
teaser: The secret rebellion of the city-states.
body: A clandestine network of Underworld ambassadors (led by L'ir'il of Patala) plotting against Persephone's regime from a hidden Parliament chamber — who try to make Rose the face of their cause, unaware she's reporting every word back to the Empress.

title: Farzinium the Dragon
teaser: The dragon who created — and would destroy — the Abyss.
body: An immense dragon sealed in the lava of the Blunt Mountain volcano by King Loosha's ancestors. It came through a tear in spacetime and is said to have created the fairy Abyss; freed by Lucy, it vows to destroy the Abyss and the cloud-cover oppression. It chose a mortal rider because its keep was warded specifically against the Unseelie.

title: Qrovil
teaser: The gentle giant elf who carries Lucy.
body: A big, kind Unseelie elf — too large to be a hunter, so he trains the young — who carries the crippled Lucy on his back across the Abyss to rally the scattered tribes, fending off attackers and slowly falling in love with her. Steady, self-deprecating, and brave.

title: Marzelle & Jhinita
teaser: Keepers of the Dragon Warrior line.
body: Leaders of surviving Unseelie tribes (Jhinita's camp 'Inatu' — 'gone'). Marzelle holds the ancestral title of Dragon Warrior and the dragon amulet her great-grandmother died stealing back from the Summer Court, guiding Lucy to the Blunt Mountain to wake Farzinium.

title: Hahyah
teaser: The story-hungry demon giant of the cold peaks.
body: A colossal demon who keeps a tiny captive to tell him stories for eons (he pets them like a pet). Chelle trades herself to Hahyah in exchange for Hel's freedom, becoming his reluctant 'little flea' minstrel — a captivity she's rescued from in the end.

title: Elioti
teaser: Txizle's Seelie fiancée, Gwen's furious guardian.
body: A knife-and-bladed-nunchuck-wielding Seelie who loved the Unseelie leader Txizle. After his death she shields Gwen from the vengeful mob — not from kindness but to make Gwen live with her guilt — then fights beside her in the prison uprising.

title: Tamzirian
teaser: The Priot warlord who imprisons the Unseelie.
body: The cruel Seelie commander of the Priot who rules the prison camp, executing rebels and using the truth of Gwen's lies to turn the Unseelie against her — claiming he protects them from the Courts above.

title: Sandra
teaser: The friend who died on Gwen's first quest.
body: Gwen's friend who joined her and Brad on their first, fatal quest to deliver a necklace to Cheyenne. When a chaos witch attacked in the Rockies, Sandra sacrificed herself to save them — but a stray bolt stole Bradley's sanity, the origin of Gwen's guilt.

title: Mag Mell
teaser: The false-utopia Celtic realm of the Underworld.
body: A lush, flower-draped city in the Underworld ruled by King Manannan, open only to those of pure Celtic blood — banshees, kelpies, dullahans, sidhe. Beautiful on the surface, unnaturally hollow beneath; home to the black-onyx Temple of Samhain where Zabasha contacts the Winter Court.

source.real: Mag Mell ('the delightful plain') is the Irish Otherworld — a paradise of eternal youth, music, and plenty where sickness and death do not exist, ruled by the sea-god Manannán mac Lir. Reached over the western sea or beneath the waves, it is explicitly the Irish cousin of Greek Elysium and Norse Valhalla: the blessed-realm archetype.
source.weave: The Weave's Mag Mell is 'a lush, flower-draped city in the Underworld ruled by King Manannan, open only to those of pure Celtic blood' — keeping the authentic ruler (Manannán) and the paradise-surface, with an unnaturally-hollow underside added. The Celtic blessed-plain placed on the cross-pantheon underworld map.

crosslinks.summary: The 'blessed paradise of the dead' is one archetype across three traditions — Irish Mag Mell, Greek Elysium, Norse Valhalla — all reserved for a worthy few; the Weave seats all three in one Underworld.

interactions.note: Greek Elysium — the same blessed-dead paradise; classical sources explicitly parallel it with Mag Mell.
Norse Valhalla — the warriors' paradise; the Irish realm is often called the Celtic counterpart to it.

title: The Xirgolov
teaser: The four most powerful objects in the Fairy Realm.
body: Four artifacts of god-tier power — a Ring (of Orivil), a bracelet, a crown, and a scepter (the scepter alone blazing brighter than the other three combined). Hoarded in Zabasha's private archive; the scepter is the key to raising the Sunken Kingdom. Nimue seizes all four to become mightier than gods, but loses them when her wrist is severed.

title: The Sunken Kingdom
teaser: The Abyss the Courts deliberately sank.
body: The truth behind the fairy Abyss: not a kingdom lost but a kingdom sunk — deliberately pushed below the clouds by the kings and queens of the four Courts. Raising it back into the sky (which needs the Xirgolov scepter and, Zabasha claims, Lucy's sacrifice) is the heroes' aim — to free the Abyss fairies from oppression and darkness.

title: The Lich King
teaser: The deathless guardian of the tomb-maze.
body: A gaunt, red-eyed undead who has transcended mortal pain and guards King Thilber's tomb-maze (and Queen Agnostia's amulet) by playing a card game that controls the labyrinth's walls and traps. Gwen beats him by cheating — steering Lucy safely through to claim the prize.

source.real: A lich is an undead sorcerer or king who has cheated death — a gaunt, often skeletal being who persists by binding its life to an object or by dark magic, guarding its hoard or tomb. Rooted in ghost and revenant folklore and crystallized in modern fantasy as the deathless, intelligent undead.
source.weave: The Weave's Lich King is 'a gaunt, red-eyed undead who has transcended mortal pain,' guarding a tomb-maze and a queen's amulet — keeping the lich's essence (the deathless guardian-undead of a tomb and treasure), here with a taste for card games.

title: Queen Agnostia
teaser: The cagey Spring Court queen.
body: Ruler of the moss-clad Spring Court, keeper of the tomb of her grandfather King Thilber and his guarded amulet. Cunning and self-serving — she sends Lucy into the Lich King's maze, later tries to have Gwen killed, then is coerced by Red into marshaling her troops against Nimue.

title: Princess Celeste
teaser: The body Zabasha wears in the Fairy Realm.
body: The fairy princess whose body the soul of Zabasha inhabits after leaving Red. When Nimue severs the hand, it is truly Celeste's hand that is maimed — a reminder that the Snow Queen's vessel is an innocent, healed in the end by Farzinium.

title: King Fortinbras & Queen Inogvia
teaser: The Autumn Court rulers Zabasha robs.
body: The Autumn Court monarchs — Inogvia an old friend of Zabasha's from their youth, Fortinbras a 'bright,' secretive Seelie. Red, guided by Zabasha-in-the-gem, slips through their castle to steal the Xirgolov bracelet Inogvia wears.

title: The Faceless Woman
teaser: The being of the Dark Planet, beyond the gods.
body: An ancient witch-made-monster on the distant Dark Planet, power beyond the gods. Once a human princess sold to a witch and experimented on for twenty years, 'saved' by a banal prince, she imprisoned the witch to steal her power and became faceless and hollow. She takes Nimue as a reluctant pupil — a dark mirror of the witch's own hunger.

title: The Unveiling of Magic
teaser: The Battle of the Obsidian Spindle exposed magic to humanity.
body: When the sky opened over a Swiss mountain pass and Rose led an army of fairies against Nimue, every satellite on Earth recorded conclusive proof of magic — undoing the secrecy fae had guarded for millennia (they once burned the Library of Alexandria to fade into myth). Rose becomes a reluctant public figure, fielding the world's fear of the fae.

title: The Board of Directors
teaser: The six supreme gods who rule the universe.
body: A council of the most powerful gods (Zeus, Brahma, Tengri, Ukko, and others) who keep the universe 'in balance' and forbid interference with mortal affairs. They run the Crystal Keep prison and a prison ship, punish dissenters, and treat lesser gods and mortals with contempt. Nox is tried before them for creating Chelle and meddling in the Fairy Realm; Rama plots to dismantle them.

title: The Celestial Realm
teaser: The anachronistic center of the universe.
body: The sunless world at the center of the universe where the gods dwell — an 'anachronistic nightmare' mixing every era (medieval, steampunk, modern) because the gods import their favorite times. Home to the Crystal Keep prison, the junction of every Obsidian Spindle, and Hepit's bar where the fugitives hide. The stars circle it rather than the reverse.

title: Rama
teaser: The vain god plotting to topple the Board.
body: A flamboyant, attention-craving 'god of virtue' who rules a circuit-board world and secretly leads a rebellion to 'destroy the patriarchy and dismantle the Board of Directors.' He recruits Red for her unique nature (more than human, less than god), helps build and then break into the Crystal Keep, and forms a deep bond with her.

source.real: Rama is the hero of the Sanskrit epic Ramayana — the seventh avatar of Vishnu, the ideal man and king, who journeys to rescue his wife Sita from the demon-king Ravana. He embodies dharma (virtue, duty, righteousness): the god-king whose entire legend is the test and triumph of moral order.
source.weave: The Weave's Rama is a flamboyant 'god of virtue' who rules a circuit-board world and leads a rebellion to dismantle the Board of Directors — keeping the core (a god defined by virtue and righteous rebellion against a corrupt order) while satirizing it into an attention-craving revolutionary.

title: Athena
teaser: The Board's loyal enforcer.
body: The goddess who serves as the Board of Directors' enforcer — capturing Chelle and Nox, escorting them to judgment, and zealously defending the Board's order even as Nox mocks her for being the gods' 'errand girl.' Believes the Board's will keeps the universe safe.

title: The Dark Planet & Carcosa
teaser: The sunless horror-world of the Faceless Woman.
body: A lightless, monster-haunted world (its capital the gothic city Carcosa) where the Faceless Woman dwells and the Lovecraftian King in Yellow, Hastur, holds court. Lit only by the inner spark of its flowers and beasts; reached via Obsidian Spindle. Red's long galactic search leads toward it; Nimue's ambition ends here in horror.

source.real: Carcosa is the lost, eerie city first named in Bierce's 'An Inhabitant of Carcosa' (1886) and adopted by Chambers — an alien place of black stars and twin suns sinking into the lake of Hali, glimpsed only in fragments. It is the archetypal Lovecraftian 'eldritch location': a city whose very geography signals something from beyond the stars.
source.weave: The Weave's Dark Planet makes Carcosa its gothic capital — a lightless, monster-haunted world lit only by the inner spark of its flowers and beasts, where Hastur holds court. It literalizes Chambers's 'black stars over Carcosa' as an actual sunless world reached through the Obsidian Spindles.
source.work: Robert W. Chambers, The King in Yellow / Bierce, 'An Inhabitant of Carcosa'

title: King Hastur, the King in Yellow
teaser: The beloved-and-feared ruler of Carcosa.
body: The Lovecraftian monarch of Carcosa on the Dark Planet — pure, oozing power, adored and feared by his gothic court of horrors and his four princesses. Nimue is sent as the Faceless Woman's emissary to his palace; rather than fall, he turns the tables, and she ends flayed and imprisoned beneath his castle.

source.real: Hastur — 'the King in Yellow' — originates with Ambrose Bierce ('Haïta the Shepherd,' 1891, where Hastur is a benign shepherd-god) and Robert W. Chambers's 1895 story collection The King in Yellow, where the name attaches ominously to a cursed city, a play that drives its readers mad, and the Yellow Sign. Chambers left the relationships deliberately unexplained — the horror lies in the vagueness. (Hastur-as-Great-Old-One and Cthulhu's half-brother is August Derleth's later codification, NOT in the public-domain originals.)
source.weave: The Weave's King Hastur IS the King in Yellow — the Lovecraftian monarch of Carcosa, holding court over a gothic horror-realm. It keeps the Chambers iconography (the King in Yellow, the lost city Carcosa) and gives the deliberately-unexplained figure a throne, a court, and four princesses.
source.work: Robert W. Chambers, The King in Yellow (1895)
source.excerpt_ref: The Repairer of Reputations; The Yellow Sign

title: Cassandra Vespertine & Baba
teaser: The witch-guides of the Dark Planet.
body: Denizens of the Dark Planet: Cassandra Vespertine, a courtly guide who exchanges 'desecrated greetings' and trades in horrors, and Baba — a deceptively kind, Spindle-spinning crone (a Baba Yaga) who covets Nimue's skin. They lead Nimue deeper into Carcosa's nightmares; Cassandra ultimately receives Nimue's flayed skin.

title: Ursula
teaser: The mermaid queen who raised — and bound — Ariel.
body: Queen of the mermaids of the Forgotten Sea, who took in the drowned Ariel at Nox's request and raised her as a daughter for 300 years — while repeatedly wiping her memories 'to protect her,' keeping her a docile, living vault for Nox's secrets. Her love and her control are inseparable.

title: The Left Eye of Rapunzel
teaser: A lost relic Queen Aine sends Ariel to find.
body: A relic — the left eye of Rapunzel — that Queen Aine, on the word of the Fates and Hypnos, believes Ariel can locate. Ariel tracks it via her mother's spirit-visions to a shrine in the first Church of the Six, only to find the box that held it already empty, stolen away.

source.tradition: German fairy tale (Brothers Grimm, public domain)
source.real: Rapunzel is the Brothers Grimm fairy tale (1812) of a long-haired maiden locked in a doorless tower, whose hair becomes the ladder to her. A tale of imprisonment, longing, and the price of a bargain (her mother's theft of rapunzel-greens from a witch's garden).
source.weave: The Weave's 'Left Eye of Rapunzel' is a sought relic — taking the fairy-tale heroine and making a piece of her a quest-object with scrying power. The tower-maiden's body becomes a holy relic in the Weave's economy of magical objects.

title: Vivian
teaser: Ariel's mermaid 'sister' — secretly Loki's pawn.
body: A mermaid raised alongside Ariel as a sister, who hunts her down on Ursula's orders. Revealed to be Loki's former handmaiden and co-conspirator: she helps him scheme to claim the Trident of Atlantis and Rapunzel's eye from Nox's vault, scorning the 'mothers' (Ursula, Nox) who 'held her down,' and aiming to rule Earth and beyond.

source.real: The mermaid who longs for another world is the heart of Hans Christian Andersen's 'The Little Mermaid' (1837); 'Vivian' also echoes the Lady of the Lake (Vivien/Nimue) of Arthurian legend. The Weave braids the little-mermaid figure with a watery enchantress-name.
source.weave: The Weave's Vivian is a mermaid raised as Ariel's sister who hunts her on Ursula's orders — set among the Little-Mermaid cast (Ariel, Ursula, the Trident) and revealed as Loki's co-conspirator. The Andersen mermaid-world given a traitor-sister.

title: Loki
teaser: The trickster who drowned Ariel 300 years ago.
body: The god of mischief, the hidden architect of Ariel's ruin: he engineered her drowning three centuries ago as vengeance for her fealty to Hypnos and the taking of his handmaiden Vivian, and murdered the kind woman Ariel believed her mother. He conspires with Vivian for the Trident and Rapunzel's eye, but is defeated by Hypnos and Ariel and imprisoned beneath the Emerald City.

source.real: Loki is the Norse trickster god — shape-shifter, schemer, father of monsters, whose cunning both aids and dooms the gods; at Ragnarök he leads the forces against them. The agent of chaos within the divine order.
source.weave: This is the Obsidian-Spindle-thread face of Loki — the same Norse trickster scheming (with Vivian) to claim the Trident of Atlantis. See also his other thread-face; one trickster, multiple appearances.

title: Nox's Vault
teaser: The goddess's vast secret undersea archive.
body: An immense, blinding-white, shadowless vault hidden in an undersea cavern where Nox hoards relics across ages — among them the Trident of Atlantis (long sought by the mermaid queen) and, perhaps, Rapunzel's eye. Its disorienting even light is a deliberate defense against intruders.

title: Zeus
teaser: The dominant power of the Board of Directors.
body: The most fearsome member of the Board — he tears souls from bodies (as he did to Nox) and reattaches them to extract secrets, favoring mind-control to avoid his own battles. He captures Red, Rama, and Brahma when Red's assassination attempt fails, proving even the rebels are outmatched.

source.real: Zeus is the king of the Greek gods, ruler of Olympus, wielder of the thunderbolt, who leads the Olympians to victory over the Titans and divides the cosmos with his brothers Poseidon and Hades. God of sky, law, and kingship, he is supreme but not absolute — bound, like all, by Fate.
source.weave: The Weave makes Zeus head of the Greek pantheon whose feud with Odin (over casting out the Four Horsemen) founds the divine politics — and whose old hoarding of creation-power, with Cronus, gates the Source until the Battle of the Obelisk.

title: Odin & Frigg
teaser: The Board allies who betray Chelle.
body: A god-king and his stoic queen of the Celestial Realm. Under the guise of hospitality, Frigg poisons Chelle's food and Odin straps her down with rune-bracers, meaning to harvest her gorgon nature for the Board — courtly cruelty behind a banquet.

title: The Circle of Truth
teaser: Rama's secret cabal against the Board.
body: A clandestine alliance of gods — Rama, iNyanga, Aditi, Brahma, Hepit, and others — working to dismantle the Board of Directors and end its tyranny. Their layered deceptions (feigning loyalty to the Board, manipulating allies like Red) make them hard to trust, but their cause is real.

title: Aditi
teaser: The kindly sari-clad goddess who frees Red.
body: A gentle goddess of the Circle of Truth, in a yellow-and-red sari, who slips into the Crystal Keep to free Red from solitary, feeding her granola bars and faith. Warm where the other gods are cruel — proof not all the Board's servants share its heart.

title: Kadlu
teaser: The exiled goddess of a dying acid-rain world.
body: A goddess hiding on a ruined world scoured by acid rain, whom the Board tried and failed to wipe out — sheltering in tunnels beneath a dead city. She knows the secret of the Spore, the blue-crystal sickness infecting and twisting the gods, and reluctantly takes in the stranded Rose.

title: The Spore
teaser: A sickness spreading among the gods, twisting them.
body: A creeping infection — manifesting as blue crystals deadly to the uninfected — that has spread among the gods, turning the righteous selfish and the weak-willed monstrous. Hypnos senses it corrupting his own people; Kadlu studies it. It may be the true rot behind the Board's cruelty and the cosmos's unraveling.

title: The Golden Locket
teaser: The relic-weapon to undo the King in Yellow.
body: A golden locket hidden deep in Baba's monster-prison — the key to defeating King Hastur. Bethel and Elvira brave the prison to retrieve it (Elvira dies in the attempt); Nimue makes it the linchpin of her wedding-day coup. At the climax it is nearly lost to a fleeing shadow, the fate of the Dark Planet hanging on its recovery.

title: Bethel
teaser: Hastur's favored torturer, turned reluctant rebel.
body: The most ruthless and loyal of Hastur's princesses, who wears the queen's crown and has long escaped his wrath by playing the game better than her sisters. Torn between betraying Nimue's plot and joining it, she is won over — and, after Elvira sacrifices herself for her, fully commits to freeing them all from the King in Yellow.

title: Elvira & the Princesses
teaser: Hastur's wives, abused into his enforcers.
body: The five princesses bound to King Hastur (Bethel, Elvira, Delilah, Lydia, and the restored Cassandra) — beautiful horrors he brutalizes and uses as torturers. Nimue turns them one by one toward rebellion. Elvira, bonding with Bethel, gives her life retrieving the golden locket, her sacrifice cementing their revolt.

title: Corben & Canterbury
teaser: Ariel's allies in the Nightmare Realm.
body: Corben, a long-stranded human survivor of the Nightmare Realm who hunts to stay alive and rescues Ariel; and Canterbury, a malformed talking rabbit and the Shadow King's servant who turns to Ariel's side. Together they help her free the realm's prisoners and reach the divide back toward the Dream Realm.

title: The Shadow King (Kelvin)
teaser: The tyrant of the fallen Nightmare Realm.
body: Kelvin, the 'Shadow King' who rules the Nightmare Realm from Epiales's old castle after the god of nightmares' death — torturing and imprisoning its denizens, desperate himself to reach the Dream Realm. Deposed by Ariel's uprising, he is spared and brought along, softening under her mercy to face Hypnos's judgment.

title: Aniza & the Key Maker
teaser: The keepers of the secret of the Dark Planet's key.
body: Aniza, the human wife of Shaun the lost 'key maker' — the only one who can forge a new key to the locked Dark Planet. Frigg trades the key maker's secret to Rama (tired of protecting him for empty promises). Aniza is found murdered, her house hiding a Spindle that becomes Rose and Chelle's escape route.

title: Maricel
teaser: Rama's kind servant who aids Rose's escape.
body: A red-sari'd servant in Rama's mansion, unfailingly warm to Rose despite her master's cruelty. When Rama turns on Rose, Maricel — her own Spore-locked memories freed — helps Rose and Chelle flee through the hidden Spindle beneath Aniza's house.

title: The Spore (the Primordials)
teaser: Outside-the-universe beings who possess the gods.
body: The true final enemy of the saga: a hive-minded Primordial force from beyond the barrier of the universe, manifesting as a blue-crystal 'Spore' that infects and possesses the gods (turning their eyes black and their wills to one), spreading the selfishness and cruelty seen across the Board. Coordinating through a shared network of minds, the Spore seize Nox, Ukko, Athena and dozens more, and attempt a ritual — using Hypnos as a conduit and Ariel as sacrifice — to tear open a gate and flood the universe with Primordials. They are repelled at the Battle of the Celestial Realm: the cure is the spores themselves (sprayed into a host's mouth) and Nimue's realm-wide banishing circle. Defeated, but a reminder of what waits outside.

title: Hope Bringer
teaser: The Elvish-engraved sword that saves the Dream Realm.
body: A sword hidden in Nox's vast vault, engraved 'Hope Bringer' in Elvish — the weapon Hypnos sends Ariel to find. She wrests its location from the imprisoned Vivian and, dying, carries it to the throne of Urgu to break the Spore's ritual and save the Dream Realm, the instrument of her ascension to godhood.

title: Rose & Chelle's Ending
teaser: The quiet life earned after the saga.
body: After the Spore are defeated, Rose and Chelle leave New York for a small Montana wheat farm — married, at peace, with their dog Cheyenne and their friend Jamil nearby. Chelle is the most powerful being in Urgu and Rose perhaps the mightiest human alive, yet what they choose is an ordinary, hard-won quiet — attending Red's memorial, finally able to simply live. The saga's promise made good: good people can seize their own destiny.

title: The Hammer of War
teaser: The obsidian war-hammer — fifth of the god-killing weapons.
body: One of the five weapons that can kill a god, wielded by War of the Four Horsemen. Long lost somewhere in Hell during Conquest, it is described in Chaos as a great hammer of black obsidian carved with runes — the clearest in-text sign that the five weapons are obsidian, matching Eternity's reveal.

source.real: The second Horseman of Revelation rides a red horse and is given a great sword and the power to take peace from the earth — the rider of War and slaughter.
source.weave: The Weave's Hammer of War is the god-killing weapon of the War Horseman — a great black-obsidian hammer — keeping the Revelation war-rider's role (the bringer of conflict) and arming him with a Titan-forged weapon.

title: Worst Thing in the Universe
teaser: God studies the universe's worst man to decide if any of it is worth saving.
body: A standalone novel narrated by God, who has shut out the prayers of his creation and chosen a single human to study: Albert Ross, statistically the worst being in the universe. Set in the distant future inside a thousand-story walled city, it follows Albert's fall from obscene wealth into the Dregs at the city's base, and the slow reckoning that follows. It is at once a tiny story about a handful of people and an argument about karma, mercy, and whether a flawed creation deserves to exist.

title: God (the Narrator)
teaser: A jaded, foul-mouthed creator who narrates the whole story.
body: The omniscient, omnipresent narrator who built this universe, his eighth attempt after seven failures. Burned out by the weight of every prayer and every life, he long ago muted the voices of his creation and put the cosmos on autopilot through karma. He sees a therapist, plays cards with a long-since-reconciled Lucifer, and has chosen to focus on one single man, Albert Ross, to decide whether humanity is worth caring about again.

title: Albert Ross
teaser: The richest, worst man alive — and a flaw in karma itself.
_sensitive: his introduction includes a coerced sexual assault of a child (Becky); anchored to his first non-graphic appearance and kept free of detail. Note for the primary on placement.
body: Albert Percival Ross the Third, the richest man in the world and figurehead 'messiah' of his family's church, who lives atop a thousand-story tower and has never lifted a finger or felt remorse. He is also a unique flaw in the universe: karma cannot register his actions, so his sins have always landed on someone else. After witnessing a man die because of him, his charmed life collapses and he is forced to discover who he might become with everything stripped away.

title: Vikram Suresh
teaser: A good man cursed to absorb another's karma.
_sensitive: Vikram dies by jumping from the tower at the end of chapter 2 after his wife and daughter are exploited; entry anchored to his living introduction and kept careful.
body: A kind, devoted husband and father whose every effort in life was inexplicably punished. Unknown to him, he is karma's chosen recipient for all of Albert Ross's sins, so misfortune followed him from a comfortable childhood down into the Dregs. Dying of an untreatable illness and driven to despair, he confronts Albert and extracts a sworn promise to protect his family. After his death he becomes a central presence in the afterlife, watching over those he left behind.

title: Sasha Suresh
teaser: Vikram's wife, hardened by the Dregs and undone by love.
_sensitive: Sasha survives by prostitution and made the decision that led to her daughter's exploitation; she is killed in the chapter 15 massacre. Handle placement and wording with care.
body: Vikram's wife, who fought her way up from the streets and whose love for her husband drove her to terrible choices to keep him alive. Wary, world-weary, and fierce, she nonetheless nurses the burned, ruined Albert Ross back to health when he crashes into her life, because in his eyes she catches a glimmer of her dead husband. Her guilt and her love define her; she becomes the moral weight Albert measures himself against.

title: Rebecca "Becky" Suresh
teaser: A Dregs child who becomes the woman who remakes the world.
_sensitive: introduced as a young child who is a victim of Albert's assault; she later remembers it. Entry anchored to her first appearance and kept free of detail.
body: Vikram and Sasha's daughter, a sharp, resilient girl raised scavenging in the Dregs. She survives the massacre that kills her mother and, inheriting Albert Ross's entire fortune, transforms it into a movement: rebuilding the Dregs, tearing down the city walls, and ending poverty across the world. Ruthless, honest, and unbroken, she grows from a naive child into the most consequential figure in the story.

title: Karma
teaser: The autopilot code God wrote so he could finally rest.
body: The universal system God built to hold every being accountable without his constant attention — a cosmic ledger that rewards and punishes actions, though never with exact or immediate change. It works perfectly on rational species elsewhere in the galaxy but breaks down badly on Earth, where free will muddies everything. God describes it as flawless, heartless, and impossible to alter without collapsing the entire universe.

source.real: Karma is the principle, central to the Indian religions, that every action carries moral consequence — good and bad deeds determining one's future circumstances, within the cycle of rebirth (samsara). It is the cosmic ethical accounting by which the universe holds beings responsible for what they do, life after life.
source.weave: The Weave's Karma is 'the universal system God built to hold every being accountable without his constant attention — a cosmic ledger that rewards and punishes' — the genuine Indian concept rendered almost literally as a divine accountability-engine running the moral books of the cosmos.

crosslinks.summary: Karma and the Reincarnation Cycle are the same Indian system — karma is the moral accounting that drives samsara, the wheel of rebirth.

interactions.note: Karma determines the terms of each rebirth in the cycle — the ledger and the wheel are one mechanism.

title: The Anomaly
teaser: A one-in-a-quadrillion glitch that misroutes a person's karma.
body: A rare fault in God's karmic code in which one being's actions are credited to someone else entirely. It surfaces across many species, usually harmlessly, but on Earth it is catastrophic: Albert Ross is the Anomaly, so every sin he commits is charged to the innocent Vikram Suresh. God cannot patch it without burning the universe down and starting over, so he lets it stand.

title: The Dregs
teaser: The lightless slum where the ground meets the sky.
body: The bottom of the great walled city, in the shadows beneath the thousand-story towers, where the poorest of the poor live among the turbines and support pillars. Cut off from sunlight and clean water, its people survive on the scraps that fall from the floors above and are treated as disposable playthings by the rich. It is where Vikram's family lives, where Albert Ross is reborn as a scavenger, and the seedbed of the change that eventually topples the old order.

title: The Walled City
teaser: A vertical society stratified by altitude.
body: A future megacity of thousand-story towers where status is measured literally by how high one lives — executives in the clouds, the middle class in the mid-floors, and the destitute in the Dregs below. Layered security checkpoints keep the castes apart, and a great wall encircles the whole city. Most residents do not even know they could go outside, a deliberately maintained ignorance that keeps cheap labor docile.

title: The City Wall
teaser: Built to keep the riffraff in, not out.
body: The great barrier around the city, guarded by soldiers whose guns point inward. Generations of propaganda — tales of monsters and nuclear winter beyond it — have convinced the poor that the outside is deadly, when in truth it is open land and sunlight withheld to deny them hope. Becky Suresh's defiance ultimately forces the government to tear it down, ending millennia of confinement.

title: The Church of Latent Currency
teaser: A religion engineered to bilk the guilty rich.
body: The 'church' founded by Albert Ross the Second by incorporating the family business as a faith, built on the tenet that wealth is God's reward and that donations buy a better place in Heaven. It preys on the guilt of the rich while crushing the poor with the belief that their poverty is a moral failing. Albert the Third serves as its infallible figurehead messiah, and the institution's collapse is one of the engines of his downfall.

title: Harry
teaser: Albert's handler, loyal only to the winning side.
body: Albert Ross's gaudy, fast-talking business manager, who manages and manipulates him for the board's ends with peanut-butter-cup bribes and constant flattery. When the company turns on Albert, Harry sides with the winners without hesitation. He later resurfaces, improbably, as a director of the FBI after testifying against his old colleagues, and strikes the deal that briefly restores Albert's fortune.

title: Dolores
teaser: Albert's half-sister, who sells him out for spite and money.
body: Albert's narcissistic, pleasure-seeking half-sister, his closest companion in debauchery and the one relative he genuinely liked. Resentful of a lifetime of being treated as lesser by their father, she sells her hidden shares of the company to the board, handing them the majority stake they need to oust Albert. She is the betrayal that begins his financial ruin.

title: Dr. Hu Wang
teaser: The board member who engineers Albert's ouster.
body: Head of the medical division of Albert Ross's company and the architect of the boardroom coup. Coldly methodical, he uncovers that Albert never truly held a majority stake, buys out Dolores's shares, and uses a long-forgotten morality clause to force Albert out with nothing. He represents the faceless corporate machinery that runs the empire while Albert merely smiles and signs.

title: Hoyt
teaser: The smug interim FBI director who parades Albert as a scapegoat.
body: The government official who takes custody of the imprisoned Albert Ross and trots him out as a public scapegoat for the economy's collapse, always speaking in a self-serving royal 'we.' He tries to intimidate Becky Suresh into silence and badly underestimates her. In the end it is he who is cornered into freeing Albert and tearing down the wall.

title: Sandy (God's Therapist)
teaser: The shape-shifting shrink who sends God to study one man.
body: God's psychologist, a being who appears in many forms — sometimes alien, sometimes a disembodied voice, most often human — and whose intellect God himself granted. She diagnoses his detachment and 'God complex' and prescribes the experiment at the heart of the book: focus on one single person in one moment to relearn empathy. She also counsels the newly dead, including Vikram.

title: The Afterlife
teaser: A personal buffer zone where souls reset before reincarnation.
body: Not the Heaven or Hell of human belief but a buffering system God built so souls across all species can 'reset' before being reincarnated into new vessels. Each soul shapes its own experience: the at-peace find bliss, while the tormented trap themselves in a self-made hell until their minds can be coaxed free — the source of near-death experiences. Vikram and Sasha Suresh are reunited here, waiting for their daughter.

source.real: Across religions the afterlife is the state of the soul after death — often with an intermediate stage (the Catholic purgatory, the Tibetan bardo, the Greek asphodel) where souls wait, are purified, or are sorted before their final destination. The buffer between one life and what comes next.
source.weave: The Weave's Afterlife is 'not the Heaven or Hell of human belief but a buffering system God built so souls across all species can reset before being reborn' — taking the comparative idea of an intermediate state (the bardo/purgatory) and rationalizing it as a cosmic reset-buffer feeding the reincarnation cycle.

title: Hospice: One Damned Good Thing
teaser: A dying convict discovers his hospice is a slaughterhouse for souls.
_needs_godsverse_merge: The credits page names the Hospice universe as co-created by Travis Gibb, Russell Nohelty, Frank Martin, Jamie Primack, David Byrne, and Michael Watson — a shared world, not solely Russell's. Primary should decide whether/how Hospice links into owned canon and whether it belongs in the codex at all.
body: A short Hospice-universe comic written by Russell Nohelty with art by Lane Lloyd. It follows Vic Madison, a terminally ill convict who is transferred to a hospice to live out his last days, only to discover the place is a front where demons harvest the wicked. Confronting the truth that a demon has been gestating inside him his whole life, Vic chooses one final act of defiance.

title: Vic Madison
teaser: A dying convict who insists he's a bastard, not a monster.
_sensitive: Vic ends his own life by stepping off a cliff to kill the demon inside him; the act is framed as sacrifice. Handle placement and wording with care.
body: An old, terminally ill inmate of Sunny Valley Penitentiary who confesses he's never done one good thing and has only a cruel inner 'voice' where a conscience should be. Transferred to a hospice to die, he uncovers its demonic purpose and refuses to be used. Discovering the voice is a real demon waiting to be born from him, he resolves that being a bastard is not the same as being evil — and makes a final choice to deny it a body.

title: Rising Suns Hospice
teaser: A serene end-of-life home that feeds the damned to demons.
body: A picturesque hospice in the countryside, bought from the DeFrain family after World War II, that takes in the dying — especially the wicked — with warm hospitality and a 'magical place to be' sales pitch. Behind its welcoming face it is a harvesting ground where demons consume tormented souls. Its staff are not entirely human and pursue anyone who learns the truth.

title: "Skippy"
teaser: The grinning hospice greeter who refuses to give his name.
body: The cheerful, broad attendant who welcomes Vic to Rising Suns and refuses, by policy, to give his real name — so Vic dubs him 'Skippy.' Relentlessly upbeat about the hospice's history and charm, he drops his friendly mask the moment Vic stumbles onto the truth, revealing himself as something inhuman that will get physical to keep its secrets.

title: The Prison Doctor
teaser: Vic's confidante, who delivers the damned for her own salvation.
body: The bespectacled prison physician who counsels Vic and arranges his transfer to the hospice, presenting it as a kindness. She is in fact complicit: in exchange for delivering wicked souls, her own soul is kept safe from corruption so she can reach Heaven. She tells Vic the hard truth about the demon inside him but refuses to repent, believing her god will protect her.

title: The Gestating Demon
teaser: The cruel inner voice that is really a demon waiting to be born.
body: The 'monster' Vic has carried his whole life in place of a conscience — not a metaphor but a literal demon, gestating inside a wicked host and feeding off their cruelty until it is ready to emerge. The hospice exists to deliver such hosts at the end of their lives. Vic's last act is an attempt to destroy his own body completely so the demon dies unborn and can never hurt anyone.

title: I'll Kill You
teaser: A stolen tuna sandwich escalates into all-out war.
body: A short, scribbly-art gag comic written and owned by Russell Nohelty. Two cafeteria acquaintances, the would-be supervillain Billy and the big-headed Clifford, fall into a feud after Clifford eats Billy's tuna fish sandwich. Their revenge spirals from threats into robot armies, force fields, and doomsday bombs, lampooning escalation and mutually assured destruction before landing on a deadpan punchline.

title: Billy
teaser: A kid who fancies himself an evil mastermind.
body: A spiky-haired boy who eats the same tuna fish sandwich every day and insists he is busy 'perpetrating evil' and 'hatching evil.' When Clifford eats his sandwich, Billy declares war, deploying an evil robot legion and a doomsday device. His mother's offhand offer of another sandwich hints the whole grand villainy may be playing out in his head.

title: Clifford
teaser: The big-headed friend who couldn't resist the sandwich.
body: A large-headed, deadpan boy who shares Billy's cafeteria table and, left to guard the sandwich, gives in and devours it. Far from defenseless, he answers Billy's escalations with laser grids, force fields, and a doomsday bomb of his own, noting offhandedly that his dad is a defense contractor. He matches Billy threat for threat to a mutual stalemate.

title: The Tuna Fish Sandwich
teaser: The 'culinary delight' that starts a war.
