body: Billy's beloved daily lunch, which he calls the most exquisite culinary delight there is. Asked to watch it while Billy steps away, Clifford eats it, and the theft of this one sandwich is the spark for the entire escalating conflict.

title: The Evil Robot Legion
teaser: Billy's army of robots that combine into one giant.
body: Billy's homemade swarm of boxy robots, summoned to destroy Clifford and capable of merging Voltron-style into a single towering mecha. They prove no match for Clifford's escalating defenses, much to Billy's dismay over his 'babies.'

title: The B.O.B. Bomb
teaser: A 21,000-megaton doomsday device — each side has one.
body: The ultimate weapon Billy brandishes to force Clifford's surrender, demanding he accept his fate or face mutually assured destruction. Clifford reveals he has one too, fractionally bigger, and both are detonated at once — a punchline on the absurdity of an arms race over a sandwich.

title: F This
teaser: A collection of deadpan, absurdist one-panel gags.
body: A short anthology comic by Russell Nohelty: thirty standalone single-panel cartoons, each pairing a loosely doodled creature or object with a bleak, apathetic, or pun-based one-liner. There is no continuing story or recurring cast — it is a sketchbook of nihilist humor (a musical note delivering a 'one note joke,' an apple noting you'll bury half the people you love, a dog sighing that life is too hard to listen to what it thinks).

title: Gherkin Boy and the Dollar of Destiny
teaser: A pickle is sent on a pointless quest for a cursed dollar.
body: An absurdist, pun-driven quest comic created, written, and drawn by Russell Nohelty (colors by Thomas Bacon), set on a planet that is itself an evil cheese danish. Gherkin Boy, a happy-go-lucky pickle, is talked into fetching the legendary Dollar of Destiny from the Woods of Doomy Gloom, armed only with a reluctant, wisecracking magic fork. The journey runs through a black hole, Hell, and a string of strange creatures before arriving at a deliberately anticlimactic payoff.

title: Gherkin Boy
teaser: A happy-go-lucky pickle and cheerful mooch.
body: The hero of the tale: a boy just like the ones you know, except he is a pickle. Known as a friendly mooch who never pays for anything and is, by the narrator's own note, a bit of an idiot, he is secretly disliked by everyone — though he never realizes it. Eager to please and easily talked into things, he undertakes the quest for the Dollar of Destiny mostly so he can keep getting a puff, and just wants to go home to his family.

title: Forkster
teaser: A transforming, foul-mouthed magic fork for hire.
body: A living, talking fork that can transform and fight, recruited as Gherkin Boy's reluctant companion. Cynical, mercenary, and constantly complaining — it would rather be at the titty bar than on a quest — it agrees to help only after being paid half a 'not very shiny' penny up front. Despite hating the job and Gherkin Boy alike, it pulls out devastating moves like 'Super Fork Jitsu' and the finishing 'Prongality' before parting ways to go home to its own family.

title: Misses Alien
teaser: A lonely eye-creature who joins the journey for the view.
body: An eyeball-shaped alien Gherkin Boy meets along the way, who becomes a traveling companion after Forkster departs. Having no family and no home, she joins him simply because it would be nice to see another part of this wretched universe.

title: The Dollar of Destiny
teaser: A cursed coin reading 'In Vodka Jesus We Trust.'
body: The legendary one-dollar coin at the heart of the quest, stamped 'In Vodka Jesus We Trust' and 'One Destiny,' hidden deep in the Woods of Doomy Gloom. It was stolen from an evil wizard by two tree spirits who were cursed for it, their souls unable to wander free until a brave hero won the dollar from them — which Gherkin Boy unwittingly does. When he finally returns it, the ones who sent him simply shrug, revealing the whole quest had no real point.

title: The Woods of Doomy Gloom
teaser: The cursed forest hiding the Dollar of Destiny.
body: The dark, dangerous forest where the Dollar of Destiny is hidden, guarded by hazards including a 'donut mattress' and home to the cursed tree spirits. Reaching and surviving it is the object of Gherkin Boy's journey.

title: The Evil Cheese Danish Planet
teaser: A world just like ours — except it's a pastry.
body: The setting of the whole story: a planet just like Earth, except that it is an evil cheese danish. Its sky is dotted with absurd cosmic neighbors — a ringed Planet Man, floating eyeballs, spirals, and UFOs — establishing the comic's nonsensical, pun-logic universe.

title: How Not to Invade Earth
teaser: Two alien slackers blow up the Moon and bumble into a war.
body: A deadpan absurdist comic written and drawn by Russell Nohelty (letters by Cammry LapKa), following two googly-eyed Venusian aliens, Reck and Trap, after Reck casually blows up Earth's Moon. The act triggers Earth's military mobilization and a clumsy escalation toward all-out war. Told in flat, understated humor over public-domain photo backgrounds, it satirizes incompetence, escalation, and the pointlessness of conquest before resolving into an anticlimactic peace.

title: Reck
teaser: A blue alien who blows up the Moon just because.
body: One of the two Venusian alien leads, a squat blue creature with an impulsive, devil-may-care streak. He casually decides to blow up Earth's Moon and pushes the button despite his friend's alarm, kicking off the whole conflict. As the consequences mount and the pair are captured, he comes to admit the disaster is all his fault.

title: Trap
teaser: The green alien who wanted no part of any of this.
body: The taller, green Venusian and Reck's anxious companion, who treats blowing up the Moon as a bad joke and immediately wants to distance himself from it. The reluctant straight man to Reck's recklessness, he is dragged into the war and capture that follow, protesting the whole way.

title: General Eyeball
teaser: A military commander mobilizing for retaliation.
body: One of the uniformed military figures who leads wartime preparations in response to the Moon's destruction, overseeing locked-and-loaded forces ready to deploy. Part of the chain of command that escalates the situation toward war.

title: Earth's Moon
teaser: Blown up on a whim — the spark for everything.
body: Earth's Moon, which Reck destroys with the push of a button for no real reason. Its sudden destruction is the inciting incident of the comic, leaving a 'big hole' that nobody wants to fix and provoking Earth into a war footing against the aliens.

title: Ichabod Jones: Monster Hunter (Book 1)
teaser: An asylum inmate, guided by a voice, wakes into a world of real monsters.
body: A full-color horror comic written and created by Russell Nohelty with art by Renzo Podestá, collecting the first arc of Ichabod Jones: Monster Hunter. Ichabod, an institutionalized young man in a straitjacket, is roused by a disembodied voice that leads him out of his cell and into an asylum overrun by monsters. As he survives one horror after another and falls in with a band of survivors, the story keeps it ambiguous whether the voice is a guiding savior or his own madness — and whether Ichabod is a hero or a tool.

title: Ichabod Jones
teaser: An asylum inmate turned reluctant monster hunter.
_sensitive: Ichabod is institutionalized and tormented by a voice that may be a hallucination; the book leaves his sanity deliberately ambiguous. Handle wording with care.
body: A frail, wide-eyed young man found strapped in a straitjacket in a padded cell, woken by a voice only he can hear that names him a monster hunter. Terrified but resourceful, he survives demons and worse using the voice's strange tricks, and proves braver than anyone expects — even earning the grudging admission that he might really be a hero. Whether the voice guides him or he is simply mad is never resolved, and Book 1 leaves him gravely wounded and fading.

title: The Voice
teaser: The disembodied guide — savior, master, or madness?
body: A disembodied voice that speaks only to Ichabod, claiming to have prepared him for his mission and steering him through every danger with uncanny knowledge — that a holy book weighs thousands of pounds to a demon, that monster intestines make a strong rope. Possessive and jealous, it warns him against trusting the other survivors and insists he needs no one. It may be a true guiding force or a symptom of Ichabod's condition; the book refuses to say, ending on its haunting 'I'm sorry, Ichabod.' In the interactive RPG adaptation, this question is finally answered: the Voice is revealed to be the archangel Uriel, who had been sheltering inside Ichabod all along — the demonic-seeming guide was an angel the whole time. (The comic deliberately leaves this open; the game makes it canon for the game's telling.)

crosslinks.summary: The Voice IS the archangel Uriel — same figure; the Voice is Uriel's indwelling form. See Uriel for the Enochic root.

interactions.note: The Voice IS the archangel Uriel — same figure; the Voice is Uriel's indwelling form. See Uriel for the Enochic root.

title: Cathy
teaser: A survivor who revives Ichabod and refuses to give up on him.
body: One of the band of survivors trapped in the monster-infested asylum, who shocks Ichabod back to life with a defibrillator after a brutal fall. Warm and stubborn where the Voice is cold, she comes to depend on him, pleading with him to stay alive — directly contradicting the Voice's insistence that he needs no one. In the RPG adaptation, Cathy is revealed to carry the archangel Samael, just as Ichabod carries Uriel — the two survivors were angel-bearers without knowing it.

title: Thomas
teaser: A leader among the asylum survivors.
body: One of the survivors Ichabod joins, part of a dwindling group that once sent teams to fight the horror and is now trapped waiting to die. Level-headed and central to the group's plans — including the desperate scheme to escape the grounds by an old rusted bus — he stands among the allies the Voice repeatedly urges Ichabod to distrust. (Other survivors named include Crane and Bishop.)

title: Jessup
teaser: A cowboy-hatted gunman who coerces Ichabod into killing.
body: A ruthless, drawling gunman encountered outside of town, who forces Ichabod to clear out the 'zomboids' massing at a nearby mountain by threatening to kill his friends. When Ichabod succeeds, Jessup reneges on the deal and orders his men to execute the group anyway, triggering the bloody shootout that ends Book 1.

title: The Monsters
teaser: Real horrors only Ichabod seems equipped to fight.
body: The creatures overrunning Ichabod's world: horned, glowing-eyed demons immune to ordinary bullets, colossal tentacled beasts with acid blood, and shambling 'zomboids' that gather by the hundreds drawn to blood. They are repelled by holy objects and by the strange methods the Voice teaches Ichabod, marking him as uniquely able to fight what others cannot.

title: Ichabod Jones: Monster Hunter (Book 2)
teaser: A wanted fugitive joins a seer and angels to end the Apocalypse.
_uncertain: Book 2's cosmology (angels vs demons, a 10,000-year accord, Satan and Six Dukes, named demons like Beelzebub) strongly resembles the angel/demon framework of the off-limits Godsverse canon (shared thread). I have NOT invented links into owned canon; primary should decide whether the Ichabod cosmology connects to Godsverse or stays self-contained.
body: The second collected arc of Ichabod Jones: Monster Hunter by Russell Nohelty and Renzo Podestá. Branded a violent fugitive by the outside world after his asylum escape, Ichabod presses on with the Voice and a new band of allies — a young robed seer with a spellbook and angels who can bless his weapons. Together they set out across a demon-ruled wasteland to confront the Dukes of Hell and undo the Apocalypse, even knowing the odds.

title: The Voice's Former Host
teaser: The hero the Voice guided before Ichabod — who died saving him.
body: Before Ichabod, the Voice guided another person, whose purpose was to become a great hero and bring hope back to humanity. Instead, he died saving Ichabod's life. This revelation reframes the Voice as a recurring entity that passes between hosts, and burdens Ichabod with the guilt that he survived at his predecessor's expense.

title: Ichabod's Fugitive Status
teaser: The world brands its would-be savior a violent criminal.
body: After Ichabod's escape from the asylum, television news reports it as a brutal crime — a knife held to an inmate's throat, a daring rooftop escape in a stolen prison truck — and broadcasts his face as armed and extremely dangerous. The survivors watch, realizing the world sees the boy meant to save it as a monster, deepening Ichabod's isolation.

title: Necromonica
teaser: A robed seer-sorceress waging war to end the Apocalypse.
_uncertain: Cosmology/naming may overlap with off-limits Godsverse canon; no links invented into owned canon. Named Necromonica in Book 4; appears unnamed (as a seer) in Books 2-3.
body: A young robed sorceress — unnamed until late in the series, when Ichabod calls her Necromonica — who carries an owl-headed staff and an ancient book said to hold the answers to ending the Apocalypse. Knowledgeable, fierce, and far warmer to Ichabod than the Voice, she recruits him to clear the demon-ruled desert, then America, then the whole Earth. She wields Latin binding and blood spells from her book, holds manifested demons in place, and grows into Ichabod's truest ally — slapping him back from the edge of death and standing with him before the demon lords.

title: The Angels
teaser: Holiness incarnate — allies who bless Ichabod's weapons.
body: Celestial beings who join Ichabod's cause, including a purple hooded figure and a blond, winged, armored warrior. Describing themselves as literally holiness incarnate, they can mend and bless a broken blade so it can slay a Duke of Hell, and claim they cannot truly die. They stand on the opposite side of the ancient war from the demons.

title: The Apocalypse
teaser: The demons won, and Hell invaded Earth.
_uncertain: This angel/demon accord cosmology may overlap with off-limits Godsverse canon; not linking into owned canon. Flagged for primary.
body: Before recorded time, two factions — the Demons and the Angels — vied for Earth and humanity. Unable to claim it outright, they struck an accord: for 10,000 years humanity would forge its own path unaided, its actions deciding whether it belonged to Heaven or Hell. That term ended in the Apocalypse, when the Demons won and invaded Earth, leaving a ruined, demon-ruled world that Ichabod and his allies hope to set right.

title: The Six Dukes of Hell
teaser: Satan's lieutenants ruling the conquered Earth.
_uncertain: Named demons (e.g. Beelzebub) and the Satan/Dukes structure may tie into off-limits Godsverse canon; not inventing links. Flagged for primary.
body: As the Apocalypse drew near and Satan knew he had won, he appointed six Dukes to carry out his domination of Earth while he himself ruled Hell. Each holds dominion over a region — one rules the whole desert from a castle across the horizon — and includes the Dark Prince Beelzebub. The seer's plan is to kill all six Dukes, then Satan, to restore the world.

title: Nightmare Elves
teaser: Blue beasts that hypnotize through eye contact.
body: Vicious blue, cat-like demons the seer calls nightmare elves. They come on their prey in the night, and when your eyes catch theirs they hypnotize you into doing their bidding — so they must be fought without meeting their gaze. Ichabod kills one with his bare hands by blocking, grabbing it by the ears, and swinging.

title: Ichabod Jones: Monster Hunter (Book 3)
teaser: One Duke down, the team learns the Devil must be forced to end it.
_uncertain: Book 3 names demons (Azazel) and leans on the Satan/Apocalypse cosmology that may overlap with off-limits Godsverse canon. No links invented into owned canon; flagged for primary.
body: The third collected arc of Ichabod Jones: Monster Hunter by Russell Nohelty and Renzo Podestá. Fresh off killing a Duke, the team learns that slaying Satan won't undo the Apocalypse — he must be forced to end it willingly. They flee a monstrous new Duke, Azazel, while Ichabod fights both the demon horde and the Voice's cold demand to abandon the captured Cathy, surviving a blood spell that drives his body to the edge of death.

title: Azazel
teaser: A hulking, ram-horned Duke of Hell with a spiked mace.
_uncertain: Named demon that may correspond to a figure in off-limits Godsverse canon; no links invented into owned canon. Flagged for primary.
body: A massive, ram-horned Duke of Hell wielding a spiked mace and adorned with skulls, who hunts Ichabod's group through the ruins. Contemptuous of humans — 'so feeble' — he overpowers the team with ease and commands an army, forcing them to flee rather than fight.

title: Sanguinem Aeternam
teaser: An inverted bloodletting curse that makes the body fight death.
body: A dangerous piece of advanced magic from the seer's book — an inverted bloodletting curse invoked with the words 'Sanguinem Aeternam.' Rather than draining life, it forces the body to fight off death, keeping Ichabod alive at the brink while the Voice delves into his mind. Its full effects are uncertain even to the caster. The RPG adaptation also introduces a separate, greater spell — the Enochiad — distinct from this bloodletting curse.

title: The Library of Ancient Books
teaser: A vault holding the most ancient books of all.
body: A chamber said to house the most ancient of all the books, which the group must move through carefully. The seer's world-saving knowledge and spells draw on such ancient texts, making the library a repository of the lore needed to fight the Apocalypse.

title: Ichabod Jones: Monster Hunter (Book 4)
teaser: The finale: the Voice's true nature, and a return to the cell.
_uncertain: Book 4 leans on the Lucifer/Dukes/Apocalypse cosmology that may overlap with off-limits Godsverse canon. No links invented into owned canon; flagged for primary.
body: The fourth and final collected arc of Ichabod Jones: Monster Hunter by Russell Nohelty and Renzo Podestá. The Voice confesses it is a demon Ichabod killed, seeking the Apocalypse's end so it can return. Brought as an offering to Lucifer's Castle, Ichabod lets the Voice possess him to bluff the assembled Dukes, then turns on the demons. The book ends by mirroring Book 1's opening — Ichabod back in his padded cell — leaving the reality of the whole saga deliberately, hauntingly open.

title: Lucifer's Castle
teaser: The Devil's stronghold, guarded by ten thousand monsters.
_uncertain: Lucifer and the demon-lord court may correspond to off-limits Godsverse canon; no links invented into owned canon. Flagged for primary.
body: The seat of Lucifer's power, guarded by some ten thousand monsters outside and worse within, where the Dukes of Hell gather in court. Ichabod is dragged here as an offering by Azazel, and it becomes the stage for the Voice's gambit to convene and deceive the assembled demon lords.

title: The Voice's Possession
teaser: The demon takes Ichabod's body to command the Dukes.
body: The Voice's risky plan and power: to possess Ichabod's mind and body and use its own authority to bend the other Dukes to its will and convene them. Ichabod fears that once he lets the demon take control it might never give the body back, and consents only because doing the hated thing is, as the Voice insists, part and parcel of being a hero.

title: Anna and the Dark Place
teaser: A grieving girl, her dead best friend's ghost, and a tear in the world.
body: Set on a near-present Earth in the Shared Thread. Sixteen-year-old Anna Aguilar, convinced she is cursed because everyone she loves dies, is visited by the glowing ghost of her best friend Katie, who reveals a widening rift to the Dark Place in the woods. With the self-taught witch Samantha, Anna races to close the rift — a quest through witch councils, goblins, trolls, and a hidden magical world — while grieving Katie and learning to let her go. Beneath the monster-hunt it is a story about grief and saying goodbye.

title: Anna Aguilar
teaser: A girl who believes her love is a curse that kills.
body: Sixteen, sharp-tongued, and grieving. Having buried her nana, her aunt, her father, and now her best friend Katie, Anna believes she is cursed — that everyone she loves dies — and tries to hold the world at arm's length to protect it from her. When Katie's ghost appears, Anna is pulled into closing a rift to the Dark Place, and into the harder work of grieving and letting go.

title: Katie
teaser: Anna's best friend, returned as a glowing blue ghost.
body: Anna's best friend, dead of leukemia, who returns as a glowing blue ghost only those attuned to magic can see. Warm and wry, she confesses she loved Anna, guides her to the rift in the woods, and helps fight to close it — knowing that mending the tear will mean leaving forever. In the Dark Place, ghosts who linger lose their shape and memory until nothing human remains.

title: Samantha
teaser: The new girl — a self-taught witch who joins the fight.
body: A transfer student and self-taught witch who can see Katie's ghost. Blunt, brave, and honest to a fault, she becomes Anna's partner in closing the rift. Captured by the witch Hilda and briefly replaced by a golem, she is the one who knows how to navigate the hidden world of witch councils, libraries, and spells.

title: The Dark Place
teaser: The underworld behind reality, where souls lose their form.
body: A realm behind the world — an underworld where the dead go and, if they linger, dissolve: losing shape, then memory, until nothing human is left (Katie's father no longer knew her name). A widening rift to the Dark Place threatens to consume the Earth, and closing it requires goblin bones, troll mucus, dragon fire, and a binding enchantment. The Dark Place is the Shared Thread's underworld — the same cosmological role Hell and the Underworld play in other threads, and it is Hades who ultimately seals it.

title: The Witch Council & Hilda
teaser: The hidden order of witches guarding the world's magic.
body: A concealed society of witches with a guarded central library (hidden inside the Museum of Man) and a high council. Hilda — handle 'Broom Hilda' — first appears as an antagonist but is revealed to be racing to CLOSE the rift, not open it; the true threat is Frank, the grief-maddened shopkeeper. Their world hides goblins, trolls, gnomes with pocket dimensions, golems, and old magic in plain sight.

title: Frank
teaser: The grieving shopkeeper who would end the world to resurrect his wife.
body: Owner of The Witch's Brew, a bumbling figure who turns out to be the saga's true danger. Maddened by grief for his dead wife Gina, he uses old magic gleaned in secret to keep the rift open and summon Hades, intending to resurrect her — willing to let the world end as the price. His ritual is what calls the god of the underworld into the Shared Thread.

title: Hades (Anna's thread)
teaser: The underworld god summoned at the climax — this thread's own.
body: The god of the underworld in Anna's thread, summoned by Frank's resurrection ritual at the climax. Utterly casual — he steps out of the summoning asking where to get frozen yogurt for Persephone, mentions his father once turned into a horse to fight a camel, and idly seals the rift to the Dark Place before strolling off. He belongs to this thread alone; like every thread, Anna's has its own gods.

source.real: Hades, Greek god of the underworld and the dead.
source.weave: In Anna's thread Hades is summoned by a resurrection ritual and is utterly casual — asking where to get frozen yogurt for Persephone, idly sealing a rift before strolling off. 'Like every thread, Anna's has its own gods': a deliberately mundane, comic face of the death-god, unique to this universe.

title: The Void Calls Us Home
teaser: A survivor, a cosmic Void that calls people to die, and the friend it took.
body: A contemporary, Lovecraftian YA story in the Shared Thread. Rebecca 'Becca' Rose survives a car crash she half-caused, swerving toward a thousand-foot black flaming eye — the Void — that calls to the grieving and the suicidal. Recovering and haunted by the Void's pull (and by her sister Mary's suicide), she falls in with a band literally named after it, and fights to pull her friend Trisha back when the Void claims her. A story about grief, suicide, and refusing the call.

title: Rebecca "Becca" Rose
teaser: A broken athlete who hears the Void calling and refuses it.
body: A former basketball star and sprinter whose life shatters in a car crash — broken arm, ribs, and shoulder — that she caused by swerving toward the Void. Stubborn, sharp, and grieving her dead sister Mary, she survives two comas, resists the Void's seductive pull, and risks herself to save Trisha. Her arc is learning to choose life and people over the emptiness.

title: The Void
teaser: A cosmic eye of fire that calls the grieving to dissolve into nothing.
body: A thousand-foot black eye in the dark that draws all light and warmth into itself, appearing to the grieving and the suicidal as an irresistible, blissful call to 'come home.' Nearly half the population has felt it. It devours souls into an endless cold cavern; those it takes can sometimes be bargained back through soul-binding. A Lovecraftian cosmic entity native to this thread — not a personified god, but a hungry nothingness behind the world.

source.real: The void or abyss — the formless dark that predates or underlies creation (Genesis's tohu wa-bohu, the Greek Chaos, Norse Ginnungagap) and, psychologically, the despair that 'draws all light into itself' — is a recurring image of nothingness as a hungry presence. The dark that calls to the grieving.
source.weave: The Weave's Void is 'a thousand-foot black eye in the dark that draws all light and warmth into itself, appearing to the grieving and the suicidal' — fusing the cosmological abyss with the lived experience of despair, the nothingness given an eye and an appetite.

title: Mary Rose
teaser: Becca's idolized older sister, lost to the Void.
body: Becca's older sister — valedictorian, field-hockey captain, kind to everyone — who died by suicide after leaving for college, a loss the family refuses to discuss and compartmentalizes. Her death is the wound that makes Becca vulnerable to the Void's call, and Becca's wish to see Mary again is what nearly pulls her in for good. Her journal becomes Becca's way of staying close to her.

title: Trisha
teaser: The damaged singer whose band is named for the Void.
body: The charismatic, damaged frontwoman of the band The Void Calls Us Home, who has felt the Void's call and channels it into her music. She draws Becca into the scene and into a doomed retreat that sends them into the Void; later the Void claims her into a coma, and Becca's soul-binding gambit is what brings her back.

title: Gwen
teaser: The bandmate who treats Becca as an equal — and a love interest.
body: Trisha's bandmate and Becca's steadier counterweight: blunt, loyal, and the one who treats Becca as a person rather than a project. Their relationship grows into something more as Becca pulls away from Trisha's gravitational chaos, and Gwen becomes her partner in the fight to save Trisha.

title: Cullen
teaser: The retreat leader whose ritual opens the way to the Void.
body: A self-styled guru who runs an illicit retreat that uses a homemade compound to send seekers into the Void for 'closure.' His experiment nearly kills Becca and ensnares Trisha, but he later helps research soul-binding — the method of trading or binding a soul (the ghost Thomas) to pull a victim back from the Void.

title: Thomas's Ghost
teaser: A bound, hollow ghost used to ransom Trisha from the Void.
body: A sad, mute ghost Becca and Cullen locate and bind in the soul-binding ritual — the spectral 'price' that lets Becca enter the Void shackled to him and bargain Trisha's soul back without a living human sacrifice. A glimpse of what lingers after the Void takes someone.

title: Time is a Flat Circle
teaser: A dying man whose every parallel life collapses into one, and the angel who walks him out.
body: A quiet, philosophical entry in the Shared Thread, narrated by an angel. Larry Lizer — a chronically ill retail worker who has lived countless parallel lives across the multiverse — finds those lives collapsing into a single body as he nears death. The angel Quieriel arrives to tell him this is his LAST life: the one where he ceases to exist entirely rather than recurring. Against that, Larry's small final days (a tentative bond with Sabrina the donut-shop owner and her daughter Melle) become the whole point. A meditation on mortality, insignificance, and meaning.

title: Larry Lizer
teaser: An ordinary dying man living a thousand lives at once.
body: A forty-year-old chronically ill retail worker — mono, cancer survivor, no family, no great ambition — who is, unknown to those around him, the convergence point of his own self across a trillion lifetimes and universes. As his illness worsens he slips between those lives, until the angel Quieriel tells him this incarnation is his last. Deliberately ordinary: not a hero, just a good-hearted man trying to face death with a little grace.

title: Quieriel
teaser: The angel who shepherds the dying out of existence.
body: An angel whose job is to appear, unbidden, to those at the end of their final life and guide them through dying — facilitating, never interceding, unless the candidate asks (via a coin he leaves them). Wry and weary after shepherding countless souls across countless worlds and timelines, he narrates Larry's story. His role gives an in-thread, ground-level view of the cosmic machinery of life, death, and recurrence.

title: Sabrina & Melle
teaser: The donut-shop owner and her daughter who give Larry a last reason.
body: Sabrina runs the donut shop across from Larry's apartment — kind, honest, quietly generous (she gives her day-old donuts to a shelter). With her sharp, talkative daughter Melle, she becomes the human connection Larry almost refuses in his final days. Their ordinary warmth is the book's answer to the vastness of the multiverse: the small thing done well.

title: Delilah Clark
teaser: A Harvard-bound girl who turns detective to clear her dead father.
body: A fiercely driven, sardonic sixteen-year-old whose single goal is Harvard — until her father's death derails everything. Convinced his 'suicide' was murder, she throws herself into investigating it, manipulating adults, breaking into his workplace, and chasing financial evidence, all while concealing her own grief-driven breakdown. Brilliant, reckless, and grieving, she ultimately uncovers the truth about her father and makes it to Harvard.

title: Alex Dewitt
teaser: Delilah's gymnast best friend and co-narrator.
body: Delilah's loyal best friend, a gifted gymnast benched by her coach, who narrates parts of the diary and stays at Delilah's side through the investigation and her hospitalizations. The steady, grounding presence against Delilah's spiraling obsession.

title: Samuel
teaser: A chronically ill boy who narrates his own brutal survival.
body: The narrator of Sorry for Existing: a chronically ill teen worn down by his father's violence, his grandfather Pop's cruelty, relentless illness, and the pity of everyone around him. Sardonic and self-loathing, he wrestles with suicidal thoughts — but his friend Frank and the alien Yva pull him, often against his will, toward living more than he thought his body could bear.

title: Yva
teaser: An alien hiding in plain sight, from a world destroyed eleven times.
body: 'Hurricane Yva' — an alien who hides in plain sight (unnoticed even by a stock boy) and befriends Samuel, freely admitting she manipulates him for her own ends. She hails from a home world destroyed and rebuilt eleven times over, each iteration engineering away the last catastrophe. She goads Samuel into walking farther, staying out later, doing more than his illness should allow — the force that makes him stronger.

title: Stuart Greenbaum
teaser: An ordinary kid who dreams of being a pulp-comic detective.
body: A thirteen-year-old with a single obsession: sleuthing like his hero, the fedora-wearing pulp detective Dan Dash. Unremarkable at school and overlooked by classmates, Stuart runs 'the Gumshoes' detective agency and finally gets a real case when Madison's father is abducted — and proves himself by helping crack it.

title: Timothy
teaser: Stuart's hyper-logical, gadget-building partner.
body: Stuart's brilliant, precise, perpetually-hungry partner in the Gumshoes — building centrifuges and spectrometers in the tree house and supplying the deductive firepower Stuart lacks. Dry, literal, and often at odds with Madison, he's the brains to Stuart's heart.

title: Madison
teaser: The popular classmate whose abducted father brings the case.
body: A well-off, popular girl who turns to the Gumshoes when her father is abducted. Braver and more headstrong than the boys expect, she refuses to sit safe — confronting the kidnapper Otis herself — and, once her father is saved, repays Stuart and Timothy with genuine loyalty.

title: The Marked Ones
teaser: In a city that ghettoizes magic, a hidden girl turns out to be its key.
body: A dystopian fantasy and its own thread. In the city of Ambrosia, magic users are forced into lightless ghettos and hunted by the Royal Military Police after a war, and history itself has been quietly rewritten. Rosie — raised among the 'Normals' by a woman she calls Mama — was secretly handed off as a baby by magic-user parents to hide until adulthood. When she's exposed, she's smuggled to the hidden walled city of Toledo, discovers she's a rare 'Dual' (wielding both Light and Water), and ultimately completes a cosmic task a predecessor failed: unleashing a blue light that makes everyone magical, ending the war and the persecution.

title: Rosie (Roselyn)
teaser: A 'Normal' girl who is secretly a Dual and the city's salvation.
body: A curious, rule-following girl raised in poverty by Mama among the Normals, hidden from the truth of her birth. Exposed as a suspected magic user, she flees to Toledo and learns she is a Dual — bearing both the Sun-mark of Light and the Moon-mark of Water — and the granddaughter of Toledo's Chief Justice Abalos. She becomes the one who succeeds where Fiona failed, unlocking magic for all.

title: Toledo (the Walled City)
teaser: A hidden city of magic behind an illusion of old-world whimsy.
body: A concealed, barrier-cloaked city of magic users, run with deliberately antiquated whimsy — typewriters, floating paperwork, illusionist-faked sunlight, labyrinthine halls built to madden intruders — ruled through the Tuppins and Chief Justice Abalos. A refuge from the RMP persecution and Rosie's destination after fleeing Ambrosia.

title: Duals (Light & Water)
teaser: Rare mages who wield two opposed magics — Sun and Moon.
body: In this thread, magic users bear a glowing cheek-mark tied to their discipline (healers, seers, illusionists, and so on). A Dual is the rare one who carries two: the Sun-mark of Light/fire on one cheek and the Moon-mark of Water on the other. Rosie is a Dual, and that doubled nature is central to her power and her role.

title: Chief Justice Abalos
teaser: Toledo's ruler — and Rosie's grandfather.
body: The Chief Justice who governs the hidden city of Toledo from its labyrinthine City Hall. Tibor's revelation that Rosie is Abalos's granddaughter is what spares her as a captured 'heretic' and ties her to the city's power structure.

title: The Cloud Queen & Fiona's Device
teaser: A sky-realm queen whose envoy was meant to make humanity magical.
body: A statuesque queen of a cloud-realm who sent her envoy Fiona to Earth to teach humans they could unlock the universe's power by mastering their own minds — or, failing that, to use a device that grants magic to all at the cost of the wielder's life. Fiona failed (an earlier failure was 'Gomorrah'); Rosie completes the task, the blue light making everyone magical and rendering the war pointless.

title: Invasion
teaser: A misanthrope falls for an alien on a family road trip — then the invasion starts.
body: A sci-fi comedy and its own thread. Joshy Carter — an eighteen-year-old gamer who can't stand other humans — is dragged on a cross-country family road trip and, in Las Vegas, falls in love with Debra, who turns out to be a Globorian: an alien who can shed her human skin to become a streak of blue light. Her family is hiding on Earth, and when Debra is exposed on live TV, it spirals into a fugitive chase and a full-blown starship battle against the Globorian fleet, with Joshy's ordinary family caught in the middle.

title: Joshy Carter
teaser: An eighteen-year-old misanthrope who falls for an alien.
body: A meek, sardonic gamer who'd rather be home with his PlayStation than anywhere near other people — 'of all the things Joshy disliked, humans were at the top of the list.' Dragged on a family road trip, he unexpectedly falls for Debra in Vegas, discovers she's an alien, and is pulled out of his shell into a fugitive run and an interstellar fight he never wanted.

title: Debra
teaser: Joshy's love — a Globorian who becomes a streak of blue light.
body: The girl Joshy falls for in Vegas, secretly a Globorian: she can melt away her human form to become a being of blue light. Her family hides among humans on Earth; when she's exposed on live television, she's thrust from a nervous teen into a fighter defending Joshy's family through the chase and the battle that follows.

title: The Globorians
teaser: The light-bodied alien race hiding on — and hunting — Earth.
body: An advanced alien species who can pass as human and revert to bodies of light. Some, like Debra's family, hide quietly on Earth; their authorities (with embassies, SWAT teams, and a battle fleet) enforce secrecy ruthlessly, abducting or eliminating those who expose them. The escalating Globorian response is the 'invasion' the title promises.

title: Tara
teaser: A human raised among aliens, fighting for vengeance.
body: A human abducted from her people and raised among the aliens, who lost the one alien who cared for her (Randall). Driven by rage at the Globorians, she becomes a hardened fighter in the climactic assault — the tactical edge in the battle to seize the Globorian ship's bridge.

title: White Rabbit & Black Jack (Wonderland)
teaser: A noir crime duology in a drug-soaked, fallen Wonderland.
body: The two books of the Wonderland thread — a hardboiled, adult reimagining of Wonderland as a corrupt city decades after the Red Queen's fall. White Rabbit and its sequel Black Jack follow NARCO detective Alice Liddell through addiction, guilt, drug cartels, and political conspiracy. Wonderland here is grimy and broken: the reality-bending drug 'White Rabbit' (once the Red Queen's gift, piped through the water) is now black-market poison, and the Looking Glass Lounge is its rotten heart.

source.real: Carroll's Wonderland — the White Rabbit, the Red Queen, the Cheshire Cat, the looking-glass — is the public-domain dreamscape of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865) and Through the Looking-Glass (1871), a world of nonsense-logic and talking creatures.
source.weave: The Weave's White Rabbit and Black Jack reimagine Wonderland as a corrupt noir city decades after the Red Queen's fall, following NARCO detective Alice — the public-domain dreamscape rebuilt as hardboiled crime fiction.

title: Alice Liddell
teaser: A guilt-wracked NARCO detective indebted to a drug lord.
body: The narrator of the Wonderland thread: a narcotics detective haunted by having shot a child, Timothy Leary, during a botched bust, and by her own addiction to White Rabbit. To keep her badge she strikes a devil's bargain with the drug lord Caterpillar, owing him her loyalty. In Black Jack she's exiled to a quiet northern precinct but is dragged back into Wonderland's corruption — and a political conspiracy around the 'White Queen.' Her sister Dinah and the reporter Arthur orbit her.

source.real: Alice is the heroine of Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865) and Through the Looking-Glass (1871) — the curious girl who falls into a nonsense-world of talking animals and mad logic. (The name nods to Alice Liddell, the real child for whom Carroll invented the stories.) Both books are public domain.
source.weave: The Weave's Alice Liddell narrates a hardboiled, adult Wonderland — a narcotics detective addicted to 'White Rabbit,' haunted and hunted in a corrupt city decades after the Red Queen's fall. It takes Carroll's curious girl and the Wonderland cast and noir-ifies them: the rabbit-hole as addiction, Wonderland as a fallen metropolis.
source.work: Lewis Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865)

title: White Rabbit (the drug)
teaser: The reality-bending narcotic that built and broke Wonderland.
body: A powerful hallucinogen — 'Rabbit' — that makes users see the bright, whimsical Wonderland of legend. Once the Red Queen piped it through the city's water so everyone lived in blissful illusion; after her overthrow it became illegal, and a black-market scourge nobody can stamp out. Chasing it is the thread's literal and metaphorical 'chasing the dragon.'

source.real: The White Rabbit is the waistcoated, watch-checking creature whose rabbit-hole Alice follows into Wonderland in Carroll's 1865 book — the threshold-guide into the dream-world.
source.weave: The Weave's 'White Rabbit' is the narcotic that pulls Alice into the noir Wonderland — literalizing 'down the rabbit-hole' as addiction. The drug takes the name and function of Carroll's guide-creature: the thing that leads you in.
source.work: Lewis Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865)

title: The Red Queen (deposed)
teaser: Wonderland's ousted ruler, remembered as its lost golden age.
body: The former monarch of Wonderland, overthrown three decades ago in the Lory Coup. Under her rule the populace lived high and happy on White Rabbit piped through the water — a 'gay old time' that nostalgics pine for, even as it was mass narcosis. Her fall ushered in the grim, sober, broken Wonderland the books inhabit.

title: Caterpillar
teaser: The drug lord who owns Alice's soul.
body: A powerful, drawling Wonderland crime boss operating out of the Looking Glass Lounge. He leverages Alice's desperation to keep her badge into a binding debt, making her his inside woman on the force — the 'devil' she bargained with, whose wrath shadows everyone she cares about.

title: The Looking Glass Lounge
teaser: Wonderland's notorious drug club — site of legendary ODs.
body: The seediest, most famous nightclub in Wonderland, a drug-and-dance hotbed since before the Red Queen's fall and home to its most infamous overdoses. Caterpillar runs his operation from its stage; it serves as the dark heart of both books.

title: Arthur
teaser: Alice's lover — a reporter 'literally from the twenties.'
body: A wry newspaper reporter and Alice's lover in Black Jack, who speaks like — and claims to literally be — a reporter from the 1920s. Evasive and connected, he becomes entangled in the political-blackmail conspiracy (Councilwoman Lane, Jack Fowler, the 'White Queen') that drives the sequel.

source.real: In the Wonderland thread Arthur is Alice's lover — a wry reporter who claims to be literally from the 1920s. The name is common; he is not the Arthurian king, but a noir character within the Carroll-derived world.
source.weave: An original noir figure inside the Weave's Wonderland — distinct from King Arthur. Noted to keep him from being mis-sourced to the Matter of Britain.

title: Uriel (the Voice)
teaser: The archangel revealed to have been the Voice all along.
body: In the Ichabod RPG, the disembodied Voice that guided and possessed Ichabod is revealed to be the archangel Uriel, sheltering inside him. At the climax Uriel tears free to unmake a wall of hellfire alongside Samael, then walks the road with Ichabod in a borrowed, ill-fitting human shape. The reveal recasts the entire 'savior, master, or madness?' mystery: the thing that sounded demonic was holiness incarnate the whole time.

source.real: Uriel ('light/fire of God') is one of the chief archangels in extra-biblical tradition, prominent in the Book of Enoch as a guide who reveals cosmic and celestial secrets to Enoch. Often the archangel of wisdom, light, and the watchful eye over the world.
source.weave: The Weave's Uriel is the disembodied Voice sheltering inside Ichabod, guiding and possessing him — taking the Enochic revealer-archangel and making him a literal indwelling guide, the secret voice within the host.

title: Samael (in Cathy)
teaser: The archangel carried by Cathy, partner to Uriel.
body: In the Ichabod RPG, Cathy is revealed to carry the archangel Samael, mirroring Ichabod's Uriel. Samael — who taught Ichabod the old reflex of reaching for the knife — gently stays his hand at the end, and remains afterward in a borrowed human shape, telling Ichabod 'the thing about the four.' One of the two angels who unmake the hellfire at the climax.

source.real: Samael ('venom/poison of God') is a fearsome archangel of Jewish tradition — accuser, angel of death, and in some texts a chief of the fallen. An ambiguous figure: a great angel whose office is severity and death, sometimes cast as the dark counterpart to the benevolent archangels.
source.weave: The Weave mirrors Uriel with Samael: Cathy carries Samael as Ichabod carries Uriel, and Samael 'taught Ichabod the old reflex of reaching for the knife.' It keeps Samael's edge — the angel of death and severity — as the darker indwelling counterpart.

title: Valac, Duke of Hell
teaser: A minor, vain hoarder among the Six Dukes — target of a heist.
body: In the Ichabod RPG, Valac is one of the Dukes of Hell: minor, vain, and a hoarder, alone with his trophies for a thousand years. His castle is infiltrated not by the suicidal front gate but through the servants' warren, where vanity is law and anything behaving 'like a hero' is reported. His self-obsession is the opening the party exploits to steal what he guards.

title: The Enochiad
teaser: The spell that closes the door Hell came through.
body: In the Ichabod RPG, the Enochiad is the spell that ends the Apocalypse — the words that close the door Hell invaded through. Taught in Venice by a man who waited four hundred years for someone who could survive arriving, it cannot merely be read: saying it the first time nearly turns the speaker inside out, leaving them bleeding from the eyes. Beelzebub notes it is also 'the key to a throne' for anyone so inclined — the rare door where the thing that empties you is the thing that saves everyone.

title: The Mirror of Lilith
teaser: A standing mirror that is a doorway into Hell — and through time.
body: In the Ichabod RPG, the Mirror of Lilith stands upright in a dry lakebed, framed in something neither wood nor bone. It does not reflect the lakebed but a red country under a wounded sky, with a city far below — the way into Hell, where 'the things in your head have addresses.' Near death and near a Duke's power, the Mirror also comes unstuck in time, sending Ichabod falling backward through his own life. Necromonica leads him to it.

title: Dragon Strife (the saga)
teaser: A generations-long rebellion against the age of dragons, won the long way.
body: A multi-generation story set within the Obsidian Spindle Saga thread, told interactively in the Dragon Strife game. In an age when dragons rule and the gods are gone, a rare northern magic-user named Sintia escapes a dragon prison and becomes the hidden architect of a rebellion she can never publicly lead — building a secret 'railroad' and a legend across decades. It runs from her prison breakout through the Fall of the great rising to its culmination generations later, when Ophelia steals the lore-book that can bring the gods back and the age of dragons ends — not in slaughter, but in the dragon-queen Ramidion choosing to call her soldiers off.

title: Sintia
teaser: The erkurios who orchestrates a rebellion from the shadows — and whose magic has no floor.
body: A northerner and an erkurios (magic-user) — a combination so rare it makes her precious and hunted. Recruited by Gilda during her escape from the Great Gate prison, she becomes 'the hand' behind the rebellion: she cannot swing the sword or show her face, so she wins the long way, through other hands and across years, building a twelve-year 'railroad' network. Raised to fear that her power has a floor — a bottom of the blood where it runs out — she spends the saga mastering control, until, cornered with a dragon on the stair, she reaches past the floor and finds none: more power than a god holds pours through her and she tears a dragon in half, a thing said to be killable only by another dragon. After the Fall she holds the whole hidden machine together alone.

title: Gilda the Unbreakable
teaser: The public face of the rebellion — bait, legend, and Ophelia's mother.
body: A scarred-jaw woman who recruits Sintia at the Great Gate breakout, sensing the tool she's been hunting. She becomes the rebellion's face — riding into firelit halls to raise armies, her name on the dragons' wanted-lists — knowing she is bait. Captured at the Fall of the great rising, presumed dead, her capture buys the secret that keeps the dragon-killer hidden and the rebellion alive. Revealed at the climax to be alive, freed at last, and to be Ophelia's mother — 'the Unbreakable returned from the dead to the woman who never knew she lived.'

title: Ophelia
teaser: Gilda's daughter, who carries a dead goddess's soul and ends the age of dragons.
body: A later-generation heroine who infiltrates the Wicked Witch Academy at Saint Agnes to steal the lore-book that can bring back the gods and end the dragons — letting herself be taken, a jade bracer clamped on to dull her power. Inside, against instinct, she finds friends (Frida, Celeste, Sylvia, Rori) and frees the helpless, as her bloodline always does. Carrying a dead goddess's soul in her veins, she stands at the burning capital at the Reckoning, ready to bring back the gods by force — and is met not by a last battle but by the dragon-queen's surrender.

title: Ramidion
teaser: Greatest of the dragons, whose century reign ends in a chosen peace.
body: The mightiest dragon, whose hundred-year reign is the only world anyone alive has known. At the Reckoning, having watched her rule only worsen across a century, she does the thing no one in the long war expected: she calls her soldiers off, meeting Gilda the Unbreakable from the other side of the war at the same conclusion — that there is a chance of peace. The age of dragons ends not in blood but in her refusal to keep it going.

title: The Great Gate
teaser: The dragon prison whose breach begins everything.
body: A massive dragon-run prison. When its east wall 'leaves' in a roar of dust and cold air, the breakout scatters the inmates — and in the chaos Gilda finds Sintia, the prisoner who lit up the mess hall with a spell she couldn't afford. The breach is the saga's first move; years later the Great Gate is taken again as a turn of the war.

title: Nhilvarna
teaser: The cold northern city that made Sintia — and sold her.
body: The gray, cold northern city of Sintia's origin: where she counted coppers toward her family's freedom and where a baron named Dubhois decided her life was his to spend. She returns to it as 'a ghost coming home,' the city already looking for a gray-lensed woman, to wake the network she came from.

title: Hagswater
teaser: A tithe-town living in the dragons' shadow.
body: A town under the dragons' dominion, defined by cages, tithe-wagons, and a square that boils over — one of the waypoints on Sintia's road and an early picture of life under dragon rule that the rebellion forms against.

anchors.chapter: a town in the dragons\u2019 shadow

title: Saint Agnes & the Wicked Witch Academy
teaser: The emperor's school for breaking witches — and the lore-book's vault.
body: The academy at Saint Agnes: the emperor's own school for breaking witches to his service, where wards are dulled with jade bracers and contracts signed in burning ink. Its archives hold one of the lore-canon books — kept free generations earlier by Sintia — that can bring back the gods and end the dragons. Ophelia lets herself be taken into it to steal that book.

title: The Railroad (the hidden network)
teaser: Sintia's underground network — cells, runners, and the safe book.
body: The secret rebellion infrastructure Sintia spends twelve years hardening: cells, couriers, village casters learning their first sigils in hidden rooms, with Fharin running the south and Miss Hectarin watching the palace. Built to survive the loss of its face — when Gilda falls, the railroad holds and goes deeper underground, 'around the wound,' the way Sintia taught it.

title: Fharin
teaser: The rebellion's man in the capital, running the south.
body: A figure won to the cause in the capital's shadow, who runs the southern half of Sintia's network and plants his own agents (such as Frida) inside the emperor's institutions. One of the pillars that keeps the railroad standing after the Fall.

title: Miss Hectarin
teaser: Mistress of an old art of unseen extraction, watching the palace.
body: A practitioner of an old art — the craft of moving people unseen and pulling them out of the empire's heart — who watches the palace for the rebellion. Her 'oldest art' is what later walks Gilda the Unbreakable out of the empire's heart unseen and returns her, alive, to her daughter.

title: Ewig
teaser: The red dragon who turns against his own kind.
body: A red dragon allied to the rebellion — the one who carries the dying fire north with Sintia and, at the Reckoning, flies with his kin over the burning capital on the rebellion's side. A dragon helping to end the age of dragons.

title: The Harvested-Dream Conspiracy
teaser: A Church program stealing dreams and re-tying souls off the Fates' books.
body: A century-long criminal operation uncovered in the Obsidian game, run from within the Cathedral. With the third Fate — Atropos the Cutter — murdered, the hour of each death goes unguarded, and the keeper of the dead seizes the shears to cut threads when he chooses rather than when measured. Under that cover, the Church harvests dreams from living dreamers, bottles them in stamped intake vessels, gathers them in the Well of Gathered Dreams, and ships them 'up the thread' using wrong-minted, dark-god passage-coins to move souls through the nexus — souls re-tied after death by the same hand, entirely off the Fates' books, timed to 'the wall.'

title: Cardinal Vessit
teaser: The cardinal at the head of the dream-harvest operation.
body: A cardinal of the Cathedral who runs the harvested-dream conspiracy from his Sanctum. The tithe-men funnel wrong-minted coin up to Vessit and never ask questions; the stolen dreams ship up to him. He sits at the center of the Church's machinery for trafficking souls and dreams through the broken guardianship of the Fates.

title: The Well of Gathered Dreams
teaser: Where the Church pools its harvested dreams.
body: A reservoir deep in the Cathedral complex (near the Blessing Altar and the Reliquary Vault) where dreams harvested from living dreamers are gathered before being shipped up the thread. The physical heart of the conspiracy's supply chain.

title: The Wrong-Minted Passage-Coin
teaser: A dark-god coin that moves souls through the nexus.
body: A passage-coin 'like nothing this realm strikes' — dark-god-minted and wrong-minted — used to return and move souls through the nexus, off the Fates' books. The tithe-men funnel these coins up to Cardinal Vessit. A documented trace of one is among the proofs that expose the conspiracy.

title: The Proof Chain
teaser: The documented evidence exposing the dream-and-soul trafficking.
body: The body of hard evidence the investigation assembles against the Cathedral conspiracy: falsified ledger entries, dock and order records, intake manifests, a traced passage-coin, and documented proof of souls re-tied after death by the same hand — a century-long program of tampered threads timed to the wall. Together this proof chain is what can expose Cardinal Vessit and the keeper of the dead.

title: The Road to Reno (Rose's resurrection)
teaser: A resurrected dreamer hunted across the desert toward Reno.
body: A present-day strand of the Obsidian game: a resurrected dreamer — Rose — must be kept alive to the end of the road to Reno, because something owed her soul is hunting her. A driverless car tries to run her down on an empty desert road, a deliberate death dressed as an accident, spoiled only by taking the hit for her. The chase ties the dream-harvest conspiracy to the dreamer at the saga's center.

title: Apollo
teaser: An Olympian hiding on Earth among unknowing worshippers.
body: In the Godsverse game, one of the Olympians — proud and sun-bright, almost certainly Apollo — is hiding on Earth, living among people who worship him without realizing what he is. A Godschurch agent is sent to capture rather than kill him, the trick being to find the god before the god finds the agent.

title: Kali
teaser: A sheikh's wife who quietly runs his house.
body: In the Godsverse game, the wife of a sheikh who holds a jeweled scimitar relic. While her husband snores, Kali watches from the dark, amused — she truly runs the house and despises the man in it, making her the key to getting through it.

title: Emiri
teaser: Keeper of a black door that shows on no map.
body: In the Godsverse game, the keeper guarding a black metal door in Istanbul that appears on no map. An agent must find the door, get past Emiri, and escape through a city full of hunting demons.

title: Hjilin
teaser: The tower-keeper in the Library of the Night.
body: In the Godsverse game, a gatekeeper figure encountered in the tower stage of the Library of the Night, standing between the agent and the cult sanctum beyond.

title: Hogarth
teaser: A caravaneer whose supply run reaches the gate of Hell.
body: In the Godsverse game, the operator of a supply caravan that runs through bandit country toward Hell. The Church can drop an agent into Hell but not past the gate Petrus guards — so the agent rides Hogarth's caravan and talks their way through.

title: Jared
teaser: A demon who fences a stolen god-killing relic in Brussels.
body: In the Godsverse game, a demon who takes a curved, ruby-hilted relic blade to Brussels to flip it — giving the agent roughly a week to recover it. The further the agent reaches from their strengths to prep, the more they come back with.

title: Odahai
teaser: Piggy's lieutenant, handing out the day's dirty work.
body: In the Godsverse game, the lieutenant of a crime boss called Piggy, who drops the daily chore list on the bar: collect debts, send messages with fists, and — last item — kill a fairy-blood informant the Church has spent months trying to reach.

title: Toni
teaser: An agent's handler on a scouting run gone deep.
body: In the Godsverse game, a Godschurch handler who frames a mission to Niloria as a simple scouting run — until the agent finds the Godless hold the full Obelisk plans, and pulling out costs six months the universe doesn't have.

title: Mags
teaser: A contact who sets the terms for facing Odin.
body: In the Godsverse game, a contact who lays out the rules for an off-book approach to Odin: tell no one at the Godschurch, because that's the whole deal. Odin respects nerve, despises flattery, and reads minds older than the agent's pantheon.

title: Dr. Butler
teaser: Ichabod's psychiatrist — who appears in the monster-world leading a church of the dead.
body: In the Ichabod RPG, Dr. Butler is Ichabod's doctor from 'the world where you are sick' — the man from the office with the watch and the clipboard. He appears in the monster-world dead, leading a church of the dead, embodying the game's central ambiguity: the figure from the world where Ichabod is mentally ill, standing in the world where he is a monster hunter, both true at once.

title: The Judge
teaser: Presides over the trial of whether Ichabod knew what he was killing.
body: In the Ichabod RPG, the Judge presides over a courtroom reckoning where the question is not whether Ichabod did these things — that is not in dispute — but whether he knew what they were. The Judge demands a plea, forcing the choice between 'not by reason of insanity' (let them say you were sick) and 'I am a monster' — the game's verdict on its own central question.

title: The Accusers
teaser: The 3am voices of the people Ichabod killed.
body: In the Ichabod RPG, the Accusers are the voices of the dead Ichabod killed — the ones you say to yourself at 3am, in the voices of the people you killed. They demand he admit that on the bus he looked, knew his victim was 'just a man,' and did it anyway. Beelzebub warns not to engage; they feed on it.

title: The Teacher
teaser: Teaches the apocalypse-ending words that kill most who try.
body: In the Ichabod RPG, the Teacher imparts the world-ending/world-beginning words — 'Ex fine, et finis est omne principium' (from the end, and the end is every beginning) — words older than the mouth that says them. They must be said until they stop killing you; most do not get past the third word. Tied to the Enochiad, the spell that closes the door Hell came through.

title: Bishop & Crane
teaser: Heavily-armed men torn apart by the monster.
body: In the Ichabod RPG, Bishop and Crane are among the most heavily armed men in the building — and the monster takes them apart effortlessly, Crane by the head and Bishop in both hands, what holds him together that last second 'not bone.' A demonstration that the wicked cannot destroy the thing, and that firepower is no defense.

title: Thread 28 — Quest Girls
teaser: The fae-and-Hell saga of a cursed Quest Girl and a runaway princess.
body: The thread of the Quest Girls saga (four books: F*ck Fairy, Go to Hell, Gods Damned, Cosmic Bastards), set on a near-present Earth braided with Fairy and Hell. It follows Lacey, an immortal cursed 'Quest Girl,' and Margaret, a princess who summons a demon and is cursed in turn, as they topple a fae regime, descend into Hell's bureaucracy, assault Heaven, and remake the cosmic order. Like every thread it is its own sealed universe; its gods, courts, and underworlds are its own.

title: Quest Girls 1: F*ck Fairy
teaser: A cursed guide and a runaway princess bring down the fae courts.
body: Book 1 of the Quest Girls saga. Lacey, a Quest Girl who fakes heroic adventures for paying nobles, is hired by Princess Margaret — newly cursed after a demon summoning that killed her mother, Queen Celeste. Their quest carries them through the pixie bureaucracy, a fae slave-auction, a prisoners' revolution, the fall of the Summer Court, a corrupted fae democracy, and finally down into Hell's bureaucratic city of Dis. Along the way Lacey and Margaret fall in love, and the wider war to come is set in motion.

title: Lacey (Laceline)
teaser: A 324-year-old cursed Quest Girl who has never killed.
body: An immortal, perpetually-broke 'Quest Girl' — one of a cursed guild who shepherd paying nobles through faked heroic adventures. Her curse grants eternal life but turns every good thing to ash and severs every attachment, so she has survived 324 years by staying lean, sardonic, and alone — and by never, ever killing anyone, the one standard she holds. Cursed by the same demon that later curses Margaret, she falls for the princess despite herself, the bond becoming a forcefield against her own bad luck. She guided Margaret's father, grandfather, and great-grandfather to the dragon G'neth.

title: Princess Margaret
teaser: A runaway princess turned wild-magic conduit.
body: Daughter of Queen Celeste, raised to court politics and empathy ('empathy can be the most powerful weapon'). Refusing a gilded life of pre-approved suitors, she summons a demon and is cursed — the same act that kills her mother. Partnering with Lacey, she discovers she is a conduit for wild magic (taught by Nobody), capable of moving whole buildings between dimensions, and grows from sheltered royal into a fighter who kills when she must. She falls in love with Lacey.

title: Queen Celeste
teaser: Margaret's mother — the real ruler, killed by the demon summoning.
body: The true power behind her drunkard husband's throne, who taught Margaret to fight for herself. Her death — caused by Harry's dealings with demons — is the wound at the saga's heart and the origin of Margaret's curse. She persists as a ghost in Dis, met again on the descent into Hell.

title: Harry (King Innocence's heir)
teaser: Margaret's brother — a fae-bred specimen who dealt with demons.
body: Margaret's insufferable elder brother, revealed to be fairy-born — bred and molded as a specimen for the Pixie Queen before being placed in the mortal royal line. Tutored in shadow magic by the wizard Horace, he deals with demons, an arrangement that kills Queen Celeste. When the demon's spell finally breaks, his full soul and guilt return and crush him.

title: The Name Book
teaser: The pixie hive's book of true names — the key to their power.
body: A dossier holding the true name of every pixie in the hive. Because pixie magic is bound to names, knowing a name strips a pixie's power, making the book the hive's ultimate vulnerability. Stolen by the Summer King; the Pixie Queen hires Lacey and Margaret to recover it. When it is finally burned, every pixie's name-magic unravels at once — destroying the Queen and ending the hive.

title: The Pixie Queen (Lyassa)
teaser: Ruler of the fae hive, undone by her own stolen magic.
body: Queen Lyassa, who runs the pixie hive through ancient etiquette-spells and stolen troll magic, and who hires Lacey and Margaret to recover the Name Book. Mercurial and cruel, she is brought down when the Name Book burns and her people's name-magic fails — though she later survives and reclaims a broken Summer Court amid the demon war.

title: Oliver
teaser: A pureblood troll who topples the fae regime in revenge.
body: The Pixie Queen's weary troll servant — secretly a pureblood troll able to manipulate shadows, a power the pixies feared and suppressed after stealing troll magic and ghettoizing his people. He engineers the Queen's downfall (burning the Name Book), frees the auction's prisoners, and rises to lead the fractious fae council that follows. Murdered by his own brother under Malzeth's influence; the heroes later seek his soul across the thousands of afterlives.

title: The Abyssal Auction
teaser: Fairy's hidden slave-market for trafficked creatures.
body: A vast, shifting auction-house carved into a canyon, where rare and helpless creatures are caged and sold as 'merchandise.' Run on cruelty and overseen by the processor Kryx, it's where Lacey and Margaret are sold, meet Nobody, and spark a prisoners' revolution organized under black-star pins (names forbidden — name-power again).

title: Kryx
teaser: The Abyssal Auction's butcher-processor.
body: The gnarled jailer who 'processes' the auction's captives — appraising, harvesting, and discarding creatures as parts. A petty sadist whose obsidian shard (etched with a black star) becomes a key object, and whose cruelty galvanizes the prisoners' revolt.

title: Nobody (Cassian)
teaser: A broken elf-mathematician who sacrifices himself to undo a curse.
body: An ancient elf met in the auction's cells, a shadow-reader who calls himself 'Nobody' to hide from a past he can't face. Touching the Name Book restores his true name — Cassian — and the memory of being a brilliant mathematician whose perfect equations were twisted into weapons by Aurora's betrayal. He teaches Margaret wild magic, then sacrifices himself working great magic with the Book, remaking how power flows through the fallen Summer Court.

title: Aurora
teaser: The betrayer who twisted Cassian's work into weapons.
body: The figure from Cassian's past who corrupted his pure mathematics into instruments of harm — the betrayal that shattered him into 'Nobody.' Her shadow hangs over his arc and his final sacrifice.

title: G'neth
teaser: The last dragon of the old world, struck from the sky and nursed back to a guardian of the new.
body: A dragon (they/them) whom Lacey has used for generations as the 'dragon' her noble clients pretend to fight — and who becomes a true ally to Lacey and Margaret. Banished long ago from a fae door, G'neth carries the weight of old choices; loyal, dryly funny, and powerful enough to fly between worlds and tear through Fairy's prisons, though their power can be bound (e.g. a magically-fixed hat).

title: Malzeth the Unraveled
teaser: A chaos demon who corrupts the new fae democracy for sport.
body: A demon lord who 'monetizes chaos,' backing Oliver's revolution purely to watch order rot into bureaucratic turmoil. He corrupts the new fae council, keeps a living house stitched from contracts that can trick Hell, and orchestrates Oliver's death — until his own death collapses the house into a sentient being.

title: Horace
teaser: The wizard who tutored Harry and engineered a sacrifice.
body: A scheming wizard who tutors Harry in shadow magic while secretly reshaping the boy's plans toward his own ritual ends — including the sacrifice that ties the mortal king's court to demonic forces. A patient corruptor working several boards at once.

title: Dis (Hell's Bureaucracy)
teaser: Hell as an endless waiting-room of contracts and queue-numbers.
body: The infernal city Lacey and Margaret descend to via a Día-de-los-Muertos portal: not fire and torment but a vast, grinding Bureaucracy where souls hold queue-numbers in the tens of millions and everything runs on contracts and fine print. Home to the Black Market clerks, the demon-lord Bureaucrat Azazel, the Council, and the Grand Central Library — and where the black coin and Hell's ledger become the keys forward.

source.real: The City of Dis in Dante's Inferno is the walled stronghold of lower Hell. The name also recalls Dis Pater, the Roman lord of the dead.
source.weave: The Weave's QG Dis is the infernal city reached via a Día-de-los-Muertos portal — not fire but a grinding Bureaucracy with queue-numbers in the tens of millions. Dante's walled Hell reimagined as the ultimate DMV, the same city as a different thread's satire.

title: Azazel
teaser: A weary demon-lord Bureaucrat of Hell.
body: A demon lord who has worked Hell's Bureaucracy for seven hundred years and is thoroughly over it — powerful, sardonic, and bound by the Council's endless protocol. He points Lacey toward Zir'kael to decode the ledger and becomes an uneasy ally against the Bureaucracy's deeper machinations.

title: Zir'kael Alzah'ar
teaser: A rogue demon scribe who decodes Hell's ledger.
body: A clever, slippery demon scribe (golden-eyed, silent-footed) whom Lacey recruits to decode Hell's ledger — every transcribed letter an act of rebellion against the Bureaucracy. Enslaved by the Bureaucracy for a time, his first act on freedom is not revenge but to lead the heroes to the truth.

title: The Black Coin
teaser: A coin of absence that hides its bearer in Hell.
body: A cool, impossibly smooth coin that seems less an object than a piece of absence — it reflects nothing, absorbs light, and bends shadows around it. It hides its bearer from Hell's watchers, making it invaluable for moving unseen through Dis.

title: Hell's Ledger
teaser: A shifting-text codex of Hell's contracts.
body: A leather-bound ledger written in a shifting amalgam of dialects and languages, holding the deep workings of Hell's contract-magic. Cursed to whoever opens it carelessly, it must be painstakingly transcribed and decoded (by Zir'kael) to unlock the secrets the heroes need against the Bureaucracy and the Council.

title: The Council (of Hell)
teaser: Hell's flickering, half-present ruling body.
body: The shadowy ruling Council of Hell — silhouettes that are 'not truly present but unmistakably there,' summoning supplicants to doors that appear from nowhere. Obsessed with protocol and contracts, they govern through signatures and fine print, and become the saga's looming institutional antagonist.

title: Lady Vash
teaser: A vampire noble who escapes execution to fight the regime.
body: An imposing, effortless vampire noble framed and nearly publicly executed by the fae council's paranoia (stoked by Malzeth). Freed, she allies with G'neth, marks Lacey with a lingering spell, and joins the hunt for a way to undo Malzeth's living house — playing both sides with cool self-interest.

title: Maison (the House)
teaser: The clay homunculus whose 'betrayal' was the plan that saved everyone.
body: Malzeth's house was never just a house — a living network of contracts and shadow stitched together by a mind clever enough to trick Hell. When Malzeth dies it begins to die too, and is ultimately given a deliberately forgettable humanoid form by an artist (with Professor Vehr). In the epilogue it lives quietly as 'Maison,' free at last of contracts and lost souls.

title: Vivian
teaser: Lacey's ghostly sister, a charming, untrustworthy fixer in Hell.
body: Lacey's older sister, now a ghost running a den in Dis between a ruined temple and a gambling hall. Centuries ago she traded Lacey away in a demon deal for eternal youth — the original wound behind Lacey's curse — and calls her 'Bean.' Slippery, theatrical, and self-admittedly a serial betrayer, she nonetheless risks everything for family: she sacrifices her voice in Dis to save them, fakes a betrayal under torture to steal Hell's Ledger back from Azazel, and uses an old 'nonexistence' tattoo to slip the Bureaucracy's records entirely.

title: Dr. Ilvane
teaser: A fearless gnome scientist of reality-distortion fields.
body: A tiny, brilliant, perpetually fascinated gnome scholar of reality-distortion who is incapable of being afraid when she could be taking data instead. Recruited by Lady Vash and G'neth to study Malzeth's living house, she argues it should not be 'fixed' but allowed to become — and proposes the illegal soul-transference that ultimately gives the house a body. Her catchphrase is that science is risky, and that's what makes it fun.

title: Professor Callidus Vehr
teaser: A Solmara scholar of soul-transference who befriends a living house.
body: A tall, silver-haired professor at the magic university Solmara and the Shadow Court's secret, illegal researcher into soul-transference and homunculi. Granted immunity by Queen Lyassa, he is brought to move the living house's soul into a vessel — but instead chooses to simply talk to it, win its trust, and stay. He guides the house to choose its own plain, ordinary body and casts the rune-work that finally makes it real.

title: Captain Firebrand
teaser: The flame-haired captain who speaks for Queen Lyassa.
body: A sharp, flame-haired captain of the Summer Court who speaks with the queen's authority and isn't eager to defend any decision to Lyassa's face. Skeptical of Vash and G'neth's warnings until she admits she has felt the realm's 'anomalies' herself — shadows stretching wrong, magic misfiring, echoes of things that never happened.

title: Warden Stonegrit
teaser: The no-nonsense dwarf warden of the Summer Court prison.
body: The prototype-dwarf warden of the Summer Court's magic-choked prison — brutal, prickly, and utterly bound to her ledger. To Stonegrit, a prisoner is simply an entry: in the book means imprisoned, off the book means free, and a princess 'and a bag of beans gets you the start of a decent chili.' (Distinct from Stonebind, a separate wall-listening magic.)

title: The Black Market Clerk
teaser: A ledger-faced fixer in Dis who trades in stolen things — like a voice.
body: A ledger-faced black-market fixer operating in the city of Dis who deals in the impossible and the stolen. It is to this clerk that Vivian sacrifices her voice, and the clerk who first names Vivian and Celeste aloud, pulling the sisters' and Margaret's mother's hidden histories into the open.

title: The Records Clerk
teaser: Malzeth's mole in the Records Department — and the key to Hell itself.
body: A middle-manager buried in Hell's Records Department with rare triplicate clearance, and Malzeth's mole inside the Bureaucracy. He reveals that every contract exists in three copies across three record rooms, and that the system only dies if all three are destroyed at once — handing Lacey a silver, skull-inlaid key that opens all three. Azazel kills him mid-sentence to keep the secret, but the key survives.

title: Vinderhall
teaser: The Bureaucracy clerk who can't stop a citation he can't refute.
body: A thin, spectacled Bureaucracy clerk (Clerk 62185762148) who denies Lacey and Margaret's request to escalate their case — until Margaret cites Section 22, Sub-Clause D of the Bureaucratic Conduct Act, which lets any living being escalate a matter of legal significance on request. Defeated by his own rulebook, he concedes they are 'technically correct, which is the only valid way of being correct,' and leads them to Management.

title: Marie Laveau
teaser: The ghost of the Voodoo Queen, met in New Orleans.
body: The spirit of New Orleans's legendary Voodoo Queen, encountered during the heroes' detour through the ghost-thick city. One of the dead guides and power-brokers who populate the novel's New Orleans arc alongside Baron Samedi.

source.real: Marie Laveau (c. 1801–1881) was a real historical figure — the renowned Voodoo Queen of New Orleans, a free woman of color, healer, and spiritual leader whose influence over the city's Voodoo practice became legendary. Her tomb in St. Louis Cemetery No. 1 remains a pilgrimage site. She is history that became folklore: a real person now woven into the spirit-world of New Orleans.
source.weave: The Weave's Marie Laveau is 'the spirit of New Orleans's legendary Voodoo Queen,' a dead guide and power-broker in the city's ghost arc — taking the real historical figure and seating her among the loa as a power in the afterlife.

title: Baron Samedi
teaser: The top-hatted loa of the dead, encountered in New Orleans.
body: The grinning, top-hatted loa of death and the crossroads, one of the supernatural powers the heroes deal with during the New Orleans leg of their journey. A reminder that this world's afterlives are many, overlapping, and each runs by its own rules.

source.real: Baron Samedi — loa of death and the graveyard, head of the Gede, top-hatted and rum-soaked, who guards the threshold between life and death. In New Orleans Voodoo he is among the most invoked and feared of spirits.
source.weave: The Weave places him among the dead guides and power-brokers of its ghost-thick New Orleans arc, alongside the historical Marie Laveau — keeping his role as the irreverent lord of the graveyard.

title: Druscilla
teaser: A figure tied to the Quest Girls' guild and curse.
body: A figure connected to the cursed guild of Quest Girls and the web of demon deals that bind Lacey and her sisters in the trade. Part of the older history the curse drags behind it.

title: Douglas ('El')
teaser: Known to Laceline by the nickname 'El.'
