body: A figure from Lacey's long life who calls her by, and is known to her through, the nickname 'El' — one of the few threads of genuine connection a 324-year-old cursed woman has managed to keep.

title: The Summer Court
teaser: The golden, blood-stained seat of Fairy's power.
body: The opulent golden court of the Pixie Queen Lyassa, all marble pillars and light from no visible source. After the coup and reconquest its grandeur is an illusion stretched thin over fresh repairs and never-quite-erased bloodstains — a throne reclaimed by force, not inherited. Later the staging ground for Lyassa's Queen's Council.

title: Malzeth's House
teaser: A demon's paranoid construct that wakes up after his death.
body: Malzeth the Unraveled's estate: not mere stone and mortar but a layered construct of contracts, bindings, and stolen magic, built to persist. When Malzeth dies and his contracts unravel, the orphaned house destabilizes, then 'becomes' — a sentient, shifting, breathing structure that calls Lacey and Margaret 'mother.' It later chooses a body and becomes Maison; the now-safe, void-floating shell is repurposed as the Name-Book library.

title: The Mall in Dis
teaser: A too-intact shopping mall in the ghost-town of Hell.
body: An eerily functional, self-aware shopping mall standing intact amid the decay of Dis, where Margaret's mother Celeste is found 'shopping.' Lacey and Margaret squat an empty storefront here and run a free-money-for-information shop — exploiting that, being alive, they can mint soul-coins by breathing — to flush out Azazel's covert operative.

title: The Grand Central Library
teaser: Hell's celestial library, where the law hides its loopholes.
body: A vast, intimidating library in Dis built in the Bureaucracy's perfect, sterile order — its motto: 'Knowledge Without Error. Access Without Chaos. Order Above All.' Zir'kael's hidden ledger clue (a Dewey-style number) leads here, to a law book whose buried clause becomes the heroes' legal weapon against the Bureaucracy.

title: Solmara
teaser: The living magic university, its arches carved with every scholar's name.
body: A sentient university of magic whose architecture shifts and judges, its great archway carved with the names of every scholar who ever passed through. Home to Professor Vehr and his forbidden soul-transference research; where the first homunculus soul-transfer is attempted.

title: Oaxaca & the Ofrenda Gate
teaser: A marigold archway that opens the road into Hell.
body: The living-world waypoint where, guided by Arturo, the heroes use a Day-of-the-Dead ofrenda and its marigold archway as a literal gate — the threshold they cross to step down into the Underworld. Site of key reunions before the descent.

source.real: The ofrenda of Día de los Muertos is the marigold-laden altar by which Mexican tradition opens a path for the dead to return for a day; the marigold's scent and color guide the souls, whose journey runs through the nine levels of the Aztec underworld Mictlán. Oaxaca is the heartland of the celebration. The altar as a literal doorway between living and dead.
source.weave: The Weave's Oaxaca & Ofrenda Gate makes the belief literal: the heroes use a Day-of-the-Dead ofrenda and its marigold archway as an actual gate down into the Underworld — taking the real tradition's flower-path-for-the-dead and turning it into a working portal.
source.work: Día de los Muertos tradition (Aztec/Nahua roots)

title: New Orleans
teaser: A ghost-thick city of loa, voodoo queens, and old debts.
body: A waypoint city dense with the dead and the divine, where the heroes treat with spirits like Marie Laveau and Baron Samedi. One stop on a journey that makes plain how many separate afterlives and powers crowd this world.

title: The Pits Beneath Dis
teaser: The hidden Hell beneath Hell, where defiant demons are broken.
body: An underground network of suffering beneath the marble offices of Dis, where demons deemed unfit for clerical work are chained and worked until broken — the Bureaucracy's quiet engine of submission. Zir'kael labored here; it is the wound at the heart of the demon rebellion.

title: The Jade Dragon
teaser: A trinket on Malzeth's desk that is a bound dragon.
body: A small jade dragon figurine kept on Malzeth's desk — secretly a full-sized dragon bound into miniature form. G'neth, who was alive when it was large, knows its true name; he trades that name to Lady Vash, who shatters the figurine to unleash the dragon and rides it out of prison in an emerald-fire jailbreak, and again to blast free of the living house.

title: The Skull Key
teaser: A silver, skull-inlaid key that opens all three record rooms.
body: A silver key inlaid with a skull, carried by the Records Clerk, granting access to all three of Hell's triplicate record rooms at once. Whispered to Lacey as the clerk dies, it is the physical means to destroy every contract simultaneously — the literal key to unmaking the Bureaucracy.

title: The Obsidian Blade
teaser: Obsidian bound to one true name, a blade that knows only the Sovereign.
body: An aware obsidian blade forged from something older than Hell, sealed in Malzeth's house. When G'neth's hand nears it, the case bursts and the blade snaps to him as if it has chosen him — taken in the raid that wakes the living house.

title: Malzeth's Coded Ledger
teaser: A living cipher in six languages that can tear realms apart.
body: Malzeth's record of his dealings, written in a shifting cipher that fuses six languages and six magic systems. Experts confirm a code that moves is alive — and this one is alive and breaking apart, rewriting the reality it's tied to. It names everyone who ever fought the Bureaucracy: a kill-list in the wrong hands, a weapon in the right ones.

title: The Nonexistence Tattoo
teaser: Pixie-dust ink that erases you from Hell's records.
body: A sigil tattooed on Vivian in pixie-dust-laced ink that absorbs magic rather than conducting it, warping reality so that to all but the most powerful magic she does not exist. A name unfiled cannot be bound — the loophole that lets her slip the Bureaucracy's tracking entirely and void the black coin's surveillance spell.

title: Name Magic
teaser: Know a true name and you control the named — and their kin.
body: The deep magic of names shared across Fairy and Hell: pixies guard their names, and demons hide theirs by fusing first and family names into one. To know a being's family name is to control them and every relative — the ultimate vulnerability. Zir'kael surrenders his true name to Lacey as a gesture of trust; G'neth wields the jade dragon's name to free it.

title: Soul-Currency of Dis
teaser: In Hell, you spend your soul one coin at a time.
body: The economy of Dis runs on soul-credit: each dead soul is allotted credit by the worth of their soul, and every purchase literally spends a piece of them — run out and you are erased, as if you were never there. The dead ration words and movement to survive. Because Lacey and Margaret are alive, their breath mints coins at no cost, making them walking gold mines the whole city hunts.

title: Soul Transference
teaser: Forbidden magic to move a soul into a crafted vessel.
body: The Shadow Court's illegal science of moving consciousness into homunculi vessels. Souls cling to their containers and fight relocation — which is fatal — so a transfer can only succeed if the soul chooses it. The method that lets the living house leave its walls behind and become Maison.

title: The Triplicate Records
teaser: Every contract in Hell exists three times — destroy all three to void it.
body: The Bureaucracy's power rests on contract magic stored in the Archives. Every contract is written in triplicate across three record rooms, and a contract is not void until all instances are destroyed at once. Destroy all three rooms simultaneously and the whole self-sustaining system collapses — the heroes' 'blow it all up' option, opposite the legal path.

title: The Bureaucracy — Heaven's Leash
teaser: Hell's rulers are angels, and the system was always Heaven's trap.
body: The great reveal: the Bureaucracy that governs Hell is run by angels, not demons — Heaven's leash. After an endless war, Heaven offered Hell's nobility peace if Hell reorganized 'under law'; the nobles signed, Lucifer was declared void by contract and bound in the deepest pit, and Hell signed itself away. The system is self-correcting, with no real loopholes — which is why only the living, the unjudged, can challenge it.

title: The Binding of Lucifer
teaser: Hell's old king, deposed not by force but by contract.
body: Once Hell's sole ruler, Lucifer was overthrown when his own dukes — Azazel among them — accepted Heaven's bargain and reorganized Hell under law. A single celestial contract declared his reign void; he could rage, but he could not burn a contract. He remains bound in the deepest pit, his presence erased from the realm he built.

title: The Petition Clause
teaser: A buried law: the living may petition the Council before death.
body: The legal lever Zir'kael points the heroes to — a clause buried in 'Introduction to Celestial Bureaucracy': prior to their death, any living human may petition the Council to reconsider the conditions of their judgment. Because the living are unjudged, this is the one door the self-correcting system leaves open. The heroes cite it to force their way up the chain to the Council itself.

title: The Queen's Council
teaser: Lyassa's fractured attempt at a democracy of queens.
body: Queen Lyassa's post-war project: a council of every queen across the realm — trolls, goblins, and all — so that power is held by everyone rather than one throne. The closest the realm can get to the democracy Oliver dreamed of, with the Name-Book library as its safeguarded heart and G'neth and Lady Vash as its stewards.

title: The Name-Book Library
teaser: Every name in the realm, guarded by a dragon and a vampire.
body: A single protected repository for all the Name Books — every name and spell woven into the world — housed in Malzeth's now-safe, void-floating house and controlled by everyone because it is controlled by no single court. Lyassa makes G'neth and Lady Vash its stewards: no longer prisoners, but keepers of the most dangerous knowledge in existence.

title: The Many Afterlives
teaser: Not one Hell or Heaven, but thousands, none speaking to each other.
body: Creation holds not a single afterlife but thousands — every culture, realm, and corner of existence running its own, by its own rules, none of them in contact. The Bureaucracy only processes humans who believed in a monotheistic god and died on Earth; a troll like Oliver falls entirely outside its jurisdiction. Oliver is finally found not suffering but happily cooking in a small food-afterlife.

title: The Joint Council
teaser: Heaven, Hell, and humanity forced to share the table.
body: The resolution Margaret and Lacey wring out of the Council: an equal body of angels and demons with humans mediating to break ties — demons gaining a say, angels accepting demons govern themselves (provided the torture of human souls ends), and Oliver, retrieved from his food-afterlife, taking the human mediator's seat. Not a clean victory; the only deal that makes sense.

title: Quest Girls 2: Go to Hell
teaser: A foster kid, a bound devil, and a war for every underworld at once.
body: The second Quest Girls book pulls a twelve-year-old from Earth into the realm of the dead and chains her to Lucifer by a Council geas. What looks like a humiliating parade of Lucifer through the underworlds is really a march to the Forgotten Realms to wake his old allies and break Heaven's occupation of the afterlife. The story crosses Egyptian, Norse, Greek, and Celtic lands of the dead before turning back to retake Hell itself.

title: Emma (Wren)
teaser: The girl the Sovereign never saw coming, who ended a god with a hidden shard.
body: Twelve years old, orphaned, shuffled through dozens of foster homes, Emma steps through a portal expecting anything to be better than the life she's leaving. Instead she is bound to Lucifer by the Council's geas, her body made to mirror his wounds and her fate tied to his. Over the war that follows she becomes its moral center, the one unjudged living soul whose freedom every contract turns on. She is freed when Seraphaniel's masterstroke dissolves the bond, and at the end she is taken in as family.

title: Seraphaniel
teaser: The contract-lawyer of the dead, who wins wars by reading the fine print.
body: A meticulous, cold figure who fights with clauses rather than blades. He exposes Isis's betrayal and blackmails her, finds the loophole that lets Isis end Osiris, and ultimately authors the contract masterstroke that breaks Emma's bond to Lucifer and routs Heaven's legal claim on the underworld in one move. Heaven's counter-suit fails against his drafting. For his trouble he is exiled to Hell, where he settles in as one of Lucifer's genuine friends.

title: Isis
teaser: The queen of the Duat who would trade anyone to keep her own throne standing.
body: Ruler of the Egyptian land of the dead, Isis hosts the parade and swears alliance, then is revealed to have quietly let Heaven occupy allied cities to protect her own realm. Using a loophole in Seraphaniel's contract she ends Osiris. When Seraphaniel uncovers her treachery he turns it into leverage. Her arc is the book's study in how the powerful sell out the vulnerable to survive an occupation.

source.real: Isis is the great Egyptian goddess of magic, motherhood, and the throne — wife of Osiris, who gathers his scattered body after his murder by Set and revives him long enough to conceive Horus. Cunning, powerful, and politically central, she is the goddess who can outwit even other gods, and whose loyalty to her family reshapes the divine order.
source.weave: The Weave casts Isis as ruler of the Egyptian land of the dead who, to protect her own realm, quietly lets Heaven occupy allied cities and exploits a contract loophole to end Osiris — turning the myth's cunning, family-first sovereign into a study of how the powerful sell out the vulnerable to survive.
source.work: Plutarch, Isis and Osiris / Book of the Dead
source.excerpt_ref: the myth of Isis and Osiris

title: Osiris
teaser: A king of the dead undone by a clause his own wife found.
body: Co-ruler of the Duat alongside Isis, Osiris is ended through a loophole in Seraphaniel's contract that Isis exploits. His fall removes one of the last independent powers in the Egyptian underworld and tightens Heaven's grip there.

source.real: Osiris is the Egyptian god of the dead and resurrection — the once-living king murdered and dismembered by his brother Set, reassembled by Isis, and reborn as ruler and judge of the underworld. His death and return is Egypt's central myth of rebirth, the green-skinned lord before whom every soul is judged.
source.weave: The Weave makes Osiris co-ruler of the Duat who is ended through a contract loophole — a fall that removes one of the last independent powers in the Egyptian underworld. It inverts the myth's resurrection: the god famous for returning from death is, this time, permanently undone by paperwork.
source.work: Plutarch, Isis and Osiris / Book of the Dead
source.excerpt_ref: the death and resurrection of Osiris

title: Hel
teaser: The ruined queen of Helheim, jailer turned ally.
body: Ruler of the Norse land of the dead, Hel holds Emma prisoner in Helheim, once the jewel of the underworld and now its ruin. When Lucifer arrives he wins her to his side alongside the Verdant Queen of Awynn, and Helheim becomes the ground where Seraphaniel's masterstroke finally breaks Emma's bond and turns back Heaven's army.

source.real: Hel, Norse goddess of the dead, daughter of Loki, ruler of the cold realm of the same name where those who die of sickness and age reside.
source.weave: The Weave's Hel holds Emma in Helheim, 'once the jewel of the underworld and now its ruin' — keeping the goddess of the cold dead, her realm fallen, on the frozen side of the cross-pantheon underworld map.

title: Persephone
teaser: The queen of Hades' realm who helped the children in secret.
body: Co-ruler of the Greek underworld with Hades. Outwardly bound by the occupation, she quietly aids Emma's party during the Tartarus episode, including the blinding of the Oracle's basin. Her secret help is one of the first cracks in Heaven's hold over the lands of the dead.

source.real: Persephone, queen of the Greek underworld, the maiden taken below who becomes its sovereign, embodiment of the seasons' turning.
source.weave: In QG2 she is co-ruler of the Greek underworld who quietly aids the heroes against the occupation — the queen who was herself once a captive, now secretly siding with the captives, a fitting thread-face of the abducted-bride-turned-queen.

title: Hades
teaser: A lord of the dead given a merciful end on his own throne.
body: Ruler of the Greek underworld. During the siege of his realm he is mercy-killed by his own lieutenant Veilion, who then defects. His death marks the turning of the war back toward Hell and the collapse of Heaven's southern front.

source.real: Hades, Greek god and king of the underworld, stern lord of the dead who rarely leaves his realm.
source.weave: In the Quest Girls 2 war, Hades rules the Greek underworld and is mercy-killed by his own lieutenant Veilion — his fall turning the war. The unmovable lord of the dead, here made a casualty of a larger campaign: this thread's face of Hades.

title: Veilion
teaser: The lieutenant who killed his king to end his suffering, then changed sides.
body: A captain in Hades' realm who, during the siege, grants his lord a merciful death rather than let him be destroyed by Heaven, then defects to Lucifer's cause. His turn breaks the siege of Hades open and brings the war to its final phase.

title: The Verdant Queen (Awynn)
teaser: A realm-spirit and a queen, the same being under two names.
body: The ruler of the Celtic underworld, merged with the realm-spirit Awynn itself, so that the land and its queen are one. She is freed from captivity during Celeste's ride to Awynn and joins Lucifer's alliance, her power proving decisive at Helheim. In later dialogue she is called simply Awynn, which is intentional, not an error.

source.tradition: Celtic (Weave's own figure within a real tradition)
source.real: Celtic myth has many sovereignty-goddesses fused with the land itself (the land and its rightful ruler as one being is a genuine Celtic theme). 'Awynn' is not a standard named deity.
source.weave: The Verdant Queen, merged with the realm-spirit Awynn, rules the Weave's Celtic land of the dead — the authentic Celtic 'land-and-queen-are-one' motif, but the specific figure and name appear to be the Weave's own. Flagged for Russell to confirm.

title: Caedren
teaser: The mad herald of the Verdant Queen.
body: A deranged messenger tied to the court of Awynn, encountered during Celeste's mission into the Celtic underworld. Distinct from Caedmon, the Heaven envoy of the Duat thread, despite the similar name.

title: Caedmon
teaser: Heaven's envoy in the Egyptian thread.
body: A messenger of Heaven who appears in the Duat and Hades episodes. Distinct from Caedren, the Verdant Queen's herald in the Celtic thread; the two never share a scene.

title: Vash (in the parade)
teaser: Lacey's demoness ally, now in the marching party.
body: The demoness introduced in Book 1 rides with the parade party through the underworlds alongside Emma, Lucifer, Lacey, and the freed Oliver, while Margaret and Celeste hold Dis. She is a steady hand through the Forgotten Realms arc, often covering for the slips where allies who stayed behind in Dis are mistakenly written into parade scenes.

title: Tariq
teaser: An ally met along the war road.
body: A male figure encountered during the underworld campaign, part of the shifting cast of allies and envoys the party gathers on the way to and from the Forgotten Realms.

title: The Duat
teaser: The Egyptian land of the dead, first stop on the parade.
body: The Egyptian underworld ruled by Isis and Osiris, where the parade is welcomed with an oath ceremony before everything sours. It is here that Heaven's quiet occupation of allied cities is exposed, that Osiris falls to a contract loophole, and that the party splits, some staying while Emma and Lucifer flee toward the Forgotten Realms under cover of a staged sandstorm.

source.real: The Duat is the Egyptian underworld — the realm the sun-god Ra traverses each night and through which every soul must journey, facing trials and the Weighing of the Heart before Osiris. Ruled by Osiris with Isis, it is a place of judgment and transformation, not mere punishment: the crucible the dead pass through toward rebirth.
source.weave: The Weave seats the Duat among the contended lands of the dead, ruled by Isis and Osiris, where Heaven's quiet occupation is first exposed — placing the Egyptian afterlife on the cross-pantheon underworld map alongside the Greek, Norse, and Celtic realms.
source.work: The Egyptian Book of the Dead

title: Helheim
teaser: Once the jewel of the underworld, now the Forgotten Realms where Emma is caged.
body: Hel's Norse realm, fallen from glory into ruin and rebranded the Forgotten Realms. Emma is imprisoned here. It becomes the decisive battlefield: Lucifer wins Hel and the Verdant Queen to his side, and Seraphaniel's contract masterstroke breaks Emma's bond and turns Heaven's army back on this ground.

source.real: Helheim is the Norse realm of the dead ruled by the goddess Hel — the cold, dim abode of those who die outside battle, reached across the river Gjöll and guarded by the hound Garmr.
source.weave: The Weave's Helheim has 'fallen from glory into ruin and rebranded the Forgotten Realms,' a decisive battlefield — the Norse cold-realm as a contested, declined kingdom on the underworld map.

title: Awynn
teaser: The Celtic underworld, a realm that is also a queen.
body: The Celtic land of the dead, Celeste's destination, where the realm-spirit and the Verdant Queen are one and the same being. Celeste's ride here frees the Queen and brings the Celtic power into Lucifer's alliance. Distinct from Helheim, Hel's Norse realm, though the war links the two.

source.real: Annwn is the Welsh Otherworld and land of the dead, ruled by Arawn, described in the Mabinogi as a realm of plenty and enchantment.
source.weave: Awynn is the Weave's Celtic land of the dead — an original name grown from the real Welsh 'Arawn/Annwn,' where the realm-spirit and the Verdant Queen are one being.

title: Tartarus & the Greek Underworld
teaser: Hades' realm, where an oracle's basin gets quietly poisoned.
body: The Greek land of the dead, ruled by Hades and Persephone. Early in the parade Emma drugs the Oracle's scrying basin to blind it while Persephone secretly helps. Much later the realm is the site of the climactic siege where Veilion mercy-kills Hades and defects.

source.real: Tartarus, the deep abyss below Hades in Greek myth, the prison of the Titans — here also used (as the Greeks sometimes did) as a name for the realm of the dead ruled by Hades and Persephone.
source.weave: The Weave's 'Tartarus & the Greek Underworld' is the Greek land of the dead in the QG2 parade, ruled by Hades and Persephone — the Greek afterlife taking its place on the contended underworld map.

title: The Oracle's Basin
teaser: A scrying pool blinded with a drop of the right poison.
body: A divining basin in the Greek underworld that lets its keepers watch the realm. Emma drugs it to blind the Oracle during the Tartarus episode, with Persephone's quiet help, buying the party room to move unseen.

title: The Council's Geas
teaser: A binding that makes one body answer for another's wounds.
body: The contract-magic the Council of Hell uses to chain Emma to Lucifer. Whatever harm Lucifer takes is mirrored onto Emma, and healing meant for one flows to both, planted early and demonstrated when Margaret's healing reaches them both at once. The geas is the engine of the whole plot: every faction's scheme turns on who controls it, and Seraphaniel's masterstroke finally dissolves it.

source.real: A geas (pl. geasa) is an idiosyncratic magical taboo of Irish and Scottish tradition — a binding obligation or prohibition, like a vow or curse, that confers power while it is kept and brings doom when broken. Heroes like Cú Chulainn live and die by their geasa: the sacred rule one cannot violate without ruin.
source.weave: The Weave's Council's Geas is the contract-magic that chains Emma to Lucifer — whatever harm he takes is mirrored onto her — keeping the genuine geas (a binding magical obligation with dire consequences) as Hell's instrument of leverage. The Irish sacred-taboo as legal-magical shackle.
source.work: Irish myth (the geasa of Cú Chulainn)

title: Heaven's Occupation of the Underworld
teaser: The dead are under guard, and their rulers signed for it.
body: Behind the parade's pageantry, Heaven has been quietly occupying the allied cities of the dead, with several underworld rulers, Isis among them, signing away their independence to survive. The war of Book 2 is the campaign to break that occupation: rally Lucifer's old allies in the Forgotten Realms, win realm after realm, and overturn Heaven's legal claim through Seraphaniel's contract before retaking Hell itself.

title: The Siege of Hades
teaser: The siege that turned when a lieutenant turned.
body: The assault on the Greek underworld in the war's final phase. It breaks open when Veilion mercy-kills his lord Hades and defects, clearing the way for the alliance to march on Hell, burn the Bureaucracy, and free every bound soul.

source.real: Hades, Greek lord of the dead, rules the underworld from his throne. A siege of his realm is the Weave's own event, but it turns on the genuine Greek death-god.
source.weave: The Siege of Hades is the QG2 assault on the Greek underworld in which Hades is mercy-killed — the war reaching the throne of the genuine Greek lord of the dead. See Hades for the mythic root.

title: The Council of Hell (reformed)
teaser: From a star chamber of dukes to a thing that actually votes.
body: The geas that bound Emma was imposed by the old Council of Hell, a body of scheming nobles, among them Malthas, Saldur, Solenzara, Veilion, Azazel, Tiraxa, and Zir'kael. After the war retakes Hell and burns the Bureaucracy, the Council is remade as a vote-governed body, the bound souls are freed, and humans return to the Library. Lucifer's old order gives way to something closer to self-rule.

title: A Family Forged in Fire
teaser: The war ends not with a throne but with a proposal.
body: Book 2 closes in the rebuilt Library: Lacey proposes to Margaret and the two take Emma in as their own. After a book spent fighting over who owns whose soul, the ending answers it with a chosen family, the orphan finally claimed and the found-family made whole.

title: The Sovereign
teaser: The crowned absence that rules Heaven, and prunes the universe to keep it.
body: The Sovereign rules Heaven not from a throne but from a height so vast no one below guesses their strings are being pulled. They present as order incarnate: a faceless void wearing armor of polished night, crowned with serrated halos, each a devoured star. Their true hunger is not chaos or conquest but certainty, power no one can challenge or escape. They speak as pressure inside skull and rib rather than sound, and use the they/them they have always claimed. Resistance, to the Sovereign, is merely a way to test the strength of a perfectly built cage.

title: Valaliel
teaser: A name lost to time, and the only thing that can end the one who buried it.
body: Valaliel is the Sovereign's true, forgotten name, the child of Heaven they were before they rose, when Nox was still their teacher and friend. The name was buried so thoroughly that even the angels who serve forgot it. Spoken with intent and joined to shadow, it is the only thing that can unmake an angel or wound the Sovereign, because a being protected by forgetting who they are loses that protection the instant the world remembers. Bound into Obsidian, the name becomes a blade that knows one enemy. The Sovereign flinches whenever it is spoken, and insists, against all evidence, that 'Valaliel is dead.'

title: The Spire
teaser: A black needle in Heaven where the dark was kept, and a friend was forgotten.
body: The Spire is a towering spike of impossible blackness in Heaven, once a repository, then a prison, finally a tomb, bound by spells older than language. It held Nox, the imprisoned darkness-goddess, behind unbreakable glass for an age. After the Sovereign's fall, Emma and the survivors strip its wards rune by rune and free her; the Spire collapses into wildflowers and morning, its purpose ended with the regime that built it.

title: Nareth
teaser: A boy who carries a goddess of darkness, and the secret that could save everyone.
body: Nareth is the hidden son of Lucifer and Erishtane, a boy who carries the imprisoned darkness-goddess Nox inside him like a second heart, her presence a violet smear behind his eyes. New to the world and to people, he is a reluctant vessel pressed into deception: he stages Maison's interrogation, helps anchor the name-binding that forges the Valaliel dagger, and makes Nox's last shadow-stand against the Sovereign in the forge, surviving though battered.

title: Erishtane
teaser: A spear-bearing warrior who would damn the universe before losing her son again.
body: Erishtane is Nareth's mother and Lucifer's partner, a silver-haired warrior who carries a spear like a held storm. Fierce and grieving, she helps recruit gods, anchors the name-magic at the Hollow Forge, and survives the seventh extraction where the angel Israfel sacrifices himself, a loss she meets with only, 'I told him not to.'

title: Kalagos, Warden of Streams
teaser: The Warden of Streams, who came with the fury of the dispossessed.
body: Kalagos is a storm-god, Warden of Streams, whose sister Kanyris was murdered and drained by the Sovereign on the glassed world of Epsilon-9 using a crude spike of dark metal. He joins the rebels less from hope than from a death-wish for vengeance, and fights through to the final stand at the Hollow Mountain.

title: Kanyris
teaser: A sky-goddess killed to prove a point, and to harvest a god.
body: Kanyris was Kalagos's sister, a sky-goddess of Epsilon-9. The Sovereign's envoys lured her with a pact requiring a 'love-tithe,' then killed her with a spike of Obsidian and consumed her power until nothing remained but a husk, proof the Sovereign had learned to make more god-killing weapons. Her death is the warning that sets the rebels racing to forge their own blade first.

title: Israfel
teaser: An angel who chose the rebels, and bought their escape with his life.
body: Israfel is an angel allied to the rebellion, quiet and grim. On the seventh and last Obsidian extraction he holds off the Sovereign's scouts so the team can escape with the final shards, his hand vanishing into light as the tether closes. He is not to be confused with Irael, the captured angel who hunts Fairy, nor Lirael, the repentant loyalist who speaks at the reconciliation council.

source.real: Israfil (Israfel) is the archangel of Islamic tradition who will sound the trumpet to announce the Day of Resurrection — the angel of the last trump, holder of the breath that ends and renews the world. Often counted among the great archangels alongside Jibril and Mika'il.
source.weave: The Weave's Israfel is 'an angel allied to the rebellion, quiet and grim,' who holds off the Sovereign's scouts on the last Obsidian extraction — borrowing the trumpet-angel of the end-times as a grave, end-game ally.

title: Irael
teaser: The captured angel who escaped, and learned how angels truly die.
body: Irael is a Sovereign angel captured and bound in the Library, who escapes when the mole cuts his glyph, then leads the angelic assault on Fairy with seven-layered, gold-barbed wings. He is the first angel unmade by the combined truth of name and shadow, when Lyassa screams his name and a troll's borrowed darkness strikes as one. Distinct from the ally Israfel and the repentant Lirael.

title: Lirael
teaser: A bound angel who, freed, asked only to be heard.
body: Lirael is a former Sovereign angel, gold-haired and scarred, who speaks for the surviving loyalists at the reconciliation council after the Sovereign falls. He does not beg pardon, only to be heard, admitting the angels served because they were bound, and offering to help find the others still hiding. Distinct from the antagonist Irael and the fallen ally Israfel.

title: Tesh
teaser: A quiet archivist at the forge, and a signal sent into the dark.
body: Tesh is a survivor who clings to a ledger and lingers at the edges. At the lighting of the Hollow Forge he secretly slips a small glowing token from a pocket and whispers into the ether: 'It's begun. They're here. Forge is lit. Come now.' His betrayal is never confronted on-page; he still appears among the survivors after the victory, a thread left dangling.

title: The Hollow Forge
teaser: An undying dwarven forge, dark for generations, lit one last time.
body: The Hollow Forge lies deep beneath the Hollow Mountain, the greatest of the dwarven forges, built when the gods were young and abandoned after the last great age. Lyassa secures it for the one task that matters: forging the Valaliel dagger. Its ancient fires are reignited for the final stand, where dwarves shape the named blade as the Sovereign's host besieges the mountain above.

title: Name and Shadow
teaser: Not black metal. Not a curse. The truth that unmakes an angel.
body: The rebels discover in Fairy that angels are not killed by Obsidian itself, the black metal was only ever the artifact, the proof. What truly unmakes an angel is cooperation: a true name spoken with intent (Sovereign, then the deeper Valaliel) joined to a troll's willingly-bled shadow magic, striking as one. Not command, not force, but the asking and the naming together, a truth reached deeper than Heaven's order. It is the principle the Valaliel dagger weaponizes.

title: The Assembly of Heaven
teaser: No crown. No Sovereign. A government that belongs to everyone, or no one at all.
body: Born at the end of Cosmic Bastards after elections, appointments, rotation, and pure chance all failed, the Assembly is Heaven's dual-chamber charter government: an Upper House of Lords (one seat per pantheon, recognized community, the Forsaken, and the Tricksters) and a Lower House of Commons (one seat per billion living mortals, fae, and supernatural beings, by open election). The Chair rotates by random draw; major changes need a two-thirds supermajority plus a citywide referendum; the Trickster seat can call a Red Flag emergency; the Forsaken hold a veto on any law harming the outcast; and if anyone seizes sole power, the Assembly dissolves itself. The answer to the impossible crown: let no one wear it.

title: The Forsaken Dead
teaser: The gods Heaven tried to forget, come at last to be seen.
body: A pantheon-house of erased and abandoned underworld gods, exiles, and forgotten dead, led by a veiled, genderless figure once called the Warden, the Keeper, the Last Witness, whose own name was lost and found a hundred times. They arrive at Heaven's gates demanding recognition rather than war, and after Hel's confession and the Weeping Gates ritual they are seated as a sovereign house of the new order, with a river-and-stars sigil and a standing veto protecting the outcast. Their cause: 'We were here. We mattered.'

title: The Wild God
teaser: Not male nor female, young nor old. It is now: pure, merciless, electric.
body: A primal forest-deity beyond any pantheon, dwelling in a grove on no map, who tests Margaret and Lacey with three trials, not of strength but of surrender: facing their own fears, their loyalty to each other, and the hardest truth of all, that the work is never finished and no one can carry it forever. The Wild God does not bind and cannot be tamed; it grants the right to leave and the right to return. Reached through the Horned Road via Cernunnos.

title: The Reckoning
teaser: For every silence, a voice. For every exile, a welcome.
body: After the Lost Law (the Sovereign's buried decree of silence and erasure) is discovered and burned, the council holds the first Reckoning: every leader confesses their complicity in the Sovereign's reign, the names of the cast-out and those who cast them are spoken aloud, and an annual remembrance is carved into the council square. Not absolution, but the founding promise of 'the city of no more forgetting.'

title: Xuanzong (the former Jade Emperor)
teaser: He gave up the throne and asked only to be called elder brother.
body: The Jade Emperor who reigned over the Celestial bureaucracy until the Lotus Rebellion. Rather than cling to power, he voluntarily relinquished the imperial title, asked to be called simply Xuanzong, and took a place at the new council as counsel rather than ruler. Princess San's brother; humbled but at peace. The title he set down passed to a successor.

title: The Jade Emperor
teaser: The throne outlasts the one who sits it.
body: The reigning Jade Emperor of the council era, the successor who took the Celestial throne after Xuanzong relinquished it. Dignified and order-minded, he leads the Chinese delegation in the water-rights negotiation against the Yoruba, holding that the waterways must flow by law, not whim. That the title could pass at all quietly echoes the book's central truth: no crown is permanent.

source.real: The Jade Emperor (Yu Huang) is the supreme ruler of Heaven in Chinese folk religion and Daoism — the celestial sovereign who presides over the vast bureaucracy of gods, grants and revokes divine offices, and maintains cosmic order through law and hierarchy. He is Heaven as government: order, propriety, and the rule of celestial law above all.
source.weave: The Weave's Jade Emperor is the order-minded sovereign who leads the Chinese delegation in cross-pantheon negotiation, holding that 'the waterways must flow by law, not whim' — the myth's celestial administrator carried into the Weave's divine diplomacy among many pantheons.
source.work: Journey to the West / Chinese folk tradition
source.excerpt_ref: the court of the Jade Emperor

title: Princess San (the Lotus Goddess)
teaser: Imprisoned under Lotus Peak for loving a mortal; freed to remake Heaven.
body: The third princess of the Celestial court, sealed beneath Lotus Peak by her own brother Erlang Shen for loving a mortal man. Freed during the Lotus Rebellion by her son Chen Xiang and the heroes, she wields the divine light of the Lotus Lantern and becomes a beloved figure of the new order, the most-wronged endorsing the reform.

source.real: In the Tang-dynasty folktale The Magic Lotus Lantern, the goddess Sanshengmu (the Holy Mother of Mount Hua) falls in love with a mortal scholar and bears a son, Chenxiang. For breaking Heaven's law against divine-mortal union, she is imprisoned beneath Mount Hua by her brother Erlang Shen — until Chenxiang, grown and armed with a magic axe and the lotus lantern, splits the mountain and frees her. It is one of China's most beloved tales of filial love defying rigid law.
source.weave: The Weave's Princess San IS Sanshengmu — the third princess sealed beneath Lotus Peak by her brother Erlang Shen for loving a mortal, freed by her son Chen Xiang. It keeps the lotus lantern as her divine light and turns the folktale's private rescue into a public 'Lotus Rebellion,' the myth scaled up to revolution.

title: Chen Xiang
teaser: A son who split a mountain to free his mother.
body: Prince of the Celestial court whose quest to free his imprisoned mother, Princess San, sparked the Lotus Rebellion when it joined with the heroes' mission. Carries the reclaimed Lotus Lantern.

title: Erlang Shen
teaser: The three-eyed enforcer who learned to serve a council instead of a crown.
body: The Jade Emperor's nephew and enforcer, a towering three-eyed general who first stood against the Lotus Rebellion, then came into the new order. Represents the Chinese pantheon at the council and stands with the reigning Jade Emperor in the water-rights talks.

source.tradition: Chinese (Journey to the West / Lotus Lantern)
source.real: Erlang Shen is a Chinese warrior god with a third, truth-seeing eye in his forehead and a three-pointed double-edged spear, nephew of the Jade Emperor and the one god who can fight Sun Wukong to a standstill. In the Lotus Lantern tale he imprisons his own sister beneath Mount Hua for marrying a mortal — bound by Heaven's law against his own family — until her son Chenxiang grows up and splits the mountain to free her.
source.weave: The Weave keeps every real detail — the three-eyed general, the Jade Emperor's nephew — and builds its Lotus Rebellion directly on the genuine myth: he seals his sister (Princess San) beneath Lotus Peak for loving a mortal, and her son Chen Xiang frees her. The faithful Mount Hua story, reweaved as a rebellion.
source.work: Journey to the West / The Magic Lotus Lantern
source.excerpt_ref: Erlang vs. the Monkey King; the Lotus Lantern

title: Eluned
teaser: A mortal druidess of the old ways; guide to the Horned Road.
body: A druidess of the old Celtic ways with a Welsh lilt, the crew's trusted guide after their alliance with the Dagda and the Tuatha De Danann. She leads Margaret and Lacey to the threshold of the Wild God's realm and calls the parley with Cernunnos on the liminal night, then remains in her grove, a keeper of the old ways. (Not to be confused with Awynn the Verdant Queen, the fae realm-queen of the council.)

source.real: Eluned (Luned/Lunete) is a figure of Welsh and Arthurian romance — the clever handmaiden of the Lady of the Fountain who aids the knight Owain with a ring of invisibility. A name rooted in genuine Welsh tradition (and the saint Eluned/Eiluned).
source.weave: The Weave's Eluned is 'a druidess of the old Celtic ways with a Welsh lilt,' the crew's guide after their alliance with the Dagda and the Tuatha Dé Danann — keeping the authentic Welsh name and the helpful-guide role from the romance tradition.
source.work: The Mabinogion (Owain, or the Lady of the Fountain)

title: Cernunnos (the Horned God)
teaser: The Wild Hunt rides at his call; the wild folk take a seat in Heaven.
body: The horned god of the Celtic wild and master of the Wild Hunt, met on the Horned Road during a liminal night. Persuaded by the heroes (and the Dagda's endorsement) to bring the untamed folk into the new council. Distinct from Cerunnos, the fae chamberlain of the Amethyst Court.

source.real: Cernunnos is the horned god of Celtic religion — antlered lord of wild things, beasts, forests, and the untamed, depicted seated cross-legged among animals on the Gundestrup Cauldron. God of the liminal and the wild, he is associated with the Wild Hunt and the threshold between the cultivated world and the wilderness beyond it.
source.weave: The Weave's Cernunnos is 'the horned god of the Celtic wild and master of the Wild Hunt,' met on the Horned Road during a liminal night and persuaded to bring the untamed folk into the new order — keeping his domain (the wild, the Hunt, the threshold) intact.

title: The Dagda
teaser: The good god of the Tuatha De Danann, host of an endless feast.
body: Father-figure of the Celtic pantheon whose alliance and famous feast bring the Tuatha De Danann into the new Heaven; his endorsement smooths the way with Cernunnos and the wild folk.

source.real: The Dagda is a chief god of the Irish Tuatha Dé Danann — 'the Good God,' a father-figure of immense appetite and power. He wields a club that kills with one end and revives with the other, owns a cauldron that never empties, and plays a harp that orders the seasons. He is abundance, wisdom, and earthy power combined: the great patriarch of the Irish gods.
source.weave: The Weave's Dagda endorses bringing the wild folk and the Tuatha Dé Danann into the new council — keeping his role as the elder authority of the Irish gods whose word carries weight among them.

title: Quetzalcoatl
teaser: The feathered serpent returns, not as conqueror nor pawn.
body: The plumed-serpent god of the Mesoamerican pantheon, recruited to the new Heaven and a sharp, riddling presence at its council and feasts.

source.real: Quetzalcoatl, the 'Feathered Serpent,' is a major Mesoamerican deity — god of wind, learning, the priesthood, and the morning star, creator-figure and bringer of knowledge and maize to humanity. Wise and civilizing, he is contrasted with the darker Tezcatlipoca; in legend he departs over the sea with a promise to return.
source.weave: The Weave's Quetzalcoatl is 'the plumed-serpent god of the Mesoamerican pantheon... a sharp, riddling presence' at Heaven's council — keeping his nature as the wise, civilizing serpent-god, here a clever voice among the assembled pantheons.

title: Bastet
teaser: The queen of cats rules her own small kingdom, exactly as she wants it.
body: The Egyptian cat-goddess, encountered keeping her own quiet domain; one of the many gods the heroes draw toward the new order.

title: Yemaya
teaser: The sea claims no master, but all who drown become her children.
body: Great Orisha of the sea, who meets the Chinese delegation in the water-rights dispute and, at the Drowned City, shares the souls of the drowned with Osiris in a brokered peace. Vast, deep, and maternal as the ocean.

title: Shango
teaser: Thunder and fire; the storm that brings change.
body: Orisha of thunder and fire, fierce and proud, who arrives with the Yoruba pantheon and stands in the council and the water-rights negotiation. The storm that asks whether any law can silence change.

source.real: Shango ( Ṣàngó) is the Yoruba orisha of thunder, lightning, fire, and justice — a former king of Oyo deified after death, fierce and proud, who hurls thunderstones from the sky. Associated with the double-headed axe and the color red, he is divine kingship and storm-power: the orisha who answers injustice with lightning.
source.weave: The Weave's Shango is 'orisha of thunder and fire, fierce and proud,' arriving with the Yoruba pantheon to stand in the council and the water-rights negotiation — 'the storm that asks whether any law can silence change.' His thunder-justice becomes a political force at the divine table.

title: Sun Wukong (the Monkey King)
teaser: Impersonate, imitate, exaggerate. The seat of power is just a stage.
body: The Monkey King, a trickster who needs no permission, swinging through the council impersonating gods and turning every solemn rule upside down. One of the tricksters who conspire to keep Heaven from crowning anyone.

source.real: Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, is the irrepressible trickster-hero of Wu Cheng'en's 16th-century novel Journey to the West — born from a stone egg, master of 72 transformations and the cloud-somersault, wielder of a shape-shifting iron staff. He storms Heaven, erases his name from the registers of death, declares himself 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven,' and is subdued only when the Buddha traps him under a mountain. He is rebellion against cosmic bureaucracy made flesh.
source.weave: The Weave's Monkey King is exactly that figure — a trickster who needs no permission, swinging through Heaven's council impersonating gods and turning every solemn rule upside down, conspiring to keep Heaven from crowning anyone. It keeps his defining trait: the anarchic force that no celestial bureaucracy can contain.
source.work: Wu Cheng'en, Journey to the West
source.excerpt_ref: Havoc in Heaven; the Great Sage

title: The Tricksters
teaser: They love the game, not the outcome. The crown is cursed; anyone who wants it shouldn't have it.
body: A loose conclave, Loki, Coyote, Anansi, Hermes, Eris, Kitsune, Raven, and Sun Wukong, who meet when Heaven's order is weakest and conspire to disrupt every attempt at a throne. Their method is chaos with a purpose: make the gods sweat, laugh, and remember what it is to be free, so no new Sovereign can rise. In the Assembly they win a permanent seat with the power to call a Red Flag emergency.

source.real: Nearly every mythology has a trickster — Norse Loki, Native American Coyote and Raven, West African/Caribbean Anansi, Greek Hermes and Eris, Japanese Kitsune (fox-spirit), Chinese Sun Wukong. Cunning rule-breakers who upend order, often bringing change or necessities by mischief.
source.weave: The Weave's Tricksters are a literal cross-cultural conclave — Loki, Coyote, Anansi, Hermes, Eris, Kitsune, Raven, and Sun Wukong — conspiring to keep Heaven from crowning anyone. It gathers the world's trickster figures into one faction, the series thesis applied to mischief itself.

crosslinks.summary: Every tradition has a trickster; the Weave gathers them into one conclave. Each member is a real-world trickster figure.

interactions.note: Loki — Norse trickster.
Coyote — Native American trickster.
Anansi — West African/Akan spider-trickster.
Sun Wukong — the Chinese Monkey King.

title: Coyote
teaser: We can't let them fall back into crowns and thrones.
body: A trickster of the desert pantheons; with Loki he takes the public lead in the tricksters' campaign of creative disorder, but of them all he most fears the council coming close to real freedom.

source.real: Coyote is the trickster figure across many Native American traditions — creator and fool, culture-hero and troublemaker, who shapes the world as often by accident as by design. Clever, greedy, lustful, and irrepressible, he breaks rules and suffers for it, yet his blunders frequently bring fire, death, or other necessities into the world.
source.weave: The Weave's Coyote is one of 'the tricksters who conspire to keep Heaven from crowning anyone' — keeping the trickster's core function: the rule-breaker who upends order, here joining a cross-cultural league of tricksters against any single throne.

title: Hermes
teaser: Everyone gambles when they're desperate.
body: The Greek messenger-trickster, who runs the odds and the side-bets through the council's chaos. One of the tricksters of the Assembly.

source.real: Hermes is the Greek messenger god — swift, cunning, patron of travelers, thieves, merchants, and heralds, who guides souls to the underworld as psychopomp. Wing-footed and quick-tongued, he crosses every boundary: between gods and mortals, between the living world and the dead.
source.weave: The Weave uses Hermes in his classic role as the crosser of boundaries and bearer of messages between divine courts — the go-between in a cosmos of many contending pantheons.

title: Pele
teaser: To beginnings, and to endings that make way for something fiercer.
body: The Polynesian goddess of fire and volcanoes, radiating heat and promise at Heaven's councils and feasts; flowers bloom and blacken at her place.

source.real: Pele is the Hawaiian goddess of fire, lightning, wind, and volcanoes — creator and destroyer of land, who dwells in the Kīlauea caldera and whose passions shape the islands themselves. Fierce, jealous, and generative, she is the living volcano: the force that both destroys and makes new ground.
source.weave: The Weave's Pele is 'the Polynesian goddess of fire and volcanoes, radiating heat and promise... flowers bloom and blacken at her place' — capturing her dual creative-destructive nature, the goddess in whose presence things both flourish and burn.

title: The Bridge of Storms
teaser: A span built by enemies, where peace is renewed each spring.
body: A bridge raised by council decree between the feuding Norse and Sumerian camps. Built and sabotaged and built again, it becomes the site of Eydis and Namtar's forbidden union and, after, an annual rite where gods and mortals renew oaths and bind themselves across old enmities. A cairn-shrine of tokens grows at its heart.

title: Eydis
teaser: A thunder god's daughter who chose a son of the underworld.
body: Daughter of Thor, a Norse negotiator who oversees her people's work on the Bridge of Storms and falls for the Sumerian Namtar, defying both camps to bind herself to him and keep the bridge standing.

source.real: In Norse myth, Thor is the hammer-wielding god of thunder, son of Odin and the most beloved defender of gods and humans against the giants. 'Eydis' is a genuine Old Norse woman's name (meaning roughly 'lucky goddess'), but is not herself a known deity.
source.weave: Eydis is the Weave's ORIGINAL character given real Norse lineage — a daughter of Thor who negotiates her people's work on the Bridge of Storms and binds herself to the Sumerian Namtar, defying both camps. The cross-pantheon romance (Norse + Sumerian) is the Weave's invention atop authentic Norse ancestry.

title: Namtar
teaser: A son of the underworld who would rather build than divide.
body: Son of the Sumerian queen Ereshkigal, quiet and patient, who works the Bridge of Storms beside the Norse Eydis and chooses union over loyalty to old feuds.

source.real: Namtar (whose name means 'fate' or 'doom') is the Sumerian god of death and disease — the sukkal (vizier and herald) of Ereshkigal, queen of the underworld Kur. In one tradition he is her son by Enlil. He carries her decrees, attends the gods' banquets in her place, and personifies inescapable fate; it is his slighting at a divine feast that sets in motion the myth of Nergal and Ereshkigal's union.
source.weave: The Weave keeps the lineage exactly — 'son of the Sumerian queen Ereshkigal' — and gives the fate-god a tender turn: quiet and patient, he works the Bridge of Storms beside the Norse Eydis and chooses union over the old feuds, a cross-pantheon romance built atop a faithfully-rendered Sumerian root.
source.work: Nergal and Ereshkigal (Akkadian myth) / Inanna's Descent

title: Karl
teaser: The scribe who recorded not just victories but doubts.
body: A young mortal scribe of the new Heaven who becomes its chronicler and, increasingly, its conscience, demanding the mortals and minor gods get a true voice and recording the names of the lost so they cannot be forgotten again.

title: Shael
teaser: A name on a banner: Shael remembers the forgotten.
body: A minor figure of the forgotten-gods cause, named only in passing on a campaign slogan during the council's chaotic elections ('Shael Remembers the Forgotten'). Single appearance.

title: Marat
teaser: A voice at the Reckoning.
body: A minor deity who speaks briefly at the Reckoning, confessing to having kept order by never truly breaking it. Single appearance.

title: Oscar
teaser: Jo's dying son — the incurable case the whole tower runs on.
body: Jo and Aesop's young son, sick with something the most advanced facility on Earth cannot cure. Aesop keeps the frozen Paradise survivors — and Jo — because their stable regeneration is the only thing slowing Oscar's decline. The boy is never healed, only held; the harvest keeps him alive by degrees. He is the knot that ties every choice together: the reason a man who insists he is not evil cages his own kin, and the human cost under the whole machine.

title: Sidney
teaser: Angel Foundation deep-cover scientist — the one who finds the machines in the blood.
body: An ex-Hort-I-Vex scientist working deep cover for the Angel Foundation, studying survivor blood and quietly smuggling the real cure. Because she does the actual science, she is the one who — looking closely enough at the tissue — finds the nanites that shouldn't be there: not a spy stealing a schematic, but a researcher seeing the truth in the DNA. Her past inside the tower (the history, the tattoo) makes her distrusted as a possible plant at the exact moment she becomes the only person who can prove what the serum really is. The distrust and the usefulness arrive together.

title: The Serum
teaser: Sold as a cure. It is a leash.
body: The 'serum' is not what keeps survivors alive — it is a control system. Nanites injected into people rewrite and tag their DNA, run experiments, and manufacture dependence: 'you need another dose or you die' is a lie. The stable regenerators heal cleanly and for free; the machines ride that healing, tearing a body down and reassembling it to run tests and calling the wreck a 'dose.' Regeneration never hurts anyone — the nanites do. Aesop's tragic-accident origin story for the serum is cover. Sidney finds the truth of it in the blood.

title: The Angel Foundation
teaser: A resistance inside the tower, smuggling the real cure.
body: An underground network working against Hort-I-Vex from the inside, moving the genuine cure to the people the tower feeds on and placing deep-cover people like Sidney where the real science happens. Where the rich have chased immortality for roughly a thousand years and never cracked it, the Foundation's aim is smaller and harder: get the cure out, and get people free of the leash.

title: The Water Order
teaser: A Dregs faction that runs on belief, not force.
body: One of the powers in the Dregs beneath Hort-I-Vex — a control order whose hold over the desperate is built on faith and ritual rather than open violence. It collects tribute and loyalty from survivors with nowhere else to go; its grip works only because the people at the bottom believe it must. It is one mode of control among several down there, alongside Edwin's underworld network and the Collectors and Scavengers who catch and pick over the newly thawed.
